- **It closes** when the caret leaves the name (before the `/`, past what was typed, or a
  selection), the `/` is deleted, what's typed holds what a name can't (whitespace, which ends the
  name, a line break, a pill, punctuation: a name is ASCII letters, digits and hyphens, matched
  folded) or is past 40 characters (`SlashCommandPicker.Closing`, what `read` says); and on Escape
  or ⌘., or when the keyboard or the window goes, as every caret list does. The `/` stays as typed,
  and nothing opens again until another is typed. While it's open the text's spelling correction,
  text replacement, smart quotes and smart dashes are off, and put back as they were when it
  closes (TextEditing's `CaretListSubstitutions`, which Mentions' picker uses too).
- **Keys** are every caret list's: ↑ ↓ ⌃P ⌃N and Page Up and Down move (one at a time they wrap,
  a page stops at the ends), Tab picks, Escape and ⌘. close. Return is this list's own, below.
- **A pick completes, and runs nothing.** Tab, or a click on a row, replaces the `/` and the
  name token it is in (the caret may be in the middle of one: `/gr|ow`) with `/` and the command's
  name, and a space if it takes an argument and no whitespace follows on its line (a line break
  doesn't count: the argument is typed on the line, not run into the one below), the caret after,
  as one step of the text's undo. Typing the argument is then the person's.

### Return, and what runs

The line is evaluated when Return is pressed, not as it's typed: a plain Return, with no ⌘, ⇧, ⌥
or ⌃ (⇧↩ is a new line, as it always was), and no text being composed. The slash list's Return and
a command line's are the same key, and one object decides which it is, before the view's own turn:

| Return | Does |
|---|---|
| With the list open, on a highlighted command that takes nothing, with only whitespace after its name on the line | Runs it at once: the line goes, the command runs. |
| With the list open, on any other highlighted command | Completes it, as Tab does, so its argument can be typed. |
| With the list open, with nothing highlighted ("No matches") | A new line, which closes the list. |
| With the list closed, no selection and the caret after the `/`, on a line that is `/name` and what follows, where the shape offers a command of that name now and it accepts what follows | Takes the line out of the text and runs the command. |
| Anything else: not a command, one the shape doesn't offer, arguments it doesn't accept, a selection, the caret before the `/` | Return as ever: a new line, or what the host does with it (a box's commit). |

A command line is its text from the `/` to the line's end, not its line break: `/name`, whitespace,
and what the command takes, trimmed at both ends. The caret may be anywhere after the `/`. The name
is matched folded, so `/LOCK` runs `lock`. In a box that commits on Return (`commitsOnReturn`, the
panel's), a command line runs and doesn't commit, and Return anywhere else commits as it does.

- **The line goes first.** The command runs after its line is taken out, never before: a command
  that makes the shape read-only (`/lock`) would refuse the text's write after it. The text is
  written through the view as an edit of the person's: undoable, heard by the host
  (`shouldChangeText`, `didChangeText`, so the host commits the shorter text as it commits typing),
  its own steps of the text's undo, the view's typing attributes, the caret left at the line's
  start on the now empty line, its list closed before and its own callbacks ignored meanwhile. The
  line break stays: a command takes a line's text and leaves the lines around it.
- **The command is the shape's as it is when Return is pressed.** It's asked of the shape then: a
  command not offered by now, or not accepting what was typed, takes nothing out, and Return is a
  Return that isn't a command's. A command that reads the text (offered only while it isn't
  blank, say) is still run once the line is gone: it's run as it was found, not asked again.

### Marking the command

A command is marked as it's typed, as a mention's pill is marked, so a line that Return would run
looks unlike one that is only text. `SlashCommandTyping` sets the view's `highlights`
([TextEditing](#the-text-view)) after every change of the text or the caret, in the text's own color
(its typing attributes') at a strength of it, so the marks follow whatever surface the text is on:

- **The `/name`**, at `SlashCommandStyle.commandFill` (18%; a pill's is 10%). With the list open it's
  the `/` and the name there (past the caret too, if it's in the middle of one), so long as the list
  lists a command for it: "No matches" marks nothing. With the list closed it's the name of the
  line the caret is on (`SlashCommandLine.nameRange`), if the shape offers a command of that name
  now, and the caret is after the `/`: the same line Return would run, whether or not its arguments
  suit the command.
- **What it's given**, at `argumentsFill` (8%), a lighter shade of the same: the line's arguments,
  only when the command accepts them. `/lock now`, which stays text, marks `/lock` alone; `/title
  Groceries` marks both; a pill in the arguments is inside the mark.
- **Nothing else.** Other lines, a line whose name the shape doesn't offer (`/wide` while the card
  isn't wide), a selection, the caret before the `/`, and a view that can't be written (which lets go
  of its highlights as it's made read-only) have no marks. Running the command takes the line out of
  the text, and its marks with it.

### Undoing a command

Two undo managers, as with every text: the board's steps and the text's own ([Undo](#undo)).

- **The board.** While the shape is edited, the editing session is one step, "Typing" (or the
  action that began it), and the line's removal is in it. The command is any other commit while a
  shape is being edited, which closes the editing step first ([Undo](#undo)), so it's a step
  between the typing before it and the typing after: the board's Undo takes back "Undo Lock"
  first, then "Undo Typing", which leaves the text without the line, and typing after the command
  is a step of its own. A command that commits nothing makes no step.
- **The text.** ⌘Z while the text is edited is the text's own, and brings the line's text back
  (the person's last edit was taking it out) and leaves the command done: text undo is the text's,
  and the command is the board's.
- **Editing ends where the core ends it.** A command that makes the shape read-only (`/lock`),
  deletes it or shows another board ends editing as any such change does, and the line's removal,
  written first, is already in the step.

### Hosting in a text view: `SlashCommandTyping`

A text view takes part by making a `SlashCommandTyping(over:owner:commands:arguments:)`: for one
shape's text (`owner`, whose commands it asks), over an `EditingTextView`, with `commands`, the
service. It holds the view and the service weakly. `arguments` reads a range of the text as runs
(the default reads it as plain text). Mentions' `MentionTextView<Scope>` makes one in `init` when it
has an owner and its editor has the service (`slashCommands`; else nil, and a slash is a slash),
and calls it where a text view's events are ([Editing: `MentionTextView`](#editing-mentiontextview)):

```swift
slashCommands = SlashCommandTyping(over: self, owner: owner, commands: commands) { [weak self] in self?.arguments(in: $0) ?? SlashArguments([]) }

override var caretListWindow: CaretListWindow? { pickerWindow ?? slashCommands?.window }   // its list is the view's own
override func insertText(_ string: Any, replacementRange: NSRange) {                      // what a person typed, not composed
    ...
    if !wasComposing, !hasMarkedText() { slashCommands?.didType(typed) }
}
override func keyDown(with event: NSEvent) {                                              // a plain Return, first
    if picker == nil, slashCommands?.takesKey(event) == true { return }
    super.keyDown(with: event)
}
// slashCommands?.didChange(isEdit: true) after the text changes, (isEdit: false) after the caret moves
// alone (not while the view is changing text) and after the view's own undo; slashCommands?.close()
// when text is shown from outside, and before the @ picker opens;
// slashCommands?.admittedShapes(at: location) for the @ just typed, as the picker opens: its rule.
```

- **What the host tells it**: `didType(_:)` after the view inserts what a person typed (a `/`
  opens the list), `didChange(isEdit:)` after the text changed or the caret moved alone (the list
  reads the query again, and closes if that's what it says), `takesKey(_:)` before the view's own
  keys (a plain Return or Enter: `takesReturn()` is the same, without the event), and `close()`.
  It opens a list only while the view is editable, has no marked text and shows no other caret
  list.
- **Its list is the view's own**: the host returns its `window` from `caretListWindow`, so the view
  `holdsKeys` while it's open and every key and close is `EditingTextView`'s ([A list at the
  caret](#a-list-at-the-caret)); a pick and a close go through the window's closures, which run
  the object's.
- **It marks the command through the view too**: `view.highlights` is the whole of it, so a host
  forwards nothing to draw ([Marking the command](#marking-the-command)).
- **It writes the text only through the view**, as an edit of the person's (`write`: break undo
  coalescing, `shouldChangeText`, replace, the caret, `didChangeText`, break again), so the host
  hears what it hears for typing and nothing else is special.
- **Which shapes an `@` may pick**: `admittedShapes(at:)`, given the index of an `@` just typed, is
  a `SlashShapeRule` when the line is a command line (`SlashCommandLine`, read with the caret at the
  `@`) whose command the shape offers now and which takes a shape, else nil: a plain line, a command
  that takes none, one the shape doesn't offer. It has the command's `kinds` (nil: any), its `rule`
  alone, for a shape already known to be of those kinds (what a list that ranks only them asks of
  each), and `admits(_:)`, the kind and then the rule. The host hands the kinds and the rule to the
  `@` picker, so `/stack @` lists only discs and any other line lists as ever.
- **Mentions** passes `arguments` that reads the attributed text: each pill's character a
  `.shape(pill.target, label: pill.shownLabel)`, the rest text. So a pill in a command line is a
  shape the command is given (`/near @Groceries` gives `arguments.shapes == [groceries]`). It asks
  `admittedShapes(at:)` as it opens the picker and passes the kinds and the rule on ([Editing:
  `MentionTextView`](#editing-mentiontextview)). The `@` picker's keys come first while it's open
  (Return picks the shape, and a second Return runs the line), opening the picker closes the slash
  list, and `show(_:)` closes both.

### Testing slash commands

- **SlashCommandsTests** hold the plugin over fixtures only: CanvasTesting's boxes, discs and cards,
  chores' added `Flagged`, `Lamp`, a kind of the target's own that offers commands in every way a
  kind can (`LampsPlugin`: its own, and over the flag it holds), and `CardCommandsPlugin(log:)`,
  whose cards have commands to type (`grow` and `width` edit, `log` and `ping` perform, `stack`
  takes one shape, a disc and no other, and the log keeps what it ran with and what its rule was
  asked, `wide` is offered only while the card is wide, `any` accepts even nothing);
  `ParkCommandPlugin(log:)` gives them `park`, which takes one shape of the kinds that hold shapes
  or own boards (with `CorralsPlugin()` and `PocketsPlugin()`) and whose rule admits all but the
  card, so it's the kinds that refuse a box; `slashHarness` is an `EditorHarness` over them and
  `SlashCommandsPlugin()`, and `PickedShapes` stands for a mention text view's reader, giving the
  line's pills once something is typed after a name. They hold registration (every form of the sugar and the report's line for each, `where` with `holds`, a kind's own command over an
  every-shape one, conflicts, names refused, `ownerNotInstalled`, `unknownKind`), resolution
  (`commands(for:)`'s order, `when`, a shape that's gone, off the board shown, kept aside or
  read-only offering none, `step:` naming the step, `accepts` by default and given, an edit command in one transaction and one step
  named for it, a command's title in title case (`move-to-back` is "Move to Back"), a `perform` command, `run`'s false,
  and a command that takes one shape: accepted with one shape it admits and run with it, not with nothing,
  text, text and a shape, a shape and text, two shapes, one shape twice, a shape the rule refuses or one

  `OfferedSlashCommand` kept after its editor is gone admitting nothing and keeping nothing alive; `when`

  a box, a disc and another card refused though the rule would take them and the rule asked of

  `SlashCommandPicker` headlessly (every kind of line break, the rows and their ranking, each way it
  closes). The typing object is held in an unshown window over a card being edited: `SlashTextView`
  is an `EditingTextView` of the target's own that forwards to `SlashCommandTyping` as
  `MentionTextView` does, `SlashHost` is the card's editor (it writes the text to the board and
  counts `commits`), and `SlashSession` drives them (`type`, `down`, `tab`, `returnKey(_:)`,
  `set(_:caret:)`, `list`, `rows`). They hold where the list opens and where a slash is a slash
  (mid-line, before text, nothing offered, read-only, pasted, undone, composed), narrowing and each
  way it closes, the substitutions off while it's open and back after, completing (with and without
  the space, in the middle of a name, a click on a row, and the list's Return on a command that takes
  a shape), Return from the list and on a whole line,
  what isn't a command being Return as ever (⇧↩, a selection, the caret before the slash, text
  being composed), the text's own undo bringing the line back while the board's undo undoes the
  command by its name with the typing next, the command's step closing the editing session's, a
  box that commits on Return not committing a command line, a command no longer offered when
  its line is entered left as text, and for a command that takes one shape: Return running it with
  one shape it admits, read from the line by the host's reader, and being Return as ever for text,
  text and a shape, two shapes or a shape it refuses; the shape marked only when admitted; and
  `admittedShapes(at:)`: a `SlashShapeRule` on its line, after a bracket and on a later line, nil on a
  plain line, for a command that takes no shape, one not offered, no command, an `@` in the name,
  before the slash, past the end, or on another line; and for `park` the rule's kinds, its `rule`

- **MentionsTests' `slashTests`** (`SlashFixturesPlugin(log:)`: `ping`, `near` (any shape, by

- **PublishingTests' `slashTests`** hold `/public` and `/private`: offered on the kinds that can be

- **TitlesTests' `titleSlashTests`** hold `/title`: offered on the kinds that keep a title (a

- **CompositionTests' `slashCommandsShippedTests`** type `/lock`, `/title`, `/public` and

## Find

Find ([`Sources/Find`](../Sources/Find)) is ⌘F: it searches the board shown and every board under
it for text that matches what's typed, as a browser's ⌘F searches a page, highlights each hit where
its shape draws it, and lists the shapes it's in, in the detail panel's place. Matching is
[FuzzyMatching](#fuzzymatching)'s `TextSearch`: folded (case, diacritics, width), a phrase, every
exact place first, then word-anchored places one typo off for words of four letters or more, at
most 100 hits a text. Find is a surface (on Canvas, DetailPanel, FuzzyMatching, Geometry, Keyboard,
Selection and Topology) and knows no kind and no concern: what a shape shows as text, and where it
draws it, the plugins that draw it say. Its plugin is `FindPlugin()`, id `find-in-boards` (never
`find`, which is the command's name, `CanvasCommand.find`). It never transacts.

### What's searched: `FindableTexts`

A contribution says, for the kinds it's for, what a shape shows as text and where:

```swift
registrar.findableTexts("title", where: { $0.holds(TitleProperty.self) || $0.registry.titleIsDerived($0.kind) },
                        look: .ring, followsZoom: true,
                        zoomedOut: { record, _, context in context.editor.titleCover(of: record.id)?.rect },
                        texts: { record, context in
                            context.registry.title(of: record).map { [FindableText(field: "title", text: $0)] } ?? []
                        },
                        rects: { record, _, ranges, context in … })   // the pill's frame, from the shape's bounds' top-left
```

- **`texts`**: the shape's texts as it shows them, plain (`FindableText(field:text:)`: `field` is
  the contribution's own name for the text, handed back to `rects`). Cheap: Find reads them into
  its index as commits change the shape.
- **`rects`**: where each range (UTF-16, of that field's text) is drawn now, a list of line rects
  per range, in world units from the shape's kept bounds' top-left (`shapes.geometry(of:)`). Asked
  only for shapes in view with hits, and kept by Find for the query while the shape's size stays
  (and the zoom, with `followsZoom`, for text sized in view points: a title's pill), so a move asks
  nothing. Keep what you lay out by text and width, so asking again is a lookup: TextEditing's
  [`StringDrawingLayout`](#where-string-drawing-puts-text) lays text out as string drawing does.
- **`zoomedOut`**: where the text is said on a shape drawn as a skeleton (a title's cover); none, or
  nil, tints the shape's bounds.
- **`affected`**: the shapes a commit changes the texts of without changing them (a note showing
  another shape's live name), O(what it changed), as a row's `affected` is.
- **`look`** (`FindLook`): `.marker`, a highlighter, multiplied over the shape's own surface, the
  text as dark over it as it was (the default: a note's text, a card's); `.wash`, translucent, for
  text over the canvas, whose color follows the appearance (an arrow's label); `.ring`, round a dark
  badge a mark would hide (a title's pill).

`registrar.findableTexts(_:where:…)` is for every shape of the kinds `where` picks (a
`FindableKind`, asked once per kind: keep it to the kinds that opted into what's drawn, never `{ _ in
true }`), `registrar.findableTexts(_:of:…)` for a kind another plugin registers, `x.findableTexts(_:…)`
for a kind's own. The point (`FindableTexts`) is keyed by kind and name (two "title"s on one kind
conflict; a blank name is refused) and its owner is Find's, so a contribution needs `FindPlugin()`
installed. Shipped, each a plugin value of its owner's own, after Find and its owner in the list, so
a list without Find leaves them out:

| Contributor | Texts | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Titles' `TitleFindPlugin` | each title, named or derived (`registry.title(of:)`), on the kinds that hold `TitleProperty` or derive one | the pill's whole capsule, ringed (it may cut the title short); zoomed out, the cover |
| Mentions' `MentionFindPlugin` | each `MentionTexts` placement's text (a  note's, an arrow's label), each mention its live name | from the render's own layout, which Find's asking keeps with the drawn text (`MentionTextMemo`; drawing keeps none); a hit in a name is the whole pill; `affected`: `rowsAffected(by:)`. Two contributions, one a look: the placements on a shape's surface, marked, and those `overCanvas` (an arrow's label), washed |

### The index, and the search off the main actor

- **Nothing before the first ⌘F.** Find's index is built then; until then a commit costs a
  revision noted. Built, it holds every text every shape shows on every board the editor can show
  (none kept aside), folded once, by shape (never in file order). The build reads the boards' ids,
  then shapes a slice of 2 ms of the main actor at a time (`FindStyle.buildSlice`) on the editor's
  scheduler, the field showing a spinner meanwhile, so a first ⌘F on a big file drops no frame.
- **Each commit after it reads only what it changed**: contributions' `affected` first (so Mentions
  has heard the commit, and its names are the commit's), then what it removed, added, changed other
  than by moving, touched `elsewhere` (a subboard's deletion drops its boards' texts, going through
  whichever is fewer), and what `affected` named. One heard out of turn, or a file put in place,
  reads everything again; a switch of board reads nothing.
- **A search a keystroke, off the main actor.** The query is folded on the main actor, and the
  index's entries (a value, shared until the next commit copies the table once) and the scope's
  order are handed whole to a detached task (`@concurrent`), which a newer keystroke cancels;
  cancellation is asked every 256 shapes and every 64K units of a text, and an older answer is
  dropped. The scope's order is kept from one search to the next while nothing but moves changed
  the file, else worked out there from Topology's snapshot (`forEachShape(inFileOrder:)`). Results
  are compact (a shape, its count, its first hit); a shape's hits are worked out again when they're
  needed (in view, current, a listed row) by matching its one text.
- **While Find is open, a commit patches the results** for the shapes it changed: a count, a shape
  without hits gone, in place; a shape gaining its first hit has the scope searched again, off the
  main actor. A move patches nothing. A commit that lands while a search is under way starts it
  again instead (it read the index as it began, and its answer would undo the patch), landing as it
  would have. Any commit but a move drops the scope's kept order, query or not.

### Scope, order, and stepping

- **Scope**: the board shown when the query last changed (or ⌘F opened Find), and every board under
  it. Stepping and rows don't scope again; typing does, and so does the scope's board no longer
  being showable (deleted, or a file put in place without it): scoped again to the board shown,
  searched again, nothing retyped. **Order**: the scope board's shapes in file
  order (what a frame holds after the frame), then each board under it, depth first, in file order.
  The count ("3 of 12") counts hits, exact and typos alike; rows are one per shape.
- **Typing** makes current the first hit on the board shown that's in view, else its first,
  brought into view (`reveal`), else the first anywhere, without showing its board: typing never
  switches boards. The first 64 results on the board shown are asked their bounds; past them, the
  shapes in view (`paintOrder(in:)`) are looked up among the results, so thousands of hits out of
  view cost what's in view.
- **Stepping** (Return and ⇧Return in the field, ⌘G and ⇧⌘G anywhere, the panel's buttons) goes hit
  by hit, wrapping, showing a hit's board and bringing it into view unless it's there. A row's
  click makes its shape's first hit current, the same way, and leaves the keyboard in the field.
  With Find closed and something typed, ⌘G opens it and lands on the first hit in view, which is its
  step, and ⇧⌘G opens it, lands there and steps back.
- **One step back.** Nothing Find does changes the selection (though showing another board empties
  it, as every switch does), and a session's way around is one step back: Selection's
  `navigate(from:_:)`, from `navigationStart` taken as Find opens. Back after Find returns to where
  it began.
- **Edits keep the current hit**: its shape and which of its hits, clamped to those left, else the
  next shape's; the camera stays.

### ⌘F, and closing

`.find` (⌘F, Edit › Find › Find…) opens Find, or, open, focuses its field with its text selected;
it ends editing first, and what's selected in the text being edited (`editor.editingSelectedText`),
one line of it, is what's typed (an attachment in it that adopts `ReadsAsText`, a mention's pill,
reads as its text, any other attachment is dropped, so a selection across a pill is searched for by
the pill's name). It's refused mid-gesture. `.findNext` (⌘G) and `.findPrevious`
(⇧⌘G) run while there are hits, or with Find closed and a query. Closing (Escape or ⌘. in the
panel, the takeover's `onEscape`, or Done) takes the highlights away, shows the panel the
selection says, and gives the canvas the keyboard; what's typed is kept, for the next ⌘F to select.
Escape on the canvas is the canvas's own (Find stays open), and so is a click on a shape.

### The highlights

`FindOverlay` draws nothing, and asks for no shapes, while Find is closed or has no hits. In full,
each hit in view is drawn where its shape is drawn (its bounds' origin and `worldDrawingOffset(of:)`),
a path per look, the current one deeper with a thin line (`FindStyle`: an orange, which reads on a
note's yellow, where a browser's yellow would vanish, and on a card's white, alike in either
appearance). A frame lays out the shapes it hasn't before for 2 ms at most (`FindStyle.layoutBudget`,
always one), tinting the rest's bounds meanwhile and asking for another frame. Zoomed out, where
shapes are skeletons with no text, each shape with hits is washed over lightly (or where its text is
said, `zoomedOut`), so a title said on it still reads, the current one washed alike and lined round,
a shape under a device pixel its pixel, once. A hit under a shape in front shows through it.

### The panel, and the host

`FindPanel(editor:onExit:heading:)` is Find's panel: its own header (no Back): the field, with
a spinner while the index is built; Done; the count with Previous and Next (tooltips from
`registry.help(_:forCommand:)`: "Next (⌘G)"); and a row per shape with hits, the window of 200 around
the current one in a lazy stack, under its board's heading (named by `heading`, which the placer
supplies: Composition passes the path's names), each the kind's symbol in the kind's tint (`registry.label(of:)`), the text
around its first hit with its hits semibold (cut on whole characters, never inside a surrogate
pair), and its count when it has more than one; "No matches". Return steps unless an input method is
composing in the field.
Composition puts it in the detail panel's [takeover slot](#the-takeover-slot) while
`editor.find?.isActive`, with `onEscape` closing Find, and `boardChrome` shows a hidden inspector
when `focusRequest` changes (and hides it again as Find closes, if it showed it,
`revealedInspector`); hiding the inspector while Find is open closes Find. `FindState` (`editor.find`, `@Observable`) is what views read: `isActive`,
`query`, `results`, `total`, `current`, `currentNumber`, `focusRequest`, `isIndexing`.

### What it costs

A commit before the first ⌘F costs a revision noted; a drag with Find open, nothing; an edit, the
shapes it changed. A keystroke costs the main actor a fold and a handover, and the search runs off
it. A frame costs the shapes in view with hits, their layouts once each. `./build.sh bench` holds
them (Find's suite, `.claude/rules/benchmarks.md`).

### Testing Find

FindTests hold Find on fixtures of their own (memos, text in a monospaced grid, whose hits' rects are
known; badges, an every-shape contribution that rings and follows the zoom; pockets two deep): the
point, the index and its upkeep, scope and order, typing, stepping and its one step back, edits,
the highlights' pixels in full and zoomed out, the frame's budget, and the panel in an unshown
window beside the canvas. Each contributor's tests hold its texts and rects to its render's ink
(MentionsTests, TitlesTests, ArrowsTests), and CompositionTests the shipped wiring: Edit › Find's
items from the canvas, Find's field and a note being edited, a hidden inspector shown, the shipped
kinds' texts found and highlighted, a subboard's contents from the root.

## Topology

Topology ([`Sources/Topology`](../Sources/Topology)) is what connects and contains what, whatever
is where: edges, a typed graph (an arrow bound at both ends, a mention), and containment, a tree
of two kinds of link (the [container](#containers) a shape is in on its board, a frame, else the
board it's on, and so which shapes it's inside). Spatial relations (a note that happens to sit
within another shape's bounds) aren't part of it; they're geometry. It's a horizontal
on the core alone: the plugins that own what a connection means (Ports, through its connector, and
Mentions) say what their shapes carry, and any plugin asks what's connected to a shape, and how,
without knowing arrows or mentions.

```swift
guard let topology = editor.topology else { return }                   // nil without TopologyPlugin
topology.neighbors(of: note)                                            // ["note-link": [a, b], "mention": [c]]
topology.edges(of: note, .incoming, types: .only(MentionEdge.id))       // who mentions it, anywhere in the file
topology.edges(ofType: .within(ArrowEdge.id))                           // every arrow bound at both ends, on any channel
topology.isInside(note, subboard)                                       // on its board, in a frame there, or on a board under it
```

### The shapes are the system of record

An edge is carried by a shape, its **carrier**: an arrow's record (its two bound ends, and its
channel, `added.channel`) is its edge, and a note's text is its mentions. Topology's index is
derived from the records, for the whole file, in memory, and never saved: nothing goes in props,
metadata or the file, so nothing can disagree with the shapes, and whatever already works on shapes
(undo, copy and paste, a deletion's cascade, migrations, `canvas draw`, a board from an older app)
works on edges with nothing more.

tldraw keeps bindings as records of their own beside the shapes (an arrow's binding to a shape is
a record from the arrow to the shape), which its store keeps in step with both. Here that would be
a second truth about each connection: records to copy, delete with either end, migrate and undo,
kept in step with the carrier they describe. And a mention outlives the shape it names, which a
binding can't. So the carrier holds a connection once ([Values that name
shapes](#values-that-name-shapes)), and the index is a way to read it.

### Edges

An `Edge` goes from `source` to `target`, of `type` (its most specific), carried by `carrier` in
`slot` ("" for the carrier itself, as an arrow is; else the name of the property that holds it, a
kind's own or an added property's key: a note's mentions are in `text`), `count` times there (a note
that mentions a shape twice: 2; an arrow: 1), and how it came to be, its `origin`: `.emitted`, as
its carrier emitted it; `.forwarded(source:target:)`, emitted with a [stand-in](#stand-ins-forwarding)
at an end, which it names there (the edge's own end is a shape the stand-in stands for); or
`.standing`, a stand-in's own edge to a shape it stands for. Its identity is its carrier, slot, type,
ends and origin; `count` is a value. `literalSource` and `literalTarget` are its ends as emitted, and
`literal` the edge as emitted. Its ends needn't be there: a mention outlives what it names, so how
an end is now is asked when it's read (`end(_:)`, below).

Only a connection bound at both ends is an edge: an arrow with a free end carries none. A shape
kept aside (`record.isOpaque`) carries none, nor does a shape on a board the editor can't show.

### Types

- **An edge type is a type** (`EdgeType`: `static let id: EdgeTypeID`, and `static var parent`
  and `static var summary`, nil by default), declared by the plugin that owns what it means
  (`registrar.edgeType(T.self)`; the `EdgeTypes` point, one declaration per id: two are a
  `conflict`). The id audit holds an `EdgeTypeID` literal to the module that declares it, as it
  does a channel's.
- **Types are a tree.** Each is under at most one parent, which some installed plugin must declare,
  and none is under itself (`EdgeTypes.check`):

  ```
  EdgeTypes: more declares edge type spark under fire, which no installed plugin declares
  EdgeTypes: more declares edge type spark under itself: spark → flame → spark
  ```
- **Shipped:** `stands-for` (`StandingEdge`, Topology's own, declared by `TopologyPlugin`: a
  [stand-in](#stand-ins-forwarding)'s edge to each shape it stands for), a root, so every
  vocabulary lists it first; `arrow` (`ArrowEdge`, Connections'), a plain arrow's type, and under it
  each channel's, `note-link` and `subboard-link`; `mention` (`MentionEdge`, Mentions'), a root; and `is-a` (`IsAEdge`, Types'), a root, from a shape to each
  type its `is` names, derived with the property rule below. A channel is an
  edge type of the same name, which `registrar.channel(C.self)` declares with it
  ([Channels](#channels)), under the family the connector names (`connects(_:edgeType:…)`), so its
  parent follows from the registry as built: `registrar.edgeType(_:parent:)` is that form, the
  parent a closure over the frozen registry. `ArrowEdge.id` is `EdgeTypeID(rawValue:
  Arrow.kind.rawValue)`, so the family's id is the arrow kind's name, said once.
- **What a type means** is its `summary`: a lowercase line, no period, saying what it joins and
  which way it runs, which a [query's vocabulary](#queries) shows beside it
  (`EdgeTypeTree.summary(of:)`; `edgeType(_:parent:summary:)` carries one, and Connections' `Channel.summary`,
  nil by default, is passed on by `registrar.channel(C.self)` to the type it declares). Shipped:
  `arrow`, "an arrow bound at both ends, from the shape it starts on to the shape it ends on, whatever
  its arrowheads"; `note-link`, "an arrow drawn on the note-link channel", and `subboard-link` likewise;
  `mention`, "a mention in a shape's text, from that shape to the shape it names"; `is-a`, "from a shape
  to each type it is, in the order of its list"; `stands-for`, "from a shape to each shape it stands for".
- **An edge reports its most specific type**, and a query names types with an `EdgeTypeFilter`:
  `.all`; `.within(t, …)`, those types and every type under them (`.within(ArrowEdge.id)` is every
  arrow, plain or on a channel); `.only(t, …)`, exactly those (`.only(ArrowEdge.id)` is plain
  arrows alone). Each also takes a sequence (`.within(types)`, a query's resolved types), and an
  empty one admits nothing.
- **A type nobody declares** (an arrow's channel from a newer app, or from a plugin that isn't
  installed) is kept as written: it's the edge's type, `types.isDeclared(t)` is false, and it has no
  parent, so only `.all` and a filter that names it match it. A channel that names a type declared
  as something else (`mention`) is the connector's family instead, so no source's edges pass for
  another's.
- **The tree** is `registry.edgeTypes`, worked out on each call, or an editor's `topology.types`,
  kept (`EdgeTypeTree`: `declared`, in plugin order, `isDeclared(_:)`, `plugin(declaring:)`,
  `parent(of:)`, `children(of:)`, `ancestors(of:)`, parent first, and `descendants(of:)`).

### Sources

What a record carries is said by sources (the `EdgeSources` point), which add up: a kind's shapes
carry what each of its sources emits, in plugin order, with no precedence.

```swift
// A kind's own, typed:
x.edges { shape, registry, sink in … }
// A kind another plugin registers (from a plugin that imports it, or a horizontal's over a kind it's given):
registrar.edges(K.self) { record, registry, sink in … }
// Every kind `where` picks, asked once per kind:
registrar.edgesForEveryShape(where: { kind, registry in registry.namingKinds.contains(kind) }) { record, registry, sink in … }
// Every shape a value of an added property names, from the shape that holds it:
registrar.edges(in: BlockedByProperty.self, as: BlockedByEdge.self)
```

- **A source is pure** (`EdgeEmitter`): a function of one record and the frozen registry. It never
  reads other shapes, geometry, services, the camera or the time, and never depends on where a box
  is. That's what lets the index follow a commit by reading only the records it changed, skip those
  it only moved (`ChangeSet.moved`), and have undo put edges back exactly. Nothing checks it: a
  source that reads more goes stale.
- **`sink.emit(type, from:to:slot:)`** says one edge. Emitting the same type, ends and slot again
  counts it again; edges keep the order they were first emitted in (a text's order).
- **Ports' source** is the connector's: `connects(K.self, edgeType: F.self, …, ends:)` emits one
  edge for a connection `ends` finds bound at both ends, typed by its channel or, drawn on none, by
  `F` ([`ArrowPortsPlugin`](#the-connector-arrows)). **Mentions'** is over the kinds that can hold
  names: each mention in mention text wherever a shape keeps it (`record.forEachNamingValue(in:)`,
  then `forEachNamingLeaf`), in the slot of the property it's in.
- **The property rule**, `registrar.edges(in: P.self, as: T.self)` for an added property whose
  value names shapes (`P.Value: ShapeNaming`), is for a relation nobody draws or writes in text
  (what a task is blocked by): every shape a value of `P` names is an edge of type `T` from the
  shape that holds it, in the slot `P`'s key names, on every kind that opts into `P`. It doesn't
  declare `T`: `edgeType` does. Types uses it for `is`: `registrar.edgeType(IsAEdge.self)` and
  `registrar.edges(in: IsAProperty.self, as: IsAEdge.self)`, so every note and arrow that is a type's
  instance has an `is-a` edge to it, in the slot `is`.
- **`registry.edges(of: record)`** is what one record carries, as its kind's sources say, pure: for
  code that holds a record the index doesn't (a transaction's), and for tests.

- **Topology's own edges are reserved.** A source that emits into the slot `stands-for`, or an edge
  of that type (`StandingEdge`, below), has it dropped (in debug builds, `reservedEdgesDropped` counts
  them), so a standing edge is only ever a stand-in's.

The registry's report shows `edge type mention` on the declarer's line, and `edges → every shape`
or `edges → arrow` on the line of the plugin that contributes the source ([The
registry](#the-registry)).

### Stand-ins: forwarding

A shape may **stand in** for other shapes, so that an arrow to it counts, for every reader, as an
arrow to what it stands for: a shape that too much points at can be pointed at through stand-ins
placed where they're wanted. The kind says so, and Topology does the rest; it knows nothing of why
(no kind, no publicness, no query):

```swift
x.standsIn(maxTargets: 50, admitting: { target, registry in … }) { shape, registry in
    .shapes(shape.props.stands)             // what its record names, on any board
    // or .provided(ForwardingKey(shape.props.question)): whatever is provided for that key
}
```

- **What it stands for** (`effective`, worked out from records alone): what the rule names, in
  order, each once (a name again is left out, the first kept), taking only shapes on a board the
  editor can show, not kept aside, not itself, not stand-ins (one hop: a stand-in never stands for
  a stand-in), and that `admitting` takes (pure, of the target's record and the registry), up to
  `maxTargets` (50 by default; `EdgeForwarding.check` refuses fewer than 1). `.provided` stands for
  nothing until an answer comes for the key its record holds now ([`provide`](#provided-answers-the-one-delivery-settling)),
  and the answer's shapes are taken by the same rule. The rule (`ForwardingRule`) is
  pure, as a source is: never another shape, geometry, a service or the time. One rule per kind
  (the `EdgeForwarding` point, keyed by kind; the report says `stands in → kind`).
- **Edges, resolved.** An edge any other shape carries with a stand-in at an end becomes one edge
  per pair of what each end stands for (an end that's no stand-in, or stands for nothing, stays
  itself), source by source, each `.forwarded` with the stand-in at each end it replaced, at most
  `EdgeForwarding.maxPairsPerCarrier` (256) per carrier, though every edge a carrier emits keeps
  one (an arrow between two stand-ins for 50 each is held to 256, not 2,500). A stand-in that
  stands for nothing leaves an edge into it as it was: nothing dangles because of a stand-in, and
  what's wrong is for the stand-in's kind to show. A stand-in's own edges are never forwarded, and
  it carries a `stands-for` edge (`StandingEdge`, Topology's own, a root `TopologyPlugin` declares:
  "from a shape to each shape it stands for"; slot `stands-for`) to each shape it stands for, so `edges(of: a,
  .incoming, types: .only(StandingEdge.id))` is what stands for `a`, and `revision(of: a)` moves as
  stand-ins come and go. An arrow from `a` to a stand-in for `a` is a loop on `a`, there once.
- **Three views** (`EdgeView`), every edge read taking one: `.resolved`, the default, every
  stand-in forwarded and standing edges, so queries, Mentions, the table of contents and any future
  reader treat an arrow to a stand-in as one to what it stands for without knowing stand-ins exist;
  `.recorded`, forwarded only through stand-ins whose record names what they stand for
  (`.shapes`), those for what's provided left at their own end with no standing edges, a function
  of the records alone (what a provided answer may be worked out from, so no answer ever reads
  another's); and `.literal`, each end as emitted and no standing edges. Copies of one fan-out that
  a view reads back as one edge are one.
- **New reads**: `forwards(of:)`, what a stand-in stands for now, in order; `standIns(for:)`, what
  stands for a shape; `forwarding(of:)`, `ForwardingState` (`.none`, `.record([…])`,
  `.provided([…])`, `.pending`, waiting for an answer); `edges(through:)`, the resolved edges
  forwarded through a stand-in, one per shape it stands for; and `standInKinds`, on the index and
  a snapshot.
- **Making one for a shape.** A kind a plugin may put down beside a shape by name rather than by a
  gesture (`canvas draw`'s edge to a shape on another board, [below](#draw)) says how, in the same
  rule:

  ```swift
  x.standsIn(admitting: { target, registry in … },
             needs: "public",                        // one word, for a message: what a shape must be to be stood for
             makes: { props, target, label in … }) { shape, registry in … }   // fill what the tool places, so it stands for `target`
  ```

  `makes` is given the props the kind's tool places (`registry.placement(for:)`), the shape to stand
  for and what to call it there (what a person picking it would have been shown: the shape's name), and
  leaves them as the kind's own writers would (References': `ReferenceEdits.pick`); `needs` is read by
  no rule, only said ("only a public shape can be stood for", "ask the user to make it public").
  `registry.standIns` (`StandIns`, main actor, nothing kept: the registry never changes) reads the
  rules without an index: `kinds`, `isEmpty`, `forwarding(of: record)` (a record's rule, applied: what
  it says it stands for, as the index reads it), `makers` (the kinds whose rule says how and that a
  tool places, in plugin order), `admits(kind, target)` (the kind's `admitting`, and never for a shape
  kept aside or one that itself stands in: one hop), `needs(kind)`, and `make(kind, standingFor:,
  label:)`, a new record in no document: the tool's shape at the origin, `makes` applied, put in step
  as writing its properties would (`DerivedProps`: a pill's width fits its label). `make` doesn't ask
  `admits`: whoever puts the shape down does, since a stand-in for a shape it may not stand for stands
  for nothing.
- **Kept sparse.** The index keeps what each carrier emitted (`byCarrier`), the resolved edges by
  each end and type (an edge filed under its ends and its literal ends, so it's found from the
  stand-in it went through too), and a carrier's resolved edges apart only where forwarding
  changed them; the other views are read by mapping each forwarded edge back through its origin.
  A file with no stand-ins keeps exactly what it did before there were any, and costs what it did
  (TopologyTests read `resolvedCarrierCount`, debug builds): each record's kind is looked up once, and
  the stand-in tables only while they hold something. An `Edge` hashes its two ends alone (it's equal
  by every field), so the sets the tables diff and collapse in cost a fraction; its origin is boxed (one
  word), and a `ShapeID` is two words, so an edge copies and compares as plain words do.

### Provided answers, the one delivery, settling

A stand-in whose record asks a question (`.provided(ForwardingKey(…))`) stands for whatever its
answer names. Topology doesn't work answers out; whoever does gives them, with no commit:

```swift
topology.provide([lens: ProvidedForwarding(key: ForwardingKey(question), shapes: matches, revision: n)])

let following = topology.follow { change in        // every change to the edges, once, whatever its cause
    for id in change.touched(types: .only(MentionEdge.id), in: topology.types) { … }
}
let source = topology.keepsSettling { batchIsOut || !topology.pendingStandIns.isEmpty }
let settled = await topology.settled(timeout: .seconds(5))   // false if it ran out
```

- **`provide`** takes answers that are never saved and never undone. One for another key than the
  stand-in's record holds now, for a shape that isn't such a stand-in (on a board the editor can
  show), or older (`revision`) than the one held for that key is dropped and touches nothing. A
  commit that changes a stand-in's key, deletes it or hides its board lets go of its answer, as
  every rebuild does (they were for the file as it was), so an answer given again after an undo
  (a memo) is taken whatever its revision. It runs a commit's stand-in pass seeded with the
  stand-ins it answered: what each stands for is worked out (the same rule as named shapes), the
  carriers at those whose shapes changed are set again, revisions bump, `touched` is its ends. A
  commit to a shape an answer names looks at the stand-in again, as one to a named shape does.
  `forwarding(of:)` is `.provided([…])` once answered, `.pending` before; `pendingStandIns` lists
  those waiting. Call it from a scheduled callback or a task's continuation on the main actor:
  never while a service hears a commit or a switch, and never from a follower (a debug assert).
- **One delivery.** `touched` is the ends of the last change to the edges, a commit's or a
  provide's, and each change is told once to every follower (`follow`, `TopologyChange`: `touched`,
  `touchedByType`, `cause`: `.commit`, `.provide` or `.rebuild`), with the index as the change left
  it; a commit that changes no edge (a move) tells nothing, and a provide that changes none leaves
  `touched` as it was. A service that kept state off edges by reading `touched` as it heard a commit
  would miss every provide, so following is the way to keep it: Mentions follows (a commit's
  backlinks are bumped as it hears the commit, a provide's at once). A follower reads only Topology
  and the file, writes no document and never provides; it lasts while its token
  (`TopologyFollowing`) is held, or until `cancel()`.
- **Settling.** A stand-in waiting for its answer leaves arrows at itself for a moment. Whoever
  provides registers a source (`keepsSettling(while:)`, a `SettleSource` token: a wait armed, a
  batch out, a stand-in asked and not answered), and says `settleSourceChanged()` when it goes idle
  with no provide or commit to say so. `isSettling` is whether any source is busy, and
  `settled(timeout:)` waits until none is: true then (at once if none is now), false when the
  timeout runs out (on `editor.scheduler`, so tests run it by hand) or the task is cancelled. Every
  delivery, provide and source change or cancel wakes the waits. A reader that must see the
  settled graph (a query after a draw) waits on it: `QueryState.run` does, given `settle:`
  ([Queries](#many-at-once-edge-views-and-waiting)).

### The index: `TopologyIndex`

`editor.topology` (nil without `TopologyPlugin`) is the file's edges, one index per editor, by
carrier, by each end and by type. It never transacts, and isn't an undo participant: it follows the
file. Every query costs what it returns, never a board:

| Query | Is |
|---|---|
| `edges(of: id, direction, types:)` | Every edge touching a shape, anywhere in the file, [resolved](#stand-ins-forwarding) through stand-ins (each read below also takes `view:`, `.recorded` or `.literal`): `.outgoing`, `.incoming` or `.either` (the default), of the types the filter admits (`.all` by default). By carrier, in the order the carriers came (those read as the editor opened in the file's order, root first; those one commit brings, a paste's or an undo's, in no order among themselves), each carrier's in the order it emits them. An edge from a shape to itself is there once. `hasEdges(of:_:types:where:)` stops at the first (that `where` takes), and makes nothing: cheap enough for what's asked on every commit (Mentions' `isMentioned`). |
| `neighbors(of: id, direction, types:)` | The shapes at the other ends, by each edge's type, each once per type, in the order its first edge comes: what's connected to a shape, and how. The shape itself, for an edge from it to itself. |
| `edges(ofType: filter)` | Every edge in the file of the types the filter admits: type by type (declared ones in plugin order, then the rest by name), each by carrier. |
| `edges(carriedBy: carrier)` | What a shape carries, in the order it emits them. |
| `end(id)` | How a shape at an end of an edge is now (`EdgeEnd`): `.live(board)` on a board the editor can show, `.unavailable` in the file on a board it can't (under an owner kept aside), `.missing` in no board of the file. |
| `revision(of: id)`, `touched` | A shape's revision, +1 each time its edges (at either end) change, from the first time it's read: reading it observes only that shape (a key path per shape, as Mentions' `labelRevision`), so a SwiftUI view of one shape's connections redraws when they change. `touched` is the shapes whose edges the last change to them, a commit's or a [provide's](#provided-answers-the-one-delivery-settling), changed (none after a switch of board), and `touched(types:)` those whose edges of some types it changed; `follow` tells each change as it comes, the way to hear one. |

### Containment

Containment is a tree, never an edge, of two kinds of link: a board's owner holds the shapes on its
board, and a [container](#containers) (a frame, a `ShapeContaining` kind's shape) holds the shapes
on its own board that are in it. One tree, so every reader follows both, whatever kind owns or
contains:

- **`parent(of:)`** is the container a shape is in on its board, else the owner of the board it's
  on (nil on the root in no container): a container's parent is its own container, else its
  board's owner.
- **`children(of:)`** is what a container holds, back to front, then, for a shape that owns a board,
  that board's shapes in no container, back to front (a kind that both owns a board and contains
  lists what it holds first).
- **`ancestors(of:)`** is what a shape is inside, the nearest first: its containers, its board's
  owner, that one's containers, and so on up; **`isInside(a, b)`** whether `a` is inside `b` at any
  depth (never inside itself; O(`a`'s depth)).

It needs no index of its own: the core knows which board every shape is on, and each board keeps
who's in which container (`CanvasDocument`'s index of who names whom, nonisolated). Only containers
the core goes by count (`document.container(of:containingKinds:)`: one kept aside, or of a kind that
holds nothing here, holds nothing, and a shape kept aside is in none). As with edges, only shapes on
boards the editor can show count (nil, none, or false for the rest). It's one piece of code,
`Containment`, a value over a `CanvasFile`, the kinds that own boards and the containing kinds,
which the index makes over the file as it is for each question and a
[snapshot](#a-snapshot-for-other-threads) keeps over the file as it was taken, so the two answer
alike. `containerKinds` (on `Registry`, the index and the snapshot) is which kinds contain others:
those that own boards (`boardOwningKinds`) and those whose shapes hold shapes on theirs
(`containingKinds`). Containment keeps nothing, so a commit costs it nothing (and a move, a
container's with what it holds, reads no record for edges either), and a board without containers
costs each question what it did before there were any (`document.namesContainers`, O(1)).

### A snapshot for other threads

`topology.snapshot()` is Topology as it is now, for any thread: a `TopologySnapshot`, `Sendable`,
taken in O(1), reading no record and observing nothing. It reads edges in one
[view](#stand-ins-forwarding), resolved unless taken in another (`snapshot(.recorded)`), and
answers `forwards(of:)` and `standIns(for:)` too; its shapes and containment are the same in every
view (containment is never forwarded: a stand-in inside a frame doesn't put what it stands for
there). It shares the index's tables (its edges as
a value) and the editor's file (read without observing it), with the edge types, and answers
through the same code the index does, the tables and `Containment`, so what it answers is what the
index would have answered as it was taken: every question about edges and containment, though not
what changed (no `revision(of:)` or `touched`). A query takes one as it takes up the file and reads
it off the main actor, uninterrupted, whatever commits land meanwhile ([Queries](#queries)).

```swift
let graph = topology.snapshot()                                         // on the main actor, O(1)
Task.detached {
    graph.forEachShape { record, board in … }                          // every shape the app can show, in file order
    graph.neighbors(of: note, .outgoing, types: .within(ArrowEdge.id))  // as the index would have answered
}
```

Beside the index's questions, it reads the file whole:

- **`forEachShape(inFileOrder:)`**: every shape on a board the app can show, kept-aside ones too,
  with its board, in file order, the tree's, depth first: the root's shapes in no container, back to
  front, each followed at once by what's inside it (what it holds, back to front, then, for a shape
  that owns a board, that board's shapes in no container), and theirs, before the next. It's
  iterative, so a chain of boards or containers of any depth is walked, and no board or container
  twice. An error its body throws stops it, and comes out as the body's own type (`throws(E)`: a
  query's cancellation is a `QueryError`).
- **`fileOrderKey(of:)`**: where a shape comes in that order, as a key that sorts lexicographically
  (for each shape it's inside, from the outermost down, then for itself, its place among what's
  directly inside the same shape: its index on its board); nil off the boards the app can show.
  O(its depth): for putting a few shapes in order without walking the file.
- **`topLevel`**, the shapes inside nothing (the root's in no container, in document order), and
  **`isTopLevel(_:)`**, O(1); **`descendants(of:)`**, every shape inside a shape at any depth, in file
  order (O(what's inside it)); and **`container(of:on:)`**, the container a record on a board is
  directly in there, O(1), with no lookup for a shape in none: what a query's walk reads for each
  shape it has, working out what's above each container and each board once.
- **`shape(_:)`**, a record on a board the app can show, kept aside or not (`isOpaque` tells), nil
  elsewhere (O(its depth)); **`presentTypes`**, the types of the edges the file has, declared or
  not; and **`end(_:)`**, as the index's.

**Hold one for a task, never past it.** Nothing is copied while it's held until a commit changes a
table it shares; that commit copies the table, once (a move changes none of the index's; a shape
added or removed copies the file's `locations`). Kept, a snapshot makes every later commit's first
change to a table copy it. And one taken by a service hearing a commit before Topology has is that
commit's file with the commit before's edges, as the index's own answers are then: `catchUp` first.
TopologyTests' Snapshots suite holds a snapshot to the index on every question, over a seeded run of
every kind of commit, switch and undo, and a snapshot taken a step before to its old answers.

### What it costs

- **As the editor opens**, every board it can show is read (the root, then down through the owners
  of boards it can show, as `canShow` has it: `registry.ownsShowableBoard`), each record's sources
  asked; a kind with none costs a lookup. Each stand-in's rule is asked as it's read; once every
  board is, what each stand-in stands for is worked out, and only the carriers at those whose
  shapes changed are set a second time, so a file with no stand-ins costs what it did. A file or a board put in place (`replaceFile`,
  `replaceDocument`) is read again, and only the carriers whose edges changed touch anything.
- **Each commit** costs what it changed: the records it removed, touched on other boards
  (`ChangeSet.elsewhere`: the boards a deletion took or a paste brought, a write to a board that
  isn't shown), added, or changed other than by moving, each read again from the file as it is now
  (a shape on no board the editor can show carries nothing). Then, where there are stand-ins: what
  each stand-in it read, and each whose record names a shape it read, stands for is worked out
  again (O(the shapes they name)), and only the carriers with an edge at a stand-in whose shapes
  changed are set again (O(that stand-in's edges)). A move reads nothing: no source, rule or
  admission may read where a box is. Undo and redo are commits like any
  other. Showing another board reads nothing: the index is the file's (`boardDidChange` does
  nothing but for a file put in place).
- **Heard first.** A service that reads the index as it hears a commit must find it up to date.
  The shipped list has `TopologyPlugin()` right after `SelectionPlugin()`, so its service is made,
  and hears each commit, before those that read it; one that may hear a commit first calls
  `topology.catchUp(changes)` with the commit it holds, which does nothing once the index has heard
  it (MentionState does, and looks up `editor.topology` as it's made, so Topology's service is made
  first).
- **A provide** costs what it changes: the answered stand-ins' rule worked out, and the carriers
  at those whose shapes changed set again, each edge diffed and filed under up to four ends and its
  type (an arrow into a stand-in for 50 is 50 edges; the per-carrier cap holds one between two to
  256).
- **Held.** `./build.sh bench`: Topology's index and Mentions' catalog of 10,000 shapes, built as
  the file opens, within 50 ms (the budget Mentions' own index had); `neighbors(of:)` of a shape
  with 100 edges within 1 ms; and a drag's input, a subboard of 10,000 deleted in a frame, and its
  undo in 100 ms, with Topology hearing them. With stand-ins (`StandInBenchmarks.swift`, the bench's
  own kinds, so a budget holds the mechanism whatever kind stands in): the index opening with 100 of them and 1,000 arrows
  into them within the same 50 ms, what's connected through 100 within 1 ms, re-pointing one with
  100 arrows within 1 ms, a drag of 50 costing a drag event nothing more, a commit while a query
  holds the file among 500 within `queryHeldCommit`, and a provide that fans out (`provideFanOut`). `recordsRead` (debug builds) counts the records
  sources read, so tests hold a commit to what it changed.

Every plugin list with a plugin that contributes to Topology's points (Ports, Mentions) needs
`TopologyPlugin()`, as one with Selection needs `KeyboardPlugin()`: a contribution to a point whose
owner isn't installed is `ownerNotInstalled`.

### What it doesn't do

- **Loose edges.** An arrow with a free end isn't an edge; there's no query for connections
  half-made.
- **Spatial relations.** A shape that happens to lie within another's bounds isn't inside it;
  that's geometry (`editor.paintOrder(in:)`, `shapeContext.bounds(of:)`). What's in a frame is what
  it holds, which the core's in-or-out rule keeps within it, not what its bounds cover (a locked
  shape a frame grows over stays out).
- **Drawing by type.** Agents read the graph with [`canvas query`](#query), through a snapshot
  (`:edge-to`, `:downstream-of`, `"Payments" *`), but `canvas draw` matches an edge it restates by
  its ends, not by its type.
- **Showing it.** Nothing in the app shows a shape's connections in general yet (a Connections
  section of its panel); what mentions a shape is shown, Mentions' Mentioned In tab and Show What
  Mentions.

## Queries

Queries ([`Sources/Queries`](../Sources/Queries)) finds the shapes of a file a query matches: a
selector in a CSS-like language over every shape on every board the app can show, by kind, title,
id, attributes typed by their kind's schema, text, Topology's containment and typed edges, and the
words plugins add. It's a surface on Topology, over the core and QueryLanguage (DrawScript lends
it only its "did you mean", `Suggestions`), knows no concern, and hears no commit: the engine every
plugin may run, where the language agents write is `canvas query` and the words the lexicon gives it.
Agents ask through [`canvas query`](#query); any plugin may ask too (words for a concern still come
through QueryLexicon, by convention, though the layers don't forbid a concern contributing one):

```swift
guard let queries = editor.queries else { return }                 // nil without QueriesPlugin
let result = try await queries.run(QueryRequest(#""Payments" sticky-note:mentions("Auth")"#, limit: 20))
result.count                                                        // every shape that matches, listed or not
result.rows                                                         // the first 20, in file order
```

The language, every form, word and refusal, is taught to agents by the canvas skill
([`reference/query.md`](../.claude/skills/canvas/reference/query.md), whose every block SkillTests
runs on a file of its own, so it can't drift from the app). What a plugin needs of it:

- **A query** is a list of selectors, commas between them, each of compounds joined by a space
  (inside, at any depth) or `>` (directly inside: in a container, or on an owner's board in no
  container); a compound is at most one head (a kind, `*`, a title in quotes, a kind with a title
  right after it, `sticky-note"Checkout"`, as CSS writes
  `div#id`, or `#` and an id) and then tests with no space between them, attributes in brackets
  and `:word`s: `"Payments" sticky-note[text*="retry" i]:mentions("Auth")`. A selector answers with
  the shapes its last compound matches, as in CSS, and a list with those any of its selectors does,
  each once.
- **QueryLanguage** ([`Sources/QueryLanguage`](../Sources/QueryLanguage)), a foundation module that
  knows no canvas, registry or plugin, reads it: `SelectorList(parsing:)`, a tree whose every part
  knows its place in the text (`QuerySpan`, in characters of the query as sent), and `canonical`,
  the one form it prints (its own words in lowercase, titles in double quotes, one space around `>`,
  no comments), which is what an answer says ran. It refuses what the text alone shows
  (`empty_query`, `syntax`, `stray_space`, `too_long`, `too_complex`, `unsupported` (also `.Name`,
  hinted toward a plugin's word through a `HintPremise` claim, `typeWord`), `not_built` for the
  words people invent that are planned, `not_an_id`, and `bad_argument` for its own words),
  stopping at the first, and knows only its own words (`Word`: `:not`,
  `:is`, `:where`, `:has`, `:inside`, `:top-level`, `:current-board`, the edge words, `:dangling`,
  `:contains`); another's argument it keeps as text for the engine to read as shapes
  (`SelectorList(argumentOf:)`, its spans in the whole query), or to refuse with the rewrite for a
  word people invent (`KnownInventions`: `:parent-of`, `:near`, `:source-of`, and `:neighbor-of`,
  the language's old name for `:connected-to`). `QueryLimits` bounds it: 8,192 characters, 1,024
  in a string, 32 levels of parentheses, 256 compounds, 20 problems said.
- **Queries resolves it** against what this app has (`queries.check(_:)`, into a `QueryPlan`,
  `Sendable`, whose `description` prints it as a tree), refusing what isn't there with the one like
  it (`unknown_kind`, `unknown_attribute`, `unknown_pseudo_class`, `unknown_edge_type`,
  `invalid_value`, `unsupported_operator`, `cannot_contain`, `no_names`; `not_built` for an
  attribute that holds a place and `=` on an object; and the words people write in brackets,
  `[kind=…]`, `[id=…]`, `[board=…]`, with what to write, and `[class=…]`, `unsupported` as `.Name`
  is), every problem that doesn't hang on another
  at once, in the query's order; and answers it, refusing a title or an id no shape has
  (`unknown_title`, `unknown_id`) rather than answering none. Nothing unknown is passed over: a
  query that runs asked what it says, and a hint is most often the query to write instead. A hint
  that is a query is never one the app would refuse for a reason the query it mends didn't have:
  one that takes for granted what only the app can say (that a title is some shape's, that a
  kind's shapes can have titles, that what it puts where a container goes holds shapes) waits for
  it (`HintPremise`, QueryLanguage's, settled by the kinds and ids as the query resolves and by the
  titles as it's answered: `#Checkout` hints `"Checkout"` only where a shape is titled so).
  A plan says three things about itself, for a plugin that keeps an answer past the moment it was
  asked: `editorWords`, the words in it whose verdict reads the editor (`:selected`, `:invalid`,
  `:current-board`, a text read through a format that reads the editor), `readsOnlyTheFile` (none does: what
  it matches is a function of the file as the query takes it up, whoever asks, whatever they have
  selected or shown), and `readsEdges` (it has an edge word, so the edge view and a wait for answers
  still arriving matter to it).

### What a query sees

- **Every shape on every board the app can show** (`canShow`'s), none kept aside: a kept-aside
  shape has no properties to read and carries no edges, and a board the app can't show is the
  file's, not the app's. `#` with such a shape's id is refused `unknown_id`, saying which it is.
- **File order**, for every answer: the root's shapes in no container, back to front, each
  container followed at once by what it holds and each shape that owns a board by that board's
  shapes, all the way down, the order Topology's snapshot walks in (`forEachShape(inFileOrder:)`, or
  `fileOrderKey(of:)` for a few shapes), so the engine never walks boards or containers itself. The
  same query on the same file answers in the same order. Both are Topology's, so without
  `TopologyPlugin` every query is `no_topology`.
- **One instant, but for what only the main actor knows.** An answer is the file as it was when the
  app took up the query, but for titles a shape works out from what it holds (a derived title) and
  validity (`:invalid`, `:warned`), which are as the app has them when the query asks: a shape a
  commit changed while the query ran can answer with its newer title or verdict, never an older one,
  and one gone since has no title and fails the word. So no main-actor code is ever handed a record
  the app has since replaced, and no plugin's cache keeps one. The board shown (`:current-board`) and
  what's selected (`:selected`) are as they were when it started.
- **Titles through the names point** (Titles', through QueryLexicon's `TitleQueriesPlugin`). A head `"Checkout"` is every
  shape whose title, folded as Titles folds one, is the literal folded, case and all, named or
  derived; several shapes may share it, and it names them all. A title no shape has is refused, so
  a no always means the shape is there: `[title="X"]`, which folds its literal the same way, is how
  to ask whether one is, its count of 0 an answer (warned `no_title_match`). A kind with a title
  right after it, `sticky-note"Checkout"`, is the kind's shapes with that title: a title head
  beside the kind's (the title's node first, as it finds its shapes), so a title no shape has is
  refused as `"Checkout"` is, one only other kinds have answers none, and a kind whose shapes have
  no titles is `unknown_attribute`, as `[title=…]` on it is. With a space between, the title is
  inside the kind's shapes, and where they hold no board the refusal (`cannot_contain`) hints the
  two together, if they can have titles. Without a names point, a title is `no_names`.
- **Attributes through the kinds' schemas** (`registry.schema(for:)`, read with
  [`KindSchema`](#a-kinds-schema)): every property, own or added, but those that hold a place (where
  a shape is isn't in the language yet: `frame`, `not_built`), and the names point's word (`title`),
  read through the names point, so a derived title is an attribute too, on the kinds whose shapes
  have titles. A literal is read by its property's schema as `draw` reads a value, and the test is
  typed by it: a number numerically (`[rank=3]` and `[rank="3"]` alike; one that isn't finite
  matches no number test), a date-time by its UTC day (`[due<2026-10-01]`) or instant, a choice from
  its list (`i`: in any case), a list by its items (`~=`), text as text (`^=`, `$=`, `*=`, `|=`, and
  `i` for any case; `<` refused). An absent true|false is its schema's default, else false
  (`[locked=false]` is every unlocked shape); `[a]` is a value that says something (true, text, a
  list or an object not empty, a number or a date there); `[a=""]` on text (mention text, a choice,
  a date, the names point's word too) is no value, absent or empty (`sticky-note[title=""]` is the
  untitled notes, since a blank title is none; `arrow[channel=""]` a plain arrow), and elsewhere
  `""` is what it always was; `[a!=v]` is `:not([a=v])`; and any other test of an absent value is
  false. With no kind named, a test applies to the kinds that have the attribute, each reading the
  literal its own way. `=` on an object is `not_built`, and a shape's metadata (`ShapeMeta`) is
  never an attribute.
- **Members inside an attribute: `[a.b.c]`.** `AttributeTest.path` holds the identifier members
  after the attribute's name (a letter or `_`, then letters, digits, `-` and `_`; a quoted name has
  none), and the printer writes them bare, `[meta.owner=Ann i]`. Only an attribute whose schema is an
  object or any JSON has members (any other is `unknown_attribute`: "note is text, so it has no
  members"), and the test is **untyped**: an object's members are whatever the shape holds, so each
  test is typed by the JSON value found at the path, shape by shape (`PathTest`, a `.path`
  comparison). A string takes the text operators, `=` and `i`, and `~=` as a word; a number takes `=`
  and the orderings when the literal reads as a decimal number (`[a.b="30"]` is `[a.b=30]`; an
  ordering with a literal that isn't one is `invalid_value`, and the `i` flag on it
  `unsupported_operator`); a boolean takes `true` or `false`; an array takes `~=` for an item; any
  other sort of value matches nothing (`[a.b^=3]` on a number). A member that is missing, null, or
  inside something that isn't an object is no value: `[a.b]` is false, `[a.b=""]` true, and `!=`
  is the `:not` of the test, as everywhere. Typing by the schemas of a shape's types is left for
  later: it would make the vocabulary depend on the file, which today is built once from the
  registry and is `Sendable`.
- **Text as a person reads it.** A string whose schema names a media type a text format reads
  (`contentMediaType`) is tested and shown as that format makes it: mention text as plain text, each
  mention `@` and the name its target has now, or the name it holds while its target is gone, never
  the stored form with its ids. `:contains("x")` is a substring of the title or of any string in the
  attributes, as they read, in any case: a filter, not search.
- **Containment, Topology's one tree.** A space and `:inside()` are inside at any depth, through
  boards and [containers](#containers) on them alike; `>` and `:has(> …)` directly inside, a
  container's own shapes, or the shapes on an owner's board in no container (a shape in a frame on a
  subboard's board is the frame's child, not the subboard's); `:top-level` is inside nothing (on the
  top board, in no container), and `:current-board` on the board shown, in a container or not. A
  kind whose shapes hold shapes, a board of them or shapes on theirs (`containerKinds`), may stand
  where a container goes; any other is `cannot_contain`.
- **What a shape is inside, named.** A row's `inside` is the names of the shapes it's inside,
  outermost first: the boards' owners as the path over the canvas names them (the owner's title,
  else its kind's placeholder, through the board names point, else its label), and the containers
  between them by their titles, else their kinds' labels (an untitled frame is "Frame"), which the
  path doesn't name.
- **A query changes nothing**: no shape, no selection, no step of undo. It never ends typing: a
  shape being typed into reads as the board has it (a note writes each keystroke, so its text as
  typed so far), and an answer that lists it, or read its text, warns that it may still change
  (`editing`).

`run(QueryRequest(text, limit:, countOnly:, properties:, edges:, settle:))` (the last two are
[below](#many-at-once-edge-views-and-waiting)) answers a `QueryResult`: `query` (the
plan's `canonical`), `count` (every shape that matches, listed or not), `rows` (the first `limit`,
`QueryBudget.rows` (100) unless it says, at most `maxRows` (10,000), in file order; none with
`countOnly`), `warnings` (`limited`, `editing`, `no_title_match`, `pending`; `QueryWarning.Reason` is open,
and the command line adds `repaired`), `shown` and `shownPath` (the board the window showed as it
took up the file, `:current-board`'s, and the boards from the root down to it: where it ran, which
the command line's `board` says), and `timings` (thread CPU on the main actor and off it, the
slices, the longest, and the costliest record: the longest stretch between two reads of a slice's
clock, the stretch after its last read included). A `QueryRow` is the shape's `id`, `kind`,
`title` (nil for none), `board`, `inside`, `properties` (its attributes as they read: own properties
as a board writes them, added ones when set, text through its format, cut at `QueryBudget.cut` (500)
characters unless `.only([…])` names it, those cut named in `cut`; never where it is, nor its name;
none for `.none`), `connection`, for a shape that carries an edge itself in slot `""` (an arrow: the
edge's type and the shapes it runs `from` and `to`, each by id and title; and, only when an end went
through a stand-in, `via` and `more`, [below](#many-at-once-edge-views-and-waiting)), and `editing`; it
encodes itself leaving out what's absent. `titles(for:limit:)` and `whereThePersonIs(selectedLimit:)` are
what [`--ask`](#--ask) sends the model, each run as a query is.

### Where it runs

A query costs the main actor what it reads and one turn, and does everything else off it:

1. **Checked**, on the main actor (`check`): parsed and resolved against the vocabulary
   (`queries.vocabulary`, a `QueryVocabulary`, `Sendable`: each kind with its label, how its shapes
   are named, whether its shapes hold shapes (`holdsShapes`, Topology's `containerKinds`) and
   whether a board of them (`holdsBoard`), what an untitled one's board is called, and its
   attributes with what each takes; the edge types in the tree's order, with their summaries; the
   words, the language's then plugins', each with its form, what it takes, what it means and an
   example; and `text`, the `<vocabulary>` block `--ask` sends: the kinds, the edge types and the
   plugins' words, since the prompt teaches the language's own), made on the editor's first query
   and kept, since the registry never changes.
2. **Taken up**, in one main-actor turn, in O(1) (`QuerySnapshot`): the file
   (`withoutObservingDocument { editor.file }`) and Topology's snapshot in the edge view the request
   names (`topology.snapshot(request.edges)`), shared and not copied; the
   board shown and the path to it; the revision and the shape being typed into; then what each word
   and text format the query uses takes (`prepare`, in word order: the selection's ids, Mentions'
   labels), every text format's when rows list attributes.
3. **Answered off the main actor**, in a task of its own (`Evaluation`), handed the snapshot whole
   (`Handover`), so the evaluation is its last holder and it's freed there, with everything read from
   it. A set at a time: each node of the plan is worked out once into the set of shapes it matches
   among the candidates its compound has narrowed to so far, and kept for the query, so nothing
   recurses per shape; a compound's tests run cheapest first (ids, titles and seeds; kinds; the top
   board and the board shown; containment and edges; attributes and text; words asked of the main
   actor last, on what's left).
   A compound with a one-step edge word (`:edge-to`, `:edge-from`, `:connected-to`, `:starts-at`,
   `:ends-at`, `:start-of`, `:end-of`, `:between`, a plugin's relation) and fewer than
   `QueryBudget.seedFromAnchors` (1,024) anchors starts from their edges' far ends, never a walk of
   every shape: `sticky-note:edge-to(#…)` costs the anchor's degree, and `:end-of(#…)` the edges the
   anchor carries. Containment walks up from each candidate (its ancestors: those of the
   container it's in, from its record, `container(of:on:)`, else its board's, each container's and
   each board's worked out once), or, when nothing narrowed the candidates, down from the
   containers, asking only the shapes of `containerKinds` what's inside them; transitive words go
   breadth first from their anchors.
   Titles and ids are checked here, against the snapshot (`unknown_title` with the titles like it,
   and, for a title standing for an edge word's or a relation's anchor where an edge of the types it
   follows points at a shape the query can't see from a carrier it can, the `:dangling` that finds
   those carriers, of exactly those types: `:mentions("Old ledger")` hints `:dangling(mention)`;
   `unknown_id`, `cannot_contain` for a title that names only shapes of kinds that hold none). The
   rows are made here too, in file order: the walk's, when every shape was walked, else
   `fileOrderKey`'s; a count isn't put in order at all.
4. **Asked of the main actor in slices**, for what only it can say: a derived name (the names point's
   `derived`) and a word's verdict (its `onMain`). `MainFacts` asks them in slices, each a
   main-actor job of its own that lasts `QueryBudget.slice` (2 ms of the thread's CPU) and at most the
   one record that crosses it, one record at least: its clock is read after the first record, then
   every `clockStride` (16) while the pace leaves room before `everyRecordAfter` (1.5 ms), and after
   every record from then on. The evaluation asks for the next slice only once it has the last one's
   answers, so a query never has more than one waiting on the main queue, and input, drawing,
   commits and other queries' slices run between them (the main run loop services its sources
   between one job and the next).
   Each shape is asked about as the app has it when its slice runs: its id looked up in the live
   file, with the board it's on now (`QueryMainContext.shape(_:)`); one gone since, kept aside, or on
   a board the app can't show has no name and fails the word.
