5. **Written** as the wire's JSON member by member, off the main actor too, where the result is let
   go of ([query](#query)).

**At once, and bounded.** Queries on one editor run at once: each takes up the file as soon as it's
asked (`--ask`'s titles and where the person is too, and a batch) and is answered alongside the
others, a snapshot of its own for each, with no line to wait in. Each asks the main actor for one
slice at a time, so several queries' slices alternate on the main queue, with the run loop's sources
between one job and the next. A query stops when its caller's task is cancelled (`cancelled`: the
evaluation looks every `QueryBudget.cancellationStride` (256) shapes and before each slice, and
`canvas` hanging up cancels the command's task) or when `QueryBudget.deadline` (8 s, before
`canvas`'s 10 s wait runs out) has passed since it was asked, running or waiting for answers to
settle (`too_slow`: a scheduled action on `editor.scheduler`, armed before the settle wait so the
wait counts against it, cancels it, and is cancelled if the query ends first, so tests reach it by
advancing a `ManualScheduler`), either stopping that query alone, since each has its own task, its
own deadline and its own slices. Every query on an editor stops when the editor goes
(`board_closed`: `QueryState` and `MainFacts` hold the editor weakly, so a query never keeps a closed
file's editor alive).

**Zero upkeep.** `QueryState` keeps nothing per shape or per board, implements no
`documentDidChange`, and overrides `boardDidChange` with nothing: a commit, a drag event's included,
and a switch of board cost queries nothing, ever, and nothing outlives a query but the vocabulary
(`liveSnapshots`, debug builds, is 0 whenever none runs).

**What a held snapshot costs.** While a query runs, its snapshot shares the file's tables and
Topology's, so a commit that lands meanwhile copies each table it changes, once: a drag event the
file's `revisions` (and, off the root, its `children`), a shape added or removed its `locations`, a
change of edges the index's tables it touches, a rename of a mentioned shape Mentions' resolutions
(while a text format holds the labels). At most one copy per table however many snapshots are held
(copy on write: the commit's first change to a table copies it, and every snapshot taken before it
keeps the old one), so queries at once cost a commit no more than one does, and none once the
answers are made, since each snapshot is let go of then; `./build.sh bench` can't tell a commit with
a snapshot held from one without (below).

### Many at once, edge views and waiting

Three additions are for plugins that keep answers and for agents that read what a stand-in makes of
the edges ([stand-ins](#stand-ins-forwarding), Topology's). All are generic: nothing here names what stands in.

- **The edge view.** `QueryRequest.edges` (an `EdgeView`, `.resolved` unless it says: every caller
  that never said keeps reading as it did) is the view of Topology's edges the query's edge words
  see: `:edge-to`, `:connected-to`, `:downstream-of`, `:between`, `:ends-at`, `:end-of`, a relation,
  and a row's `connection`. Resolved, an arrow into a stand-in is an arrow into what it stands for;
  `.recorded` forwards only through stand-ins whose own record names what they stand for and leaves
  one that stands for what was provided at its own end, which is what a stand-in's own query reads
  (it asks what to stand for, so it can't see through itself); `.literal` is as drawn. Taking up the
  file is `topology.snapshot(request.edges)`; evaluation is unchanged, the snapshot answers in the
  view it was taken in.
- **A connection that went through a stand-in** says so. In the resolved view an arrow into a
  stand-in has one edge for each shape it stands for, and a row reads them: `from` and `to` are the
  first pair in file order (by where each starts, then where each ends), `QueryConnection.via` (a
  `QueryVia`, `{from, to}`, each only if that end was a stand-in) says which stand-in each end went
  through (`Edge.origin`), and `more` (`[QueryPair]`) holds the other pairs, in file order. Both are
  nil for a connection as drawn, so a row's JSON is what it was but for these members; `canvas
  query` writes them member by member (`QueryOutput`), a stand-in untitled, so its end is its id
  alone. An arrow into a stand-in that stands for nothing yet stays at the stand-in, as drawn.
- **A batch, ids only.** `queries.matches([QueryMatchRequest])` answers many queries
  (`text`, `edges`, `limit`, `admitting`) in one go and returns, in order, each one's
  `Result<QueryMatches, QueryError>`: `canonical`, `ids` (the admitted matches in file order, at
  most `limit`), `count` (all admitted) and `revision` (`editor.revision` as the file was taken up,
  the same for all). The file is taken up once, in one main-actor turn, with one snapshot of
  Topology in each view the requests ask for, and every request is evaluated in one evaluation that
  shares what it reads: the shapes walked, the title index, and the names, so a derived name (asked
  of the main actor in slices) is read **once per batch**, however many requests name titles. Each
  text is checked once however many requests carry it, a query asked in two views among them (debug
  builds count `checks`), over the edge types read once.
  `admitting` is asked of each match off the main actor, before `limit`: the first match is the
  first one admitted, and `count` counts those. No rows are built. A request the engine refuses
  (`check`, then the names pass) is that request's `.failure`, with the reason and message `run`
  would give (a hint that waits on titles is left as it is); a cancellation, the deadline or a
  closed file fails every request that wasn't refused. `checkNames(plan)` is the names pass alone
  (`unknown_title`, `unknown_id`, `cannot_contain`: what `run` does before it evaluates), with
  nothing evaluated and no rows, and takes up nothing for a plan that names no shape: what a plugin
  that translates English to a query checks, beside `check`, before it keeps one.
- **What a word reads** (`QueryReads`, `.file` or `.editor`) is said when it's added, and a plan
  reports it (above). `registrar.queryPseudoClass(…, reads: .file, prepare:, seeds:, matches:)` and
  `queryTextFormat(…, reads: .file, prepare:, read:)` take a `prepare` that is given a
  `QueryFilePreparation`: Topology's snapshot, whose edges are in the request's view, and the
  registry, and no editor; and no `onMain` (its context lends the editor). So the claim "this word
  reads only the file" can't be false by accident: code that reads the live editor, the selection,
  the camera, a service or Validation doesn't compile there. A word added the other way, with a
  `prepare` that takes `QueryPreparation`, reads the editor, as every word did; a relation reads the
  file. What a plugin keeps that is a function of the records alone reaches a file word through a
  **fact of the file**: a type that adopts `QueryFileFact` (`static func current(in editor:) -> Self`,
  `Sendable`, asked on the main actor in the turn the query takes up the file, O(1): a value the
  plugin keeps, shared) is read with `preparation.fact(MyFact.self)`. The word still can't reach the
  editor; the claim that the value reads only the records is made once, where the fact type is
  declared, and reviewed there. Shipped, `QueryLexicon` classifies each: `:selected`, `:invalid` and
  `:warned` read the editor, as does `:current-board` (the board shown, the language's own); Mentions'
  text format reads the file, through the fact `MentionedNames` (`MentionState.labels`: each mentioned
  shape's name, from its record), so a query that searches note text (`[text*=…]`, `:contains`)
  reads only the file and a stand-in's own query may use it. The structural words, attributes,
  kinds, titles, text and the edge words, relations included, read the file.
- **Settling.** `QueryRequest.settle` (a `Duration`, nil: don't wait) makes a query that reads edges
  wait, before it takes up the file, while `topology.isSettling` (answers a stand-in asked for are
  still arriving), at most that long (`QueryBudget.settleWait`, 2 s, what `canvas query` passes,
  `--ask`'s query too). The wait holds no snapshot, and no other query waits for it; a plan with no
  edge word never waits. It counts against `QueryBudget.deadline` (armed before the wait, so the
  evaluation has what's left), which keeps a slow query inside `canvas`'s 10 s: it's refused
  `too_slow`, with its hint, not left to the client's timeout. If the time passes with answers
  still arriving the query runs anyway and adds `QueryWarning.pending(n)` (reason `pending`; `n` the
  stand-ins asked and unanswered), saying that what it reads of edges may change. An agent that
  draws and then queries reads the settled graph, or is told it didn't.

### What plugins add

Queries knows no plugin: what shapes are called, what an untitled owner's board is called, words
beyond the language's, how text of a media type reads, and what's selected come through points
Queries declares ([QueryPoints.swift](../Sources/Queries/QueryPoints.swift)), which QueryLexicon
fills with this app's words, a plugin value for each concern it imports (QueriesTests fill them
with words of their own). Without one, a query does without:

| Point | Sugar | What a query gets | Without it | Shipped |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `QueryNames` | `registrar.queryNames(attribute:source:named:derived:fold:)` | The attribute names are tested by; per kind, whether its shapes are named, derived or neither; a named shape's name, read anywhere; a derived one's, on the main actor; how a title a query writes is folded | No titles: a title head is `no_names`, and rows have none | TitleQueriesPlugin |
| `QueryBoardNames` | `registrar.queryBoardNames(placeholder:)` | What an untitled owner's board is called, per kind | Its kind's label | BoardQueriesPlugin |
| `QueryWords` | `registrar.queryPseudoClass(_:_:example:prepare:seeds:matches:onMain:)` (reads the editor; with `reads: .file` and a file-only `prepare`, no `onMain`), `querySelection(_:_:example:selected:)`, `queryRelation(_:_:example:types:direction:)`, `queryRelation(_:_:example:reads:transitive:namesTypes:prepare:seeds:related:)` | A word: a pseudo-class, the person's selection, a relation over edges of exactly some types, or a relation answered from a fact of the file | The word is `unknown_pseudo_class` | MentionQueriesPlugin, ValidationQueriesPlugin, TypeQueriesPlugin, SelectionQueriesPlugin |
| `QueryTextFormats` | `registrar.queryTextFormat(mediaType:describes:prepare:read:)` (and with `reads: .file`) | How strings of a `contentMediaType` read, anywhere | Text read as stored | MentionQueriesPlugin |
| `QueryEngines` | none: `QueriesPlugin`'s mark, which only Queries makes | That the app answers queries (`registry.answersQueries`), for what has a registry and no editor | `canvas query` and `query-vocabulary` answer `no_queries` | QueriesPlugin |

`QueryNames` and `QueryBoardNames` take one contribution each, `QueryWords` one a word and
`QueryTextFormats` one a media type (their report lines: `query names`, `query board names`, `query
word :mentions`, `query text text/x-canvas-mentions`; `query engine` on queries'). QueryLexicon's
five registrations, whole (each plugin's words are its own nested `enum Word: String`, and
`ValidationQueriesPlugin` registers each of its two in a helper, whose `has` is below; `TypeQueriesPlugin` adds `:is-a(S)`, a transitive `namesTypes` relation over `TypeIndex.graph`, and reads a type where `is` is read as its title)
([TitleQueries.swift](../Sources/QueryLexicon/TitleQueries.swift),
[BoardQueries.swift](../Sources/QueryLexicon/BoardQueries.swift),
[MentionQueries.swift](../Sources/QueryLexicon/MentionQueries.swift),
[ValidationQueries.swift](../Sources/QueryLexicon/ValidationQueries.swift),
[SelectionQueries.swift](../Sources/QueryLexicon/SelectionQueries.swift), and [TypeQueries.swift](../Sources/QueryLexicon/TypeQueries.swift)):

```swift
// TitleQueriesPlugin: a shape is called what Titles calls it; a named title read off the record anywhere,
// a derived one on the main actor.
registrar.queryNames(attribute: TitleProperty.key.rawValue,
                     source: { kind, registry in
                         if registry.titleIsDerived(kind) { return .derived }
                         return registry.properties(for: kind).contains(TitleProperty.key) ? .named : .none
                     },
                     named: { TitleProperty.folded($0[TitleProperty.self]) },
                     derived: { record, registry in registry.title(of: record) },
                     fold: { TitleProperty.folded($0) })

// BoardQueriesPlugin: an untitled owner's board is called what the path calls it.
registrar.queryBoardNames { kind, registry in registry.boardPlaceholder(of: kind) }

// MentionQueriesPlugin: Topology's mention edges as two words, and mention text as a person reads it.
registrar.queryRelation(Word.mentions.rawValue, "its text mentions a shape S matches", example: #":mentions("Checkout")"#,
                        types: [MentionEdge.id], direction: .outgoing)
registrar.queryRelation(Word.mentionedBy.rawValue, "a shape S matches mentions it", example: #":mentioned-by("API gateway")"#,
                        types: [MentionEdge.id], direction: .incoming)
registrar.queryTextFormat(mediaType: MentionTextFormat.mediaType, describes: "mentions read as @Name", reads: .file,
                          prepare: { $0.fact(MentionedNames.self).labels },
                          read: { stored, labels in MentionText(stored: stored).plainText { labels.label(of: $0) } })
// MentionedNames: QueryFileFact, `current(in:)` is `editor.mentions?.labels`, a function of the records.

// ValidationQueriesPlugin: :invalid and :warned, which only the main actor can say.
registrar.queryPseudoClass(word.rawValue, summary, example: ":\(word.rawValue)",
                           prepare: { _ in () },
                           matches: { _, _ in .onMain },
                           onMain: { record, board, _, context in has(severity, record, on: board, context) })

// SelectionQueriesPlugin: the person's selection, as the query takes up the file.
registrar.querySelection(Word.selected.rawValue, "the person has it selected", example: ":selected") { $0.selectedShapeIDs }
```

- **An edge names its ends**, so a kind draw can't name (no naming property, no derived title) has no edges to list: `PortEdgesPlugin`'s `sides` is empty for it, though the kind has ports (`registry.drawCanName`).
- **Names are titles.** A kind's shapes are `.named` when it opts into the title Titles keeps
  (`TitleProperty`), read off the record on any thread; `.derived` when Titles works them out (no
  shipped kind's), read through `registry.title(of:)` in slices, which
  wins for a kind that's both, since Titles falls back to it for the shapes nobody named and only
  the main actor can say which; else `.none`. `source` is asked once per kind, as the vocabulary is
  made. The attribute must be a word a query writes bare (`QueryNames.check`), and `[title="X"]`
  folds its literal through `fold`, so it matches exactly what the head `"X"` does. The rule is
  `draw`'s own (DrawLexicon's [`TitleNamesPlugin`](#what-draw-takes-from-other-plugins)), so the two name shapes alike.
- **Boards are named by Boards' rule**: the owner's name, else `placeholder` for its kind (asked once
  per kind), else its label (`registry.label(of:)`). `BoardQueriesPlugin`'s is `registry.boardPlaceholder(of:)`,
  which [`editor.name(of:root:)`](#boards) reads, so a row's `inside` says what the path's crumbs say.
- **A pseudo-class** (`:invalid`) takes no argument. `prepare` runs on the main actor in the turn the
  query takes up the file, taking what it needs there, O(1) or O(what it holds) (a set of ids, a
  service's value), and what it returns (any `Sendable`) is handed as it was to the rest: `seeds`, if
  given, the only shapes that can match, which a compound then starts from; `matches`, anywhere (on
  any thread, for several queries at once), `.yes`, `.no` or `.onMain` for each shape the query
  tests (a `QueryShape`: its record, its board and the Topology snapshot); and `onMain`, in slices,
  for those `matches` leaves to the main actor, about the shape as the app has it then, with a
  `QueryMainContext` (the registry, the editor, the revision as the query started, `shape(_:)`, and
  `shapes(on:)`, a board as the app has it now, one `ShapeContext` per board per query, made again
  once that board's revision changes). A word is lowercase words joined by hyphens, and never one of
  the language's own or one it refuses as invented (`QueryWords.check`).
- **The person's selection** is a pseudo-class of one sort: `querySelection` takes the shapes
  selected, in the selection's order, as the query takes up the file (so a change of the selection
  while a query runs changes nothing it answers), seeds and matches them, and is what `--ask` tells
  the model is selected (`whereThePersonIs`), in that order. At most one plugin says what's
  selected (`QueryWords.check`).
- **A relation** (`:mentions(S)`) is `:edge-to(S, only t)` under a word of its own: `.outgoing`, the
  result has an edge of exactly one of `types` (none under them) to a shape S matches; `.incoming`,
  a shape S matches has one to the result. Its types must be ones an installed plugin declares.
  `MentionQueriesPlugin`'s follow `MentionEdge.id` alone, so a shape that mentions itself counts (Mentions'
  `isMentioned` leaves it out).
- **A relation from a fact of the file** (`queryRelation(…, reads: .file, transitive:, namesTypes:,
  prepare:, seeds:, related:)`) is for what a plugin keeps and edges don't say. `prepare` takes the
  fact (`file.fact(Facts.self)`, a `QueryFileFact`, O(1)); `related(shape, fact)` lists the shapes a
  shape is related to directly, and `seeds(fact)` every shape that has any (the only shapes that can
  match). `:word(S)` matches the shapes related to one S matches; `transitive` also those related
  through other shapes, however many. The engine reads `related` forward once per query and word,
  then works backward from the anchors, breadth first, each shape once: a cycle ends where it
  began, and a shape in one is related to itself. It reads only the file (`readsOnlyTheFile`), waits
  for answers still arriving as an edge word does (`readsEdges`: the fact may rest on edges), and
  with few anchors starts a compound as a one-step edge word does. A relation declared
  `namesTypes: true` (at most one) is the word `.Name` is refused toward: `unsupported`, hinted
  `:word("Name")` once a shape is titled so (the claim `HintPremise.Claim.typeWord`, settled with
  the titles), else the plain `:contains("Name")` hint, and a refusal that never says "class" or
  "schemas". `[class=Name]` is refused the same way.
- **A text format** makes a stored string what a person reads, anywhere (`read`), with what `prepare`
  took; `describes` says so in the vocabulary, beside the attribute (`text (mentions read as
  @Name)`). Mention text reads through [`MentionState.labels`](#the-service-mentionstate), taken as
  the query takes up the file (a fact of the file, `MentionedNames`), so a gone target reads as the
  name its mention holds.
- **Validity is Validation's cache where it's current, else its rules.** `:invalid` and `:warned`
  leave every shape to the main actor (`.onMain`). There, a shape on the board shown, with nothing
  committed since the query started (`context.revision`), takes
  [`cachedResult(for:)`](#a-horizontal-plugin) while it's `.current`; any other runs its kind's rules
  against the board it's on as the app has it (`registry.validationIssues(of:in:
  context.shapes(on: board))`), which is what Validation will find once that board is shown. A
  query never makes Validation read a board, so Validation's first read (100 ms at 10,000 shapes,
  in one turn) is never a query's.

**What a plugin list needs.** `QueriesPlugin()` needs `TopologyPlugin()` (without it, every query
is `no_topology`). Each of QueryLexicon's plugins needs `QueriesPlugin()` (a contribution to a
point whose owner isn't installed is `ownerNotInstalled`) and its own concern's plugin:
`MentionQueriesPlugin` is refused without `MentionsPlugin()`, whose `mention` edge type its words
follow, while `TitleQueriesPlugin`, `ValidationQueriesPlugin` and `SelectionQueriesPlugin` find
nothing without Titles, Validation or Selection (every kind untitled, no shape invalid, nothing
selected), as DrawLexicon's do without theirs. `QueryCommandsPlugin()` needs `AutomationPlugin()`,
and `--ask` `QueryTranslationPlugin` and `LanguageModelsPlugin` (else `no_model`). The shipped list has them after
DrawLexicon's: `QueriesPlugin(), QueryTranslationPlugin(prompt: QueryPrompt.system, referenceRule: QueryPrompt.referenceRule), TitleQueriesPlugin(), BoardQueriesPlugin(),
MentionQueriesPlugin(), ValidationQueriesPlugin(), SelectionQueriesPlugin()`, then
`QueryCommandsPlugin()`; the prompt stays in Composition, since its examples name the shipped kinds.

### What it costs

`./build.sh bench` holds queries on generated boards of 1,000 and 10,000 shapes and files of nested
boards ([QueryBenchmarks.swift](../Tests/BenchmarkTests/QueryBenchmarks.swift), members of
`extension Budget`): main-actor budgets in the test thread's CPU, off-main ones in the answer's
`timings` (or, for what they don't cover, the answer's JSON and `--ask`'s request, every other
thread's CPU while it runs, `cpu {}`), and only the frames on the wall clock. In release, 1,000 /
10,000 shapes, ms (measured again 2026-10-09, the generated board's schema cards type notes now,
longer notes that query, validation and Find read as notes):

| What | Budget | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| A query's main-actor time (`queryMain`): reading and resolving `sticky-note[text*="note" i]:not(:inside(*))` and taking up the file, also after a drag event that moved every shape | 0.2 / 0.5 | 0.067 / 0.071 |
| The vocabulary, made on an editor's first query (`queryVocabulary`) | 1 | 0.086 |
| That query off the main actor, first after the file opens, 100 rows: every shape walked, every note's attributes written and its text read with live names (`queryScan`) | 5 / 40 | 4.34 / 37.5 |
| A note by its name (`"Title 5004"`), every name read, off the main actor (`queryTitleOffMain`) | 1 / 5 | 0.57 / 3.20 |
| And on it: every derived name asked, in slices, on a board looked at (`queryTitleMain`) | 0.5 / 4 | 0.035 / 0.028, no slices: no shipped kind's names are derived |
| Notes with an edge to a subboard 100 of them mention, `:edge-to(#…)`, brief rows (`queryByID`) | 0.5 | 0.35 / 0.34 |
| And their rows with their attributes (`queryByIDRows`) | 2 | 0.52 / 0.53 |
| `:downstream-of` along a chain through every shape, and `:component-of(*)` over one component of them all (`queryGraph`) | 3 / 30 | 1.18, 1.27 / 9.42, 10.1 |
| Every construct that walks, and a nest as deep as the language allows, on a board and ten boards deep (`queryPathological`) | 25 / 250 | 3.8 / 45.7, the worst |
| `:invalid` over boards not shown, the main actor's time in all (`queryInvalidHidden`) | 15 / 150 | 8.48 in 5 slices / 88.1 in 44 (a type's schema checked too) |
| A slice: 2 ms and the record that crosses it, the longest of any query here (`querySlice`) | 3 | 2.068; the costliest record 0.400 |
| `* --limit 10000` off the main actor: the rows and their JSON, let go of there (`queryRows`) | 15 / 150 | 3.5 / 45.7 |
| That command's main time (`queryRowsMain`: `queryMain` and `queryTitleMain`) | 0.7 / 4.5 | 0.071 / 0.174 |
| Its main time beyond its query's own, making and letting go of the answer (`queryMain`) | 0.2 / 0.5 | 0.063 / 0.141 |
| A commit adding a note while a query holds the file, more than without (`queryHeldCommit`) | 0.1 / 0.5 | none: 0.049 held, 0.064 not / 0.265, 0.412 |
| A drag event's input with the shipped list and a query run first, more than without queries (`queryUpkeep`) | 0.01 | none: 0.0432 with, 0.0431 without / 0.2900, 0.2905 |
| A drag's frames at 60 Hz while `:invalid`'s slices run, the worst (`queryFrame`, wall clock) | 16 | 10.8 / 10.6, none dropped |
| `--ask`'s request without the model, on a board looked at: main (`askAssemblyMain`) | 1 / 5 | 0.105 / 0.115 |
| And off it (`askAssemblyOffMain`) | 3 / 10 | 0.587 / 4.74 |

- **No type is cold.** Types' index reads every type of a file as it opens, and every
  type as it changes, on any board, and a query reads only what's stored, never a type's schema. On a board never shown, as the file
  opens, `queryTitleMain` measures 0.024 / 0.027.
- **Rows of derived kinds cost the main actor their names.** 10,000 rows of the generated board
  hold none today (no shipped kind derives its title; its type notes are named), so the command is held to `queryMain`
  and `queryTitleMain` together, and what it costs beyond its query's own to `queryMain`: the answer
  is made and let go of off the main actor.
- **Mention text is read twice.** Mentions' text format parses each note's stored text again
  (`MentionText(stored:)`, some 6 µs a note) though the record holds it parsed: about half of a full
  row of a mentioning note, most of `queryScan`, and why full rows of 100 notes are held to 2 ms, not
  `queryByID`'s 0.5 ([Not built yet](#not-built-yet)).
- **Frames** are driven by a strict main-queue dispatch timer (`FrameDriver`), each timed from the
  first fire it answers, so a dropped frame counts as late: a run-loop `Timer` in a windowless
  process fires up to 7 ms late on its own. While slices run a frame starts at most one slice late
  (1.9 ms; 0.1 without), and the worst without queries is 9.0 / 9.3.
- **A held snapshot's copy** (the file's `locations`, some 10,000 entries at 10,000 shapes) is lost
  in a commit's own 0.36 ms; debug builds check that the query holds the file at the commit, so the
  case is real.

**No index, on purpose.** An index would cost every commit, a drag event's included (whose input is
held to 1 ms at 10,000 shapes), and a copy of what it indexes kept in step. What it would save is
small and off the main actor: walking every shape and filtering by kind is some 0.5 ms at 10,000;
named titles are a read per titled shape; derived ones their owners keep; edges and containment are
Topology's already. Attributes are written as JSON only for the candidates a test reaches, and text
read only for those a text test reaches. Should a budget miss on queries asked again and again, the
next step is a warm cache ([Not built yet](#not-built-yet)).

### What it doesn't do

- **Where shapes are.** Positions, sizes and overlaps aren't in the language (`:near`, `:left-of`,
  `:within`, and attributes that hold a place, are `not_built`), and inside is containment's (boards
  and containers on them): what's drawn within a shape's bounds isn't inside it unless it's in it
  (`cannot_contain`, for a container side that can only be kinds whose shapes hold no shapes).
- **`.Task` as a selector** (`unsupported`: a type is found by  the word a plugin gives it)  and `=` on
  a whole object (`[a.b]` tests a member).
- **Edges as answers.** A query lists shapes: a connection is asked for as its arrow
  (`arrow:starts-at("A"):ends-at("B")`, whose row's `connection` says where it runs), the shapes it
  runs from and to as `:start-of(arrow…)` and `:end-of(arrow…)` (the source and the target of each
  edge in slot `""` that a shape the anchor matches carries, of the types given, and only a shape the
  query ranges over: a mention's carrier, whose edges are in its text's slot, has none), and a
  mention as the shape whose text holds it.
- **Ranking and meaning.** `:contains` is a substring filter; ranked or semantic search would be a
  horizontal of its own.
- **CSS with no meaning here.** Shapes have no siblings, order or columns (`+`, `~`, `:nth-child`,
  `||`), no pseudo-elements, and a query sees no pointer (`:hover`): each is `unsupported`, never read
  some other way.
- **Acting on what it found.** A query selects, reveals and changes nothing. Its rows' ids name the
  shapes in a later query (`#…`), never in a `draw` script, which names shapes by title.

### Testing queries

- **QueryLanguageTests** hold the language on fixture words only (card, box, disc; rank, status,
  due; wire, hot-wire, pipe; the unknown words glows and stacked): trees and spans, the canonical
  form (a fixed point), every refusal (reason, message, hint, offset, length, line, column), the
  limits at their edges, the words and the inventions, and seeded fuzz: trees generated from the
  grammar round-trip, and random edits never crash, reprint as their canonical form when they parse,
  and keep every span inside the text.
- **QueriesTests** hold the engine over fixtures only: CanvasTesting's `Chore` (`ChoresPlugin`: kind
  `chore`, labelled "Task", holding every schema type, and the added `Flagged`, key `flag`), with
  pockets, tiles and links graded as wires; a `caption` names point, board names, words (`:starred`,
  seeded; `:heavy`, off the main actor, counted by `Tally`; `:audited`, asked on it, counted by
  `MainCalls`; `:wired-to(S)`, a relation) and a text format (`text/x-shout`), all in
  `queryPlugins`; `shelf()` and `hiddenShelf()` (a kept-aside owner, a board the app can't show);
  `yard()` (CanvasTesting's corrals, captioned, nested on the top board and on a pocket's board, one
  holding a pocket: every containment construct through them, from either side, file order, rows'
  `inside`, hints and `holdsShapes`);
  `choresHarness` (every schema type, every operator); `storyHarness` (the design's table of every
  construct, on fixtures: `citesPlugin`'s edges from chores' tags, `pickedPlugin`'s selection,
  `faultyPlugin`'s verdicts); and `wiresHarness` and `danglingHarness` (edges). `answer`, `matched`,
  `refusedAnswer` and `expectMatches` run queries through `awaitResult`, which turns the main run loop
  for the slices, and `plan(_:on:)` reads a plan (`description`, a tree).
- **Stand-ins, batches, reads and settling** are held on fixture stand-ins (StandIns.swift: a `Proxy`
  for the shapes its record cites, a `Lens` for what was provided, `relay()`, wires into them; Topology
  tests have their own): `edgeViewTests` (the three views on the same arrows, standing edges, a
  stand-in with nothing to stand for), `connectionViaTests` (`via` and `more`, in file order, per
  view), `matchesBatchTests` (one capture for all, no rows built, admission before the limit and off the
  main actor, the revision stamp, a refusal that is one request's, names read once for the batch
  by `derivedTitlesAsked`, each text checked once by `checks`, a view per request, cancellation, no
  waiting for a query before it), `checkNamesTests` (as `run`
  refuses, nothing evaluated, nothing taken up for a plan that names nothing), `readsTests`
  (`fileReadsPlugin`: a `reads: .file` word and text format given the snapshot and registry; `editorWords`
  in order and without repeats; `readsEdges`) and `settleTests` (a wait that ends on settling, one that
  ends on the time and warns `pending`, no wait for a plan with no edge word or no `settle`, the wait
  holding up no other query, cancelled waiting, the wait counting against the deadline), with `Working` as a source of busy work. QueryCommandsTests
  write a connection through a stand-in, and wait for answers on a `ManualScheduler`; CompositionTests'
  QueryShippedTests pin each shipped word's reads; BenchmarkTests' `referenceBatch`.
- **What runs where** is held by `QueryState`'s debug counters (`liveSnapshots`, `captures`, `checks`,
  `mainSlices`, `recordsEncoded`, `derivedTitlesAsked`, `verdictsAsked`, `universeWalks`,
  `seededFromAnchors`) and `threadsPlugin` (a name, a text format's `read` and a word's `matches`,
  each off the main thread). `SlowWord`, with `burn(_:)`, makes records cost what a test says: a
  slice's bound with a costly record, the costliest record's stretch after the last read, one slice
  queued at a time, a run-loop `Timer` firing between slices (the run loop's sources run between
  them, not only queue order), cancellation mid-slice, the deadline reached by `h.wait(8_000)` inside a
  slice on the `ManualScheduler`, queries at once (a quick query, and a batch, taking up the file and
  answering while a slow one is mid-slices, each over a snapshot of its own, `liveSnapshots` 2 while both
  are held; a cancelled one, or one out of time, stopping alone), and a closed file (an editor held only in
  a box a word empties). A word whose `prepare` commits lands a commit in the turn the query takes
  up the file: attributes are the capture's, a derived name the live record's. UpkeepTests hold zero
  upkeep.
- **QueryLexicon's tests** use fixtures only, through `EditorHarness` and `QueryState`: TitleQueriesTests
  CanvasTesting's kinds titled as TitleNamesTests title them (derived names asked on the main actor,
  and read live after a commit lands); BoardQueriesTests a `drawer`, which opens its board with a
  placeholder, and a `crate`, which doesn't and is called by its label, and titled corrals between
  them, which a row names and the path doesn't; MentionQueriesTests a `scribble` of mention text,
  titled pockets to mention, and a `strand` edge type its words ignore;
  ValidationQueriesTests card and tag rules that count their runs (the board shown answered from the
  cache, another board by its own rules in slices, and never Validation made to read a board); and
  SelectionQueriesTests a `:shifting` word that changes the selection mid-query. BoardQueriesTests and
  MentionQueriesTests name shapes with a names contribution of their own over `TitleProperty`, since
  they have no `TitleQueriesPlugin`.
- **QueryTranslationTests** hold the translator on fixture chores and a `ScriptedLanguageModel`: how
  an answer is read (`AskAnswer.parse`, ParseTests), what it answers and asked, each failure's reason
  and message (`QueryTranslationError`), no model or no queries, and the deadline in a model call;
  and `translate` (TranslateTests): the canonical query returned and nothing run, a wrong title and a
  word that reads the editor each repaired once (and refused twice an unusable answer), the 40 s mark,
  the 55 s deadline, a cancelled task, and the `.reference` request (no selection, no word that reads
  the editor, the rule line) against the `.person` one.
- **QueryCommandsTests** run `query`, `query-vocabulary` and `--ask` as the server does (`start`,
  `finish`, `run`, `answered`, `refused`) over chores, pockets and links, captions naming them,
  "Untitled Pocket" boards, and a `Desk`: `:picked`, the selection word, and `:slow`, asked on the
  main actor; with a `ScriptedLanguageModel` (`queue`, `holdsAnswers`, `requests`). The deadline and
  the repair mark are reached with `h.wait(…)` on the `ManualScheduler` (from inside `:slow` for a
  query run, from `onPicked` for the request's assembly), and `QueryOutput.lastBuiltOnMainThread`
  (debug builds) says where an answer was built.
- **CompositionTests** hold the shipped pieces on the story file, `QueryStory`: the design's "Roadmap"
  (a Payments subboard holding a Refunds one, notes that mention each other and a shape that's gone,
  arrows on a channel and on none, and types, one of them invalid), its ids
  `00000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000000NN` named by letter (`ids("C, Y")`), `fileOrder`, `file(in:)`,
  `harness(pasteboard:model:)` and `document(windowed:)`. Its untitled, invalid type V holds
  `{"type": "object" "title": "Invoice"}`, a comma left out (a type's name is its title, never
  its schema's, so V stays untitled); a type's last reading as an object is
  kept by id for the whole process, so a test that mends V's JSON changes what its highlights
  read in every story after it: mend a copy. QueryShippedTests run the design's table of every construct row for row
  (`StoryQuery.table`: shapes in file order, the count, the canonical form, each refusal's reason);
  QueryCommandLineTests run `canvas` as built against `CommandServer` on the story open in a
  `BoardDocument` (`configureQueryBoards(pasteboard:model:)`, `startQueryServer(for:)`, which holds the
  board weakly so a closed file's editor can be seen to go, and `RunningCanvas`, a `canvas` left
  running, a held `--ask`, while the test does something else: a `draw` answered meanwhile, a
  `--timeout` that lets go of the model's call, a file closed under it answered `board_closed` at
  once); BoardsTests `:current-board` across a switch (no change set worked out, no snapshot left);
  and SkillTests every `query` and `query-error` block ([Testing plugins](#testing-plugins)).
- **The prompt.** QueryPromptTests hold `QueryPrompt.system` to the language: each of its
  `runnableExamples` answered on the story, each of its `illustrativeExamples` refused there with its
  reason, every query written after "→" listed, nothing that reads as a query left out of the lists,
  every `:word` the language's, a shipped plugin's or one the prompt says not to invent, the kinds,
  edge types and words it assumes the shipped vocabulary's, in its order, and the skill's
  `query-prompt.md` equal byte for byte; so a prompt change lists each new query-like example in one
  of the two lists. "Query eval board" holds `QueryEvalBoard` (59 shapes on six boards: look-alike
  titles, plain arrows, note and schema links, a mention two boards away) to what it's built with,
  and "Query prompt, live" checks each case of `scripts/query-prompts/cases.tsv` offline, its
  reference query finding exactly the shapes it expects; with `QUERY_LIVE=1` it asks the model
  ([`--ask`](#--ask)).
- **BenchmarkTests' Query benchmarks** are above; `cpu {}` sums a command's main-actor jobs without
  polling the run loop, and `FrameDriver` drives frames on a strict dispatch timer.

## Boards

A file holds a tree of boards: the root, and one for each shape of a kind that owns one (the core's
`BoardOwning`; [Boards in a file](#boards-in-a-file)). Boards
([`Sources/Boards`](../Sources/Boards)) is the horizontal that gets you around them, whatever kind
owns them. It builds on Selection (opening), ContextMenus (Open), DetailPanel (the Open button),
Keyboard (⌘↑), Titles (what a board is called) and TableOfContents (the rows a crumb's menu lists),
and none of them learns what a board is.

A board-owning kind opts in with one line, on its own registrar
([OpensBoard.swift](../Sources/Boards/OpensBoard.swift)):

```swift
registrar.shape(SubboardDefinition()) { sub in                 // SubboardDefinition: BoardOwning
    sub.title(pill: false)                                        // Titles names its board
    sub.opensBoard(placeholder: "Untitled Subboard", systemImage: "rectangle.stack")
}
```

or, for another plugin's kind, `registrar.opensBoard(Pocket.self, placeholder:systemImage:)`. The sugar
contributes to Boards' `BoardKinds` point (at most one per kind; its report line reads
`board → subboard "Untitled Subboard"`) and brings, in the same call:

- **Opening**: Selection's `opens("Open")`, which shows the shape's board
  (`editor.showBoard(BoardID(owner:))`), so a double-click, Return, Enter, ⌘↓ and Go › Open Selection all
  enter it ([opening a shape](#selection)), and so does its row in the table of contents: Return
  once the row is picked (in the app's panel, the canvas's Return, since picking a row shows the
  shape's panel and gives the canvas the keyboard), and a double-click only where the list stays
  put, not in the app's panel ([opening a row](#the-table-of-contents)).
- **Open** first in its context menu (`BoardsMenuGroup`, order 0, as Finder's Open is). With several
  selected it opens the first, in selection order.
- **A Board tab** in its panel (`BoardTab`, order 50, a horizontal's feature tab) with an Open button,
  `DetailCommandButton("Open", …, command: .openSelection)`, in a section `enabledWhileReadOnly()`,
  so a locked shape's is enabled too.

`BoardKinds.check` refuses a kind whose definition isn't `BoardOwning` (the form for another plugin's kind can't say so
in its types), and a contribution for every kind: only a kind that owns boards has one to open. So
a plugin list with `opensBoard` in it needs Selection, ContextMenus and DetailPanel installed, as a
list with a mentionable kind needs DetailPanel, for its Mentioned In tab.

`BoardsPlugin` itself ([Boards.swift](../Sources/Boards/Boards.swift)) is small:

```swift
registrar.service { BoardCrumbs(editor: $0) }                   // the path, kept for BoardPath
registrar.command(.enclosingBoard, shortcuts: [KeyChord(KeyChord.upArrow.key, .command)],
                  isEnabled: { !$0.board.isRoot && $0.session == nil && $0.editingShapeID == nil }) { $0.goToEnclosingBoard() }
```

- **Going up.** ⌘↑ (and Go › Enclosing Board) runs `editor.goToEnclosingBoard()`:
  the board above, with the shape whose board it left selected there. It's
  `editor.goUp(to: board)` for the parent: any board above the one shown (on `boardPath`), with the
  owner of the board below it on the path selected, as one step back
  (`showBoard(_:selecting:)`), so ⌘[ comes back down. Off the root only, never mid-press, and not
  while a shape is being edited, where ⌘↑ is the text's; on the root its key passes.
- **Names.** `editor.name(of: board, root:)` is what a board is called: its owner's title (Titles;
  a blank one is none), else its kind's placeholder, else its kind's label (`registry.label(of:)`);
  `root` for the root (the file's name). `editor.symbol(of:)` is its kind's symbol (`opensBoard`'s,
  else its label's), nil for the root. Composition's table-of-contents
  heading and the path both read them. `registry.boardPlaceholder(of: kind)` is the placeholder a
  kind opens its boards with (nil for a kind that doesn't), the registry's alone, which both read,
  and so does a [query](#queries): its rows name the boards a shape is inside by the same rule,
  through QueryLexicon's `BoardQueriesPlugin` (BoardsTests' "A board's placeholder" holds it).
- **In the app** (Composition and the app's window): the table of contents' header names the
  board shown, with its symbol and a way up (`ShippedPlugins.contentsHeading(for:rootName:)`, the
  board shown's crumb as a `ContentsHeading` with `up: .enclosingBoard`, called Enclosing Board as
  the Go menu calls it, its tooltip "Enclosing Board (⌘↑)", from Keyboard's
  `registry.help(_:forCommand:)`; on the root the file's name, `detailPanel`'s `rootName`, as the
  window and the path's root crumb have it, else "Board"); the window's subtitle names the board
  shown, nothing on the root, where the title is the file's name (`BoardConfiguration.boardName`,
  which the app fills with `ShippedPlugins.boardName(of:)`, the last crumb's title, and the window
  controller reads observed, so it follows a switch or a rename);
  the path is over the canvas (`ShippedPlugins.boardPath(editor:rootName:)`, the root's crumb the
  file's display name, `BoardViewState.fileName`); and the Go menu has Back (⌘[), Enclosing Board
  (⌘↑) and Open Selection (⌘↓), sent to the board's window controller wherever the keyboard is, and dimmed
  while text has it, where the menu bar leaves those keys to the text (`MenuBar`: AppKit's menus
  take a disabled item's key and beep), so they move its caret. Jump To… (⌘K), JumpTo's, will follow
  them after a separator (the command `.jumpTo` is named; nothing claims it yet). The file opens on the board left
  open, with each board's camera as it was left (`BoardViewMemory`; below).

### The path

`BoardPath(editor:rootName:)` is where you are, as data-canvas shows it: a small capsule of
crumbs over the top middle of the canvas, root first, the board shown last, in a material pill 8
points below the canvas's top edge (`BoardsStyle`). The host places it over the whole canvas, with
`.overlay(alignment: .top)`, so a crumb's menu can stay inside it; only the pill and the menu take
clicks. It shows nothing on the root. `BoardPath.coveredHeight(on:)` is how far down it reaches on
a board (to the pill's bottom, about 35 points; none on the root), which the app tells the editor
(`BoardConfiguration.coveredTop`, the editor's `coveredTop`), so a board's first visit, Zoom to
Fit and `reveal` fit shapes below it, where their titles' pills aren't under it.

```
        ╭────────────────────────────────────────────╮
        │  Plans  ›  …  ›  Kitchen 🔒 ›  **Pantry**  │
        ╰────────────────────────────────────────────╯
                           ┌──────────────────────────┐
                           │ › ▤ Groceries            │  the pointer on Kitchen: its rows
                           │   ▤ Spices               │
                           │   ▭ Pantry               │  the way you came, highlighted
                           │   ▭ Fridge               │
                           └──────────────────────────┘
```

- The root's crumb is `rootName` ("Board" when that's empty); the others are `name(of:)`. The
  board shown is bold and isn't a button. Each crumb is at most 180 points wide, truncated past it,
  with its name as its tooltip. The crumbs are separated by ›s, and nothing else marks them but the
  lock below (no caret for a crumb's menu, below: the owner found ⌄s beside the ›s busy).
- **A lock marks where the path turns read-only.** Each crumb says whether its board is read-only
  (`BoardCrumb.isReadOnly`: a [locked](#locking) subboard's board, and every board under it; the
  root's never is; from where the path turns read-only, `editor.readOnlyStart`, which the editor
  works out in one climb, as asking each board would cost the path's depth squared), and the path draws a small lock
  (`BoardsStyle.readOnlySymbol`, `lock.fill`, in the secondary color, 3 points after the name,
  "Read-only" as its tooltip and to assistive apps) after the name of the first crumb whose board is
  (`BoardCrumbs.readOnlyStart`), once: the boards below it are read-only too, and the lock above
  says it of them all, so none shows another. It's part of the crumb (a long name is cut short
  before it, and a click on it goes up, as the name's does). Folded into "…", it's the lock on that
  crumb's item in the menu, ahead of its name (an item's attributed title with the symbol after the
  name would put the symbol into its `title`), and a crumb below the fold has none: the menu never
  marks a crumb the first read-only one isn't.
- More than four crumbs fold the middle into "…", a menu of the boards it hides, root side first:
  root › … › parent › current (`BoardCrumbs.layout(rootName:)`). "…" is a button built as a board
  above's crumb is (borderless, in its gray and the pill's type), which shows an `NSMenu` of them
  lined up with its leading edge, starting at the pill's bottom edge, where a crumb's menu starts
  (AppKit puts a menu's first item where it's popped up, and its own padding above that, so it's
  popped up `BoardsStyle.systemMenuTopPadding` lower); `BoardPath.foldedMenu(_:editor:)` makes that
  menu, so a test reads and chooses its items without showing it (shown, it's modal). A SwiftUI
  `Menu` draws as a pop-up button, which takes no style from around it and draws without the pill's
  vibrancy: its "…" was darker than the crumbs on a light pill and near white on a dark one. To
  assistive apps "…" is a pop-up button, "Boards between", whose press shows the menu and whose
  children are its boards, each a button going up to its board: an `accessibilityRepresentation`,
  a `Menu` with a primary action (a representation without one does nothing when pressed).
- A crumb, or an item of "…", runs `goUp(to:)`: it shows that board and selects there the shape the
  path came through, as data-canvas's crumbs do, one step back.
- **It redraws only when the path does.** The view reads only `BoardCrumbs.crumbs`, which the
  service makes again when another board is shown, and when a commit changes a board above the one
  shown (they hold the owners whose titles name the crumbs, and whose locks make boards read-only: a
  file put in place, a lock landing in a commit on one of them), checking each one's revision, so a
  commit on the board shown (a drag's every event) costs a look at the path's revisions and redraws
  nothing. A crumb's title, or whether its board is read-only, changing is the path changing.

#### A crumb's menu

Every crumb has a menu, as data-canvas's do, though unmarked (data-canvas puts a caret after the
title): the pointer on the crumb shows the menu below it, lined up with it. It lists what's in that crumb's board, as the table of
contents lists it (Boards builds on TableOfContents for it: `ContentsOutline`,
[below](#another-boards-outline)), with the shape whose board is next on the path highlighted: the
way you came. The board shown's crumb lists its own shapes. So from inside a subboard you can jump
into another, or to any shape on any board on the way here, without going up and hunting for it
on the canvas. (data-canvas's crumbs listed their boards' subboards this way at first, and later
the board above instead, VS Code's siblings; the owner chose what's in the crumb's board.)

- **What it lists** is `BoardCrumbs.menu(of: board)`, a `CrumbMenu`: the board listed (the
  crumb's) and the shape highlighted there, nil on the board shown's; the menu is nil for the board
  shown while it has no shapes (kept as commits change it, `shownIsEmpty`, so the path never reads
  the document), and without the table of contents, whose rows a menu shows. The rows are the table of contents' with nothing selected, each as its kind draws
  it, nested rows behind a disclosure triangle, a subboard's its board's rows, so a menu reaches
  any shape below its board too.
- **Picking a row** closes the menu, then follows its shape, `editor.follow(id)`: into it if its
  kind opens its board (`opensBoard`: `editor.goInto`, as following a mention of a subboard does),
  and else to it, shown selected on its board (`editor.goTo`). Either is one step back, so ⌘[
  returns. `follow` is Boards' rule for picking a shape from anywhere in the file, written once:
  the crumbs' menus and Jump To's palette both call it. The highlighted
  row goes back into the board it's the way to, and a row of the board shown's own menu selects
  its shape there.
- **Hover intent**, data-canvas's timers (through `editor.scheduler`, so a test's clock drives
  them): the menu shows once the pointer has stayed on the crumb 150 ms, so a crumb passed over
  shows nothing, and closes 150 ms after the pointer has left it and its crumb, unless it's back on
  one of them by then. Another crumb's menu takes its place once the pointer has stayed on that
  crumb. A click on a crumb closes its menu (the board shown's goes nowhere else), and so does
  another board shown. One menu shows at a time: `BoardCrumbs.openMenu`, which the view drives with
  `pointerEntered(crumb:)`, `pointerExited(crumb:)`, `pointerEnteredMenu()`,
  `pointerExitedMenu()`, `closeMenu()` and `pick(_:)`, and a test headlessly.
- **The panel** is 300 points wide, as tall as its rows up to 360 before it scrolls, 6 points below
  the crumb, on a thick material with data-canvas's shadow, and kept 8 points inside the canvas
  (moved left, and shorter, where the canvas is small). data-canvas's is as wide as its rows,
  from 260 to 380; a lazy list can't measure the rows it hasn't made, so here the width is fixed.
  It opens at the top of its rows. A menu showing or closing redraws only the menu (`CrumbMenuLayer` reads `openMenu`, the pill
  never does), and the menu reads its board's rows, as they are while it shows.
- **The canvas under it.** Where the pill or a menu is over the canvas, the pointer isn't on the
  canvas: `CanvasView` asks the window what's at the pointer, and a view the host put over it has
  it, as the minimap does (the tool hears the pointer leave, so nothing under the path is hovered).

### Subboards

Subboards ([`Sources/Subboards`](../Sources/Subboards)) is the vertical with a board inside: the
`subboard` kind, a card that opens onto a board of its own. It's a whole kind in a handful of lines,
because everything it does is a horizontal's
([Subboards.swift](../Sources/Subboards/Subboards.swift)):

```swift
registrar.shape(SubboardDefinition()) { sub in                     // SubboardDefinition: BoardOwning
    let place = sub.placement(size: Subboard.defaultSize) { Subboard() }
    sub.tool(label: "Subboard", systemImage: "rectangle.stack", shortcut: "b", placing: place)
    sub.tint(SubboardStyle.border)                                  // the card's indigo, wherever it's listed by its kind
    sub.title(symbolInPill: true)                                   // Titles keeps its name, in a pill after the symbol
    sub.opensBoard(placeholder: "Untitled Subboard", systemImage: "rectangle.stack")
    sub.mentionable(following: .opens)                              // Mentions: by its title; followed, it's entered
    sub.contentsRow { _ in                                          // in the card's indigo, as its mentions are
        ContentsLabel("", placeholder: "Untitled Subboard", systemImage: "rectangle.stack", color: Color(nsColor: SubboardStyle.border))
    }
    sub.details(header: { $sub in TitleHeader($sub, placeholder: "Untitled Subboard", systemImage: "rectangle.stack") }) {}
    sub.subboardLinks()                                             // Connections: ports on its own channel, then on every other
}
registrar.channel(SubboardLink.self)                                // which this plugin declares
```

(The row and the header are in files of their own, `SubboardRow.swift` and `SubboardHeader.swift`,
as SwiftUI sugar is, and the channel and the ports in `SubboardLinks.swift`.)

- **Its props are its frame**, 240 × 160 placed: `Properties<Subboard>(title: "Subboard") {
  Property("frame", \.frame).required() }`. What it's called is the title Titles adds (`title`,
  marked `x-canvas-owner` in its schema), and its board is the core's, kept under its id, so its
  props hold neither; its schema is marked `x-canvas-board`. Placing one keeps no board: a board
  with no shapes isn't kept.
- **B places one** where the canvas is pressed, following the pointer until release, as every box
  tool does: one undo step, "Add Subboard".
- **The card** (`SubboardDefinition.render`, `SubboardStyle`, world units) is the whole frame, and
  its extent is its box: a card with a 10-point radius, the canvas's shadow and a 1.5-point indigo
  border (`NSColor.systemIndigo`). Its
  colors follow the appearance it's drawn in, each a dynamic `NSColor` resolved in the render: a
  faint indigo over white on the light canvas, a raised indigo-gray on the dark one, since a
  subboard is a place on the canvas, not a sheet of paper as a note is. Its title is Titles' pill
  above it, after the `rectangle.stack` symbol (`symbolInPill: true`), as every
  titled shape's is; an untitled one has none. The card shows what its board holds: its preview,
  the core's rough picture of the board (`context.drawBoardPreview(ofBoardOwnedBy:in:maxScale:)`,
  fitted 12 points inside the card at no more than a tenth of its size,
  `SubboardStyle.previewMaxScale`, so a board of one note shows a small note in the middle and one
  of hundreds fills the card; every shape a silhouette in one muted gray, as the minimap draws, a
  subboard inside just its rectangle); until that's built, a few frames, how many shapes, from
  `context.shapeCount(inBoardOwnedBy:)`: "1 shape", "12 shapes" (the shapes on its own board, not
  those further down); and for an empty board the kind's symbol over "Empty", the caption alone
  where there's no room for both. The symbol isn't drawn over a count, so a card about to show its
  preview doesn't flash it. The count is read as the card is drawn, and a preview is of one
  revision of its board, so neither is ever stale: a write to the board while another is shown
  (`transact(on:)`) redraws the canvas as any commit does.
- **Its outline** (the selection's, a hover's, the hint) is the core's, the card's rounded edge
  (`indicatorPath`) [stood off it](#outlines) like every closed shape's: the core strokes every
  outline a constant 1.5 view points wide in the accent color (2.5 and fainter for a hover), and
  drawn on the edge that line would cover the card's indigo border, which it's close to in hue and
  width, so a selected card would barely read as selected; stood off 4 view points, its corners
  growing with it (at 100%, a 14-point radius round the card's 10), a gap of the canvas lies between
  the border and the line. The card does nothing for it: the kind says only its edge. Validation's
  ring, [Validation](#a-horizontal-plugin), stands 3 view points past the outline, and the title's
  pill, 9 points above the top edge, stays clear of both.
- **Zoomed out** the card is its [skeleton](#skeletons) ([SubboardSkeleton.swift](../Sources/Subboards/SubboardSkeleton.swift)):
  fills alone, square (its corners are 3.5 points on screen at most there, so its outline is its
  frame's, as the core draws every rect's: a ring filled on the edge, over the half-point border it
  covers, so a selected card shows there as the accent color three times as wide in place of the
  indigo; no outline stands off zoomed out as it does in full, since stroking each subboard in view,
  which is what a standoff would be, costs far more than the ring, and ⌘A zoomed out outlines every
  one of them),
  with no shadow, symbol or count: its border's indigo, never under
  half a view point (just under 35% the card's own 1.5 is about that, so nothing jumps), the card
  inside it, and its board's preview, asked for as the full card asks for it, in the same rect at
  no more than a tenth of its board, drawn once it's built and big enough on screen, else nothing.
  Two fills and the preview; its title is Titles' [cover](#a-cover-zoomed-out), over it, as there's no pill zoomed out.
- **Opening it** is Boards': a double-click, Return, Enter or ⌘↓ with it the only one selected, Open
  first in its menu, the Open button in its panel's Board tab, and Return once its row is picked (a
  double-click on the row only where the list stays put, not in the app's panel). ⌘↑ comes back with it selected, and ⌘[ retraces. Its panel's header renames it, a run of
  typing one undo step; its row is its symbol and its title, or "Untitled Subboard".
- **Mentioning it** is Mentions': a note's `@` picker offers it by its title, or "Untitled
  Subboard", with its symbol, and a double-click on its pill (or Go to) enters it
  (`following: .opens`, Selection's `goInto`), from its board or another, one step back.
- **Connecting it** is Connections' ([Ports](#ports)): ports on all four sides, on a channel of its
  own, `subboard-link` (`SubboardLink`, its border's indigo), and then on every channel there is
  (`ports(SubboardLink.self)`, then `portsOnEveryChannel()`), so anything that has ports connects
  to a subboard and a subboard to anything that has them: a note on its own
  channel, either way round, and two subboards on `subboard-link`. A dot is its first channel's
  color, and a drag is drawn on the first of its channels the shape it ends on takes, so a
  subboard's dots are indigo, a drag to another subboard is a `subboard-link` and one to a note or
  a card is theirs. An arrow keeps its channel, so a note's link to a subboard can be re-aimed onto
  notes and subboards only, and a subboard's to another onto subboards only. The top dot is in the
  row its title's pill is in, as a note's and a card's are. A pill that stands for one has the same
  dots and links ([Ports at a stand-in](#ports-at-a-stand-in)). Frames have no ports, so an edge
  between a subboard and a frame, in `canvas draw`, says `channel: none`.
- **Deleting it** deletes its board and every board under it, as one step, like any shape's;
  undoing it brings them all back with every id.
- **Locking it** ([Locking](#locking)) locks what's on its board, at any depth: the core makes a board
  whose owner is read-only read-only itself, and so every board under it, a subboard on it included,
  locked or not. Its card is entered as ever, the card's own lock chip is the card's, and on the
  board no shape changes (each try shakes it) and nothing goes on it; the toolbar dims the tools that
  place shapes, Paste is off, no port dots show, and [the path](#the-path) puts a lock after the
  crumb where it starts. Unlocking it frees every board under it.
- **Turning a frame into one** is Transform's ([Transform](#transform)): Subboards takes the container
  channel after its shape block, `registrar.turnable(into: Subboard.self, through: ContainerChannel.self) { … }`,
  which brings Turn into Subboard to the menu of a shape that holds shapes, and `/turn-into-subboard`. The
  subboard keeps the frame's id and title, sits at its corner at 240 × 160, and holds on its board what the
  frame held.

It ships after the sticky note (the toolbar's Subboard, B), with Boards after Titles, and its props
have a fixture (`Fixtures/kinds/subboard.v0.json`) as every shipped kind's do; a whole file of
boards nested two deep, with notes and a bound arrow on each, is
`Fixtures/files/nested-arrows-mention.v4.json`, read and written back byte for byte (written once
notes' and arrows' text could hold mentions, though none says anything that mentions);
`nested-mentions.v4.json` is the same file from before arrows' text could, and `nested.v4.json` from
before sticky notes' could, each read with each board's notes and arrows brought up to date; and
`nested-arrows-mention-across.v4.json` is the same file with a note on the root and one two boards
down mentioning each other (`nested-mentions-across.v4.json` from before arrows', brought up to date),
read, shown live opened on either board, and written back byte for byte
([Mentions across boards](#mentions-across-boards)).

### The core's part: board previews

A shape that owns a board can show what's on it: `context.drawBoardPreview(ofBoardOwnedBy: id, in:
rect, maxScale:)`, in its render, draws a rough picture of that board into `rect` (world units),
fitted (the board's proportions kept, centered, and no larger than `maxScale` times its own size, if
given: a board of little is small in the middle rather than as big as one of hundreds), and returns true; or draws nothing and returns false, while the
picture isn't built yet, for a board with nothing to show, and for a rect under 16 view points
either way on screen (nothing to see, so a board zoomed out over many owners asks for none), and
the render draws something else (the subboard card, its count):

```swift
if !context.drawBoardPreview(ofBoardOwnedBy: shape.id, in: SubboardStyle.preview(in: body), maxScale: SubboardStyle.previewMaxScale) {
    drawCaption(context.shapeCount(inBoardOwnedBy: shape.id), in: body)
}
```

A [skeleton](#skeletons) may ask for one too, as the subboard's does, in the same rect and at the
same `maxScale`, so the card shows the same picture either side of 35%; the core's default skeleton
never asks.

The picture is the minimap's kind ([Silhouettes.swift](../Sources/Canvas/Rendering/Silhouettes.swift),
the core's, host API, which the minimap draws with too): every shape on the board as a silhouette of
its geometry (its outline filled, or stroked when it's open, or a container's, a frame's, so what
it holds shows on it; under 4 pixels both ways, its bounds, or a line from its first point to its
last when it's open; under a pixel, the pixel it's in: the rule, `Silhouettes.form`, that the
default [skeleton](#skeletons) goes by too), all in one muted gray, and nothing of what a shape
draws, no text and no colors, so a subboard inside is its rectangle, and a shape costs the same
whatever its kind. It's the core's
`BoardPreviews` ([BoardPreviews.swift](../Sources/Canvas/Rendering/BoardPreviews.swift), host API,
`editor.boardPreviews`):

- **Kept by board and revision.** A preview is of the board as one revision of the file had it
  (`file.revision(of:)`), a mask at most 256 pixels on a side. Asked for once the board has changed,
  by an edit or an undo (a revision never comes back), it's dropped, never drawn, and built again.
  The 64 drawn last are kept, the one drawn longest ago going first, but never one the frame before
  drew: with more owners in view than that, those past the number show their count until there's
  room, instead of each frame building one by evicting another, and asking for another frame,
  forever.
- **Sharp up close.** A preview shown larger than its mask (zoomed in, or on a 2× screen, where
  a card at 100% already is) is drawn as paths instead: every shape its outline, kept with the mask
  in cells of a grid over the board, so only the cells in view are drawn, lines 1.5 device pixels
  wide as the mask's are its pixels. Paths cost a shape each (some 1 to 2 µs), so a frame draws
  1,000 that way at most (`pathShapes`), over every preview it shows; past that, the mask, enlarged,
  as for a board of 10,000 shown whole, until zooming in leaves fewer of its shapes in view.
- **Built a chunk at a time.** A board asked for waits its turn, those asked for longest ago first.
  At the start of each frame the editor builds for 2 ms (`frameBudget`), a chunk of shapes at a time
  (the shapes' geometry, from a `ShapeContext` with no index, then their silhouettes), as many as
  fit at what shapes have cost so far, and at least one chunk (16 shapes); while any wait, it asks
  for another frame (`editor.scheduler`). One finished at the start of a frame is drawn in it. One
  whose board changed before it was built is dropped unbuilt, and so is one no shape asked for in
  the frame just drawn (`endFrame()`: its owner scrolled away, or the board was left; showing
  another board drops them all), so a frame builds only for what's in view. So ten subboards of
  10,000 shapes in view fill in over sixty to a hundred frames, each one a frame's worth
  (`./build.sh bench`).

## Frames

Frames ([`Sources/Frames`](../Sources/Frames)) is the vertical with shapes in it: the `frame` kind,
a region of its board that holds what's put down in it. Holding is the core's
([Containers](#containers)): the definition adopts `ShapeContaining`, with nothing to implement,
and the core moves what a frame holds with it, paints it above it, holds it read-only while the
frame is locked, lets go of it when the frame is deleted, and keeps what's put down from sitting
across its edge. The rest is opt-ins, as a subboard's are
([Frames.swift](../Sources/Frames/Frames.swift)):

```swift
registrar.shape(FrameDefinition()) { frame in                     // FrameDefinition: ShapeContaining, BrushHitTesting
    let place = frame.placement(size: Frame.defaultSize, minimumSize: Frame.minimumSize) { Frame() }   // what a click and draw place, never under 96 × 64
    frame.tool(label: "Frame", systemImage: "rectangle.dashed", shortcut: "f", placing: place) { _ in FrameTool(placing: place) }
    frame.tint(FrameStyle.tint)                                    // its gray, wherever it's listed by its kind
    frame.title(placeholderInPill: "Frame")                        // Titles keeps its name; untitled, a dimmed pill to grab
    frame.mentionable()                                            // Mentions: by its title; followed, it's gone to
    frame.resizable(minimumSize: place.minimumSize)                // Selection's eight handles, no smaller than it's drawn
    frame.frameRow()                                               // the table of contents, named by Titles
    frame.frameHeader()                                            // renamed in the panel's header
    frame.turnable(through: ContainerChannel.self)                 // Transform: turned into whatever takes the container channel
}
registrar.createFrameItem()                                        // Create Frame, in the context menu, around what it's for
```

- **Its props are its frame**: `Properties<Frame>(title: "Frame") { Property("frame", \.frame).required() }`.
  What it's called is the title Titles adds, and what it holds is each held shape's own
  `container`, the core's, so its props hold neither; it owns no board, so its schema is a plain
  box's. The kind is spelled as the core's own member every box has, `frame`, which the audit can't
  tell from it, so there it's an ordinary word that no module owns ([The module graph](#the-module-graph)).
- **The look** (`FrameStyle`, world units but for the border's width and reach, which are view
  points): a quiet region, a rounded rect (12) with an opaque surface a step up from the canvas,
  white on the light canvas and a 0.15 gray on the dark, in a hairline border just inside its edge
  (a view point at every zoom, black at 12%, white at 14% in the dark), and no shadow: a place on the
  canvas, not a sheet of paper. The dots stop at its edge, and what it holds sits on it. Its colors
  are dynamic `NSColor`s resolved in the render, as a subboard's are, and its outline (the
  selection's, a hover's, the hint a drag into it shows) is its rounded edge. Zoomed out it's its
  [skeleton](#skeletons) ([FrameSkeleton.swift](../Sources/Frames/FrameSkeleton.swift)): its surface
  and its border's ring over it, square, two fills, in the colors they are in full; what it holds
  draws its own skeletons over it, and its title is Titles' [cover](#a-cover-zoomed-out), over both, at its top left (there's no pill zoomed out). In the minimap and a board's
  preview it's its outline, as every container's silhouette is (`Silhouettes`, `hollow`), so what it
  holds shows there too.
- **Pressed hollow** (its `hitTest`): a frame that holds shapes is pressed and hovered only on its
  border, 6 view points either side of its edge (`FrameStyle.borderReach`, which its `hitMargin`
  declares), so a press inside it is the canvas, where a click deselects and a drag is a marquee,
  and the pointer there hovers nothing; one that holds nothing (`ShapeContext.hasContents`) is
  pressed anywhere inside too, as any box is. Its title's pill grabs it, as every pill does its
  shape ([DecorationHits](#drawn-for-a-shape-decorationhits)), and so does an untitled frame's
  dimmed "Frame", there for that (`title(placeholderInPill:)`). What finds shapes by point
  (`editor.shape(at:)`: an arrow's end) goes by the same test.
- **The marquee** selects a frame when it reaches the frame's edge, or holds it whole, never when
  it's drawn wholly inside it, where it selects what the frame holds (Selection's `BrushHitTesting`);
  with ⌘, only what it holds whole, as ever.
- **The Frame tool** (F, `FrameTool`): a drag draws one from the press to the pointer
  (`DrawingFrameSession`), shown over what it's drawn on with its surface at 30%, so what it will
  take in shows through, and put down at the release; a click places one of 640 × 400
  (`Frame.defaultSize`) centered on it, and so does a press that goes less than 12 view points from
  where it began along either axis (`FrameStyle.smallestDrawn`, a click's jitter). Drawn, it's never
  smaller than its placement's `minimumSize` (`Frame.minimumSize`, 96 × 64, which resizing, Create
  Frame and `canvas draw` read there too), grown from the press toward the pointer; ⇧ draws a
  square and ⌥ draws it about the press, as a resize keeps its proportions and its center, each as
  it's pressed or let go; the canvas scrolls at its edges; Escape puts nothing down, and the tool
  stays. Either way it's put down as a placed shape is, through the core's `editor.place` (a drawn
  one with `place(_:in:)`, the rect it drew): one step, "Add Frame"; settled, so a frame drawn in a
  frame is in it, and it takes in what it's drawn over that's mostly inside it, nudging in what
  hangs over its edge and out what's mostly outside, gliding there; selected, with the default tool
  back. Into a locked frame nothing is put down, and that frame shakes. A click inside a frame too
  small to hold 640 × 400 puts the new one over it, not in it, since it doesn't fit there, and the
  frame under it is settled as anything a frame lands on is.
- **The tool says what it places.** What makes shapes without the pointer places a kind as its
  tool's placement says (`registry.placement(for:)`: `canvas draw`, `canvas kinds`), and a tool of
  the kind's own says it too: `frame.tool(label:systemImage:shortcut:placing:_:)` registers
  `FrameTool`, made per editor by the closure, with `place` as its placement, which the tool puts
  down itself for a click. So `canvas draw` draws a frame 640 × 400 unless `size:` says otherwise.
- **Create Frame** ([CreateFrame.swift](../Sources/Frames/CreateFrame.swift)), in the context menu of
  any shapes a frame can hold (any with a box; an arrow alone has none), puts a frame down around
  them, holding them, through the core's `editor.place(_:around:padding:minimumSize:)`
  ([Containers](#containers)): 32 world units past them (`FrameStyle.padding`), and past an arrow
  between two of them, never under 96 × 64 where the frame they're all in has room, in that frame, just
  below the lowest of them in the stack. They stay where they are; what the new frame lands on beside them is settled as what a drawn frame lands on is
  (mostly inside comes in, nudged fully in; mostly outside is nudged out; gliding there). It's
  untitled and selected, one step named as the item ("Create Frame"). A locked shape among them (or
  one in a locked frame) leaves it all as it was, and shakes. An item for the canvas, as Turn into
  Subboard is, in a band of its own (`FramesMenuGroup`, 70: after Turn into's 60, before Cut, Copy
  and Paste), so Frames is on ContextMenus. tldraw's Frame Selection is the model, with three
  intended deviations: the padding is world units, as the model is, where tldraw's is 25 view points
  (zoomed out, that would reach over the neighbors); the frame goes just below the lowest of them,
  not on top of everything, so it covers nothing beside them that was above them, and shows on a big
  shape under them (a zone `canvas draw` drew); and a locked shape among them refuses the whole, as Turn
  into does, where tldraw frames the rest around it. Not built: tldraw's ⌥⌘G, Remove Frame and Fit
  to Content.
- **Opt-ins.** Titles keeps its name, shown in its pill (untitled, a dimmed "Frame"; no symbol, since
  its look says what it is), and `TitleHeader` renames it in its panel's header ("Untitled Frame").
  Mentions offers it by its title, its symbol in its gray (`NSColor.systemGray`, its row's too), and
  following a mention goes to it (`goTo`), with Mentioned In in its panel and Show What Mentions in
  its menu; untitled, the picker leaves it out. Selection resizes it, and the core settles, at the
  end of the resize, what it leaves hanging over its edge and what it grows over
  ([Containers](#containers)). Its row is its symbol and "Untitled Frame", named by Titles; the
  table of contents lists what it holds under it. Locking, which opts every kind in, locks it, and
  with it what it holds. No ports: nothing is drawn from a frame's sides. Transform's container channel
  (`frame.turnable(through: ContainerChannel.self)`, the last of its opt-ins) makes it something that can be
  turned into whatever takes the channel, a subboard in the app, from its menu ([Transform](#transform));
  Frames only offers the channel, names no kind that takes it, and brings no Turn into item or command of
  its own.

It ships after Subboards (the toolbar's Frame, F, between Subboard and Schema: the two ways of
grouping shapes, a region of the board and a board of its own, side by side), with its fixture,
`Fixtures/kinds/frame.v0.json`; `Fixtures/files/frames.v5.json` is a whole file, read and written
back as read: a frame holding a frame, which holds a note and a subboard, and a schema card (a kind no
longer shipped, kept aside, so its board's write-back moves its version into it as `v`),
beside a locked frame holding a note, and a note on the subboard's board (CompositionTests'
`FrameFile`). FramesTests hold the kind, its hollow test, its marquee, its look, its tool, Create Frame
(CreateFrameTests) and what it offers Transform (TurnTests, with CanvasTesting's pocket taking the channel) over
CanvasTesting's boxes, frozen for read-only (`FreezingPlugin`); CompositionTests' FramesShippedTests
the shipped pieces together: notes dropped in and out, a group across an edge, a locked frame
refusing a drop, a frame moved with a locked note in it, frames in frames, resizing over notes,
deleting one, pressing its inside, its pill, the tool, Create Frame around two notes and the bent
arrow between them, a locked frame's contents, the skeleton, the file, and a note mentioning one in
the app's canvas view; TransformShippedTests turn one into a
subboard ([Transform](#transform)).

## Transform

Transform ([`Sources/Transform`](../Sources/Transform)) turns a shape into another kind: a frame into a
subboard, from its context menu or as a command. It's a concern on [context menus](#context-menus) and
[slash commands](#slash-commands), and it exists because the two kinds can't meet any other way. A vertical
imports no other vertical, so Frames can't name Subboards (the audit refuses even the string `"subboard"`
in Frames) and Subboards can't name Frames. What turns into what is a graph, and its edges are
**channels**: a kind *offers* one, another kind *takes* it and says how, and a shape can turn into each
kind that takes a channel its own kind offers. The core knows none of it. It lends two generic things, the
transaction's `turn(_:into:)` and `move(_:toBoardOwnedBy:)` ([Containers](#containers), [Boards in a
file](#the-editor-and-the-file)), which a target turns with.

```
┌─────────┐  offers   ┌───────────────────┐   takes  ┌───────────┐
│  frame  │ ────────▶ │ container channel │ ◀─────── │ subboard  │
└─────────┘           └───────────────────┘          └───────────┘
 Frames imports Transform, and so does Subboards; neither imports the other
```

```swift
// In FramesPlugin.register, last of the frame's opt-ins:
frame.turnable(through: ContainerChannel.self)

// In SubboardsPlugin.register, after its shape block:
registrar.turnable(into: Subboard.self, through: ContainerChannel.self) { container, transaction in
    guard transaction.turn(container.id, into: Subboard(frame: CGRect(origin: container.frame.origin, size: Subboard.defaultSize))) else { return }
    transaction.move(container.held, toBoardOwnedBy: container.id)
}
```

### Offering and taking a channel

A channel is a type conforming to `TransformChannel`
([Transform.swift](../Sources/Transform/Transform.swift)): the `Source` a shape coming through it hands the
target, a `name` (what the registry's report calls it), `admits(_:)`, which kinds may offer it (given a
`TransformKind`: the kind, its definition, so its capabilities, and the registry; every kind by default),
and `source(of:in:)`, which reads what the shape hands over in the transaction that turns it, before the
target changes anything. A channel that has nothing to hand over for a shape returns nil: the target's turn
doesn't run, and the shape stays as it is. Conform in an extension, as with every protocol that has a
default (`admits` is the one that could be misspelled). The sugar:

| Sugar | For |
|---|---|
| `x.turnable(through: C.self)` | This kind's shapes can be turned into whatever takes the channel, inside `registrar.shape { x in ... }`. |
| `registrar.turnable(K.self, through: C.self)` | The same, for another plugin's kind. |
