| `registrar.turnable(into: P.self, through: C.self, label:) { source, transaction in ... }` | Shapes of the kinds that offer the channel can be turned into `P`'s, and the closure is how: it gets what the channel handed over and the transaction. |

- **Offering is keyed by kind and channel** (`TransformSources`): a kind offers a channel once, and two
  claims are a `conflict` ("corral offering container"). The point's `check` refuses a kind the channel
  doesn't admit (`invalid`: "bad offers the container channel on box, which can't offer it"), and a
  channel offered by every kind. Only a kind offers one, so there's no sugar for every shape.
- **Taking is keyed by the kind turned into** (`TransformTargets`): a shape turns into a kind one way, so a
  kind takes one channel, and a second claim is a `conflict` ("disc"): a second channel into one kind would
  share its menu item and its command. If one is ever needed, that's where it's decided.
- **The graph** is `registry.turnTargets(of: kind)`: each kind whose target takes a channel `kind` offers,
  in plugin order, never `kind` itself.
- **`TransformPlugin()` is the owner.** It registers the service and nothing else, and a list with a kind
  that offers a channel or takes one needs it (`ownerNotInstalled`). A target brings a menu item and a
  command, so it needs `ContextMenusPlugin()` and `SlashCommandsPlugin()` too, and a kind whose id can't be
  typed as a command's name ("odd_one") is refused (`invalid`, from the commands' point).
- **The report** shows each contribution: `offers channel container → frame` on Frames' line and `takes
  channel container → subboard · CanvasContextMenu · /turn-into-subboard → every shape` on Subboards',
  and `service TransformState` on its own ([The registry](#the-registry)).

### What a target brings

Taking a channel is the whole of a feature: the same call brings its menu item and its command, as an
opt-in does for a horizontal.

- **Turn into `label`** in the context menu: an item for the canvas, as Show What Mentions is, since what
  a shape can turn into is what the registry knows, not the shape. It's in `TransformMenuGroup`
  (order 60: after Mentions' 50, before Cut, Copy and Paste, 100), shown when every shape the menu is for
  can turn into the kind, so a menu for a frame and a note has none. The label is what the target kind's
  schema is titled (a subboard's is "Subboard"), else its id, unless the call gives one.
- **`/turn-into-<kind id>`** on the kinds that offer the channel, the target's own kind apart (it has
  nothing to turn into): a command for every shape (`slashCommandsForEveryShape`), taking no arguments.
  Typed on a line of a shape's text, it turns the shape; a frame has no text, so nothing ships that types
  it yet, though it's offered (`commands(for:)`) and runs (`run(_:on:with:)`). Where a kind that offers
  the channel does have text, it lists before `title` and `lock`: every shape's commands are offered in the
  order of the plugins that contribute them, and Subboards is before Titles and Locking.
- **One undo step**, "Turn into Subboard", named as the item is. Slash commands name their steps in title
  case for this: "Turn Into Subboard" beside the menu's item would read as a mistake
  ([Running a command](#what-a-shape-offers-and-running-a-command)).

### Turning

`TransformState` (`editor.transforms`, nil without the plugin) is the service. It keeps nothing per shape
(each kind's targets are worked out once, the registry being frozen, so `boardDidChange` is overridden with
nothing), and it's what the item and the command call:

```swift
let transforms = editor.transforms
transforms.targets(of: frame)                    // [Subboard.kind]: none for a shape off the board shown or kept aside
transforms.canTurn(frame, into: Subboard.kind)   // true: a read-only shape can too, and turning it is refused
transforms.turn([frame], into: Subboard.kind)    // true: one undo step, "Turn into Subboard"
```

- **`turn(_:into:)`** turns those of its shapes that can, each once, **innermost first** (the deepest in
  containers, then back to front), in one `editor.transact`. A frame inside another turns first and moves
  what it held onto its own board, so by the time the outer one reads what it holds, the inner one is a
  subboard in it. A frame selected with the frames inside it turns them all.
- **It keeps the container it's in, then it's put down as a placement is.** A turned shape comes out a
  different size (a subboard is 240 × 160), so it may hang over the container it's in, or reach into
  another. One that hangs over its container is shifted back inside it, `Settlement.gap` in, where it
  fits, since the in-or-out rule judges by area and would put a shape mostly outside out; then
  `transaction.settle(turned)` is that rule ([Containers](#containers)), nudging it clear of another
  container it reaches, and the editor glides it there.
- **Once one is refused, no other target runs**: the turn will be thrown away. The rest are still checked
  for read-only, so every one that is shakes.
- **All or nothing for read-only shapes.** A shape that's locked, in a locked container, or on a locked
  subboard's board, isn't turned,
  and neither is one that holds a locked shape: the target moves everything, so if anything it would move
  is read-only (`transaction.refusedShapes`), or a read-only container would take the turned shape, the
  whole turn throws out of its transaction. Nothing changes, no step is made, and the refused shapes are
  heard (`editor.refuseChanges(to:)`, so Locking shakes them). A shape that's read-only is refused before
  its target runs. A target that throws turns nothing either. `turn` returns whether it turned any.

### The container channel

`ContainerChannel` ([ContainerChannel.swift](../Sources/Transform/ContainerChannel.swift)) is the first
channel, and the only one that ships: it's offered by the kinds whose shapes hold shapes
(`ShapeContaining`: `admits` is that, so the registry refuses it on a box), and hands the target a
`TurningContainer`: the container's `id` and `frame`, and what it `held`. That's the shapes in it at any
depth (read when its turn comes, so fewer by what an inner container that turned before it took onto
its own board), and every shape whose props bind shapes (`ShapeReferencing`: an arrow) that is bound to
some of those and to nothing else. An arrow between two of its notes goes with them; one bound to anything
that stays, the container included, or to nothing, stays.

### A frame into a subboard

Frames offers the channel and Subboards takes it; each is one line, and neither knows the other. The
turn is the target's: `transaction.turn` makes the frame a subboard, and `transaction.move` puts what it
held on the subboard's board. A turn that took is followed by a move; one that didn't (the guard) leaves
a frame, which owns no board for `move` to move onto (`move` would move nothing and say false).

- **The subboard is a subboard's size at the frame's top-left corner**, `Subboard.defaultSize` (240 × 160),
  whatever size the frame was.
- **It keeps the frame's id**, and with it everything that goes by id: the arrows bound to it and what
  mentions it (a mention is live, its pill shows the subboard now, and following it enters the board),
  its place in the stack, the frame it's in, and its title, which both kinds hold (`TitleProperty`: Titles
  keeps it, and `turn` carries over the added values the new kind holds too). The values it doesn't hold
  go, and what the new kind holds that the old one didn't is a default.
- **What it held goes onto the subboard's board**, under the same ids and in the same places (world
  coordinates are kept) and in the order they were. A frame owns no board, so the subboard's is new to
  the file, or, for a frame with nothing in it, none is kept. Frames inside stay frames there, holding
  what they held, and a subboard inside takes the board it owns with it, as every board goes with its owner.
- **Bindings** are to shapes on the same board, so the turn lets go of those across the edge, as a cut
  does: an arrow bound to a note inside and a note outside keeps its end on the one outside, and the
  other end stays where it's drawn. Arrows between shapes that all move go along, bound. A name, a mention
  of a note that moved, is kept: it never cared which board the note is on.
- **Undo** puts back the frame, every shape in it and every binding, in one step.
- **What isn't built**: the reverse (a subboard into a frame), a transform in `canvas draw`, and a `/` typed
  on the canvas. A shape with text that offers the channel would get `/turn-into-subboard` for free.

### Testing transform

- **TransformTests** hold the mechanism over fixtures only, since Transform knows no shipped kind:
  CanvasTesting's corrals (they hold shapes, as a frame does) offer the container channel and turn into
  pockets (they own a board, as a subboard does), with a target written as Subboards' is
  ([Support.swift](../Tests/TransformTests/Support.swift): `corralsTurnIntoPockets()`), a `Tagline` added
  property both kinds hold, as both hold a title, and a channel of the tests' own, `BoxChannel` (only a box
  offers it, and it hands over the box's id if the box is narrow), turning boxes into discs, so that the
  mechanism is held apart from containers. They hold registration (the report's entries, the graph in plugin
  order, conflicts, a channel's `admits`, `ownerNotInstalled` and `unknownKind`, a command name that can't be
  typed), resolution (`targets(of:)`, `canTurn`), the menu (a right-click: the item in its band, choosing
  it, nested corrals selected together turning innermost first, a corral and a box showing none, one item
  for each target, a source that says no), the command (offered where it should be, one step named as the
  item is), all or nothing (a frozen box in the corral, a frozen corral, one in a frozen corral, one deep
  in nested corrals, a target never run for a read-only shape, a target that throws), the in-or-out rule
  and bindings.
- **FramesTests' and SubboardsTests' `TurnTests.swift`** hold each end of the edge over a partner of its
  own, since neither can use the other: Frames offers the channel with a pocket as the target (the title
  carried over, a frame inside still a frame holding its box, no Turn into item or command until a kind
  takes the channel, a locked box or frame refusing); Subboards takes it from corrals that offer it (the size and
  the corner, what the corral held on its board, a link inside riding and one across let go, the table
  of contents, Return entering it, `/turn-into-subboard`, an empty corral).
- **CompositionTests' `transformShippedTests`** hold the shipped pieces together, on a pasteboard of
  their own: a frame titled Groceries, holding two notes and a frame that holds a note, a note beside it
  that mentions it, and arrows bound to the notes, turned from its context menu (the item between Show
  What Mentions and Create Frame, before Cut; the subboard, its title, its board; the mention live and the pill, the row and
  the panel of a subboard; one arrow riding along and one letting go; the canvas drawn without what
  moved, and as it was after Undo), as a command, with a locked note or a locked frame leaving everything
  as it was, a frame turned with the frame inside it, a frame on a subboard's board turned there (and Undo
  from the root showing that board), the frames file's Roadmap (a frame holding a frame,
  a subboard with a board of its own and a card kept aside) turned with every board in its place, and the file
  after a turn read back through `BoardCodec`. The registry's report holds `transform`, Frames' `offers
  channel container → frame` and Subboards' `takes channel container → subboard`.

## Jump To

Jump To ([`Sources/JumpTo`](../Sources/JumpTo)) is ⌘K, and Go › Jump To…: a palette that goes to a
shape by what it's called and where it is, as VS Code's file switcher goes to a file. Name a
subboard, skip one, name another two levels down, then the shape, and the list narrows. It looks at
titles and the containment tree and never at contents (that's Find's). It's a vertical that no kind
opts into and nothing imports, as [Reordering](#every-shape-reordering) is one: a shape is listed
when its kind has a title ([Titles](#a-horizontal-plugin), named or derived), and that's all a kind
does for it. It builds on Boards (a pick is `editor.follow`, below), Titles, Topology (the tree),
Keyboard, TextEditing (its field and its list), FuzzyMatching and Geometry. It doesn't import
Mentions: a row's symbol and tint are its kind's label's (`registry.label(of:)`, the core's), the
one color a kind has in the list, the picker and Mentioned In; a kind that declares no tint is
untinted.

```
 ╭────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
 │  alpha gamma check                             │   a capsule at the top middle, below the path
 ╰────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │ ▭ Checkout          Alpha › Beta › Gamma      │   the app's caret list, under it, 560 wide,
   │ ▭ Checkout    Alpha › Beta › Gamma › Epsilon  │   10 rows shown: the kind's symbol, the title,
   └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘   the path, what matched in semibold
```

- **`JumpToPlugin`** (id `jump-to`) registers a service, `JumpToState` (`editor.jumpTo`), and
  `registrar.command(.jumpTo, shortcuts: [⌘K], isEnabled:)`: it ends editing, then opens the palette,
  or, open, asks its field for the keyboard again with its text selected; never mid-gesture. It
  changes no document, so it leaves no step of undo. The menu item is the same command, so ⌘K
  works from a note being edited and a panel's field too, where it's the menu bar's key.
- **The catalog** is every titled shape on every board the editor can show, named or derived, none
  kept aside, each with the container it's directly in (a frame, else the owner of its board), its
  title's folded keys in one buffer, as Mentions' catalog keeps its labels. It's built the first
  time the palette opens, in slices of 2 ms on the main actor (`editor.scheduler`; the first at once),
  so a commit before then costs a note of its revision; after, a commit costs what it changed (a
  move reads nothing; a rename reads the shape; shapes on other boards a commit reached, a deleted
  subboard's or a paste's, are taken out or read as well), and a file put in place, or a commit
  heard out of turn, reads it again. A commit while it's being built is applied to what's read so far,
  the shapes on boards not read yet read when their turn comes, so commits that never stop (an
  agent's draw, a sync) can't keep it from finishing. It keeps no path: a container's rename costs nothing in it.
- **Ranking.** A word names titles alone, `FuzzyMatcher.rank` over the buffer (the `@` picker's
  workload). Several words are pieces placed in order along a path, a group of neighbors to a
  name, names skipped as they like, the last in the shape's own title (`PathMatcher`): the last
  piece is matched against every title first, and only what it matches is scored by its path, a
  container's row (the best score of placing the first g pieces along the chain to it) made once per
  query for everything under it, so a shape costs one match for each group the last could be in. A
  container's name must be a name, never a scatter of its letters (a bare subsequence matches only
  the shape's own title); an untitled container is on the path by what its kind is called, dimmed,
  and is never matched. Ties go to the fewer names skipped, the shallower path, a recent pick, and
  the file's order.
- **An empty query** lists "Recent" (up to five of this window's picks) and "Nearby" (up to five
  titled shapes in view on the board shown, nearest the middle of the view).
- **The palette** is `JumpToPalette(editor:onExit:)`, which Composition's `boardChrome` places over
  the canvas: closed it's nothing; open, a scrim (a clear button, so a click lands on it, closes the
  palette and isn't the canvas's), and a capsule below the part of the canvas the host leaves clear,
  taken as it opened (so below the path over a subboard), with an `EditingTextView` in one line. Its
  list is the app's one caret list (`CaretList` in a `CaretListWindow` made with `anchorRect:`,
  [TextEditing](#a-list-at-the-caret)). ↑ ↓ ⌃P ⌃N and Page Up and Down move, Return and Tab pick,
  Escape and ⌘. close; the keyboard goes back to the canvas as the person closes it, and the palette
  closes by itself once anything else takes the keyboard (Find's field, the panel's).
- **A pick** is `editor.follow(id)` ([Boards](#a-crumbs-menu)), one step back: into a shape whose
  kind opens its board, else to it, a frame fitted into view, never forced to a readable zoom.

JumpToTests hold it over CanvasTesting's boxes, pockets and corrals, titled through Titles' property:
the catalog's laziness, slices and upkeep, the ranking over a story file ("alpha gamma checkout"),
the empty query, picks and the palette in a window; CompositionTests' JumpToShippedTests as the app
wires it. `./build.sh bench` holds a keystroke (one piece ≤ 2 ms over 10,000 shapes, several ≤ 4 ms),
the build's slices (≤ 3 ms) and what a commit costs with the plugin in the list.

## Moving

Moving ([`Sources/Moving`](../Sources/Moving)) is two slash commands that move the shape whose text
they're typed in: `/move-to @Groceries` puts a note in a frame, or onto a subboard's board, and
`/move-near @Checkout` puts it beside a shape, on the first of its four sides that's free, or, with
none free, on the side that frees up nearest. Both reach every board of the file the app can show,
not only the one shown, and the shape each takes is a pill picked with `@` on its line, where the
picker lists only what it takes (for `/move-to`, with nothing typed, every frame and subboard it
takes, on every board, nearest first). It's a vertical that no kind opts into and nothing imports, as
[Jump To](#jump-to) and [Reordering](#every-shape-reordering) are: on [slash
commands](#slash-commands) for the commands, on the [table of contents](#dragging-rows) for its
drops that move shapes (`ContentsMoves`), and on Placing for where a shape
lands, since it places a shape as [`canvas draw`](#draw) places one (the same solver, the same
obstacles, the same zones) and moves it with the core's own tools, as draw's commit does.
Placing (`Sources/Placing`) is a surface of its own, the solver moved out of Moving, so any plugin
that puts a shape down, not only Moving, places it the same way: `Surroundings(on:moving:in:)`, with
`near(_:within:)` beside a shape, `inside(_:)` in a frame and `anywhere()`, each answering a
`Landing` (the board, the box, the shapes to raise it above); Moving keeps the glue for its `Block`
and the commit.

```
┌──────────────────────────────┐
│ Ask about the beta           │   a note being edited
│ /move-near @che              │   the command, then @ and what narrows the picker
│ ┌──────────────────────┐     │
│ │ ▭ Checkout           │     │   the @ picker: only what the command takes
│ └──────────────────────┘     │   Return picks it; Return again moves the note
└──────────────────────────────┘
```

```swift
// In MovingPlugin.register: on every kind whose shapes have a box, the kinds a drag moves.
registrar.slashCommandsForEveryShape(where: { hasBox($0.definition) }) {
    SlashCommand("move-to", argument: "@frame or subboard", kinds: { $0.containingKinds.union($0.boardOwningKinds) },
                 shapes: { target, owner, editor in Destination(of: owner, into: target, in: editor) != nil },
                 step: "Move") { id, arguments, editor in
        guard let target = arguments.shapes.first else { return }
        Move(id, in: editor)?.into(target)      // asks its rule again, places, commits
    }
    SlashCommand("move-near", shapes: { target, owner, editor in admitsNear(target, for: owner, in: editor) },
                 step: "Move") { id, arguments, editor in
        guard let target = arguments.shapes.first else { return }
        Move(id, in: editor)?.near(target)
    }
}
```

- **`MovingPlugin`** (id `moving`, the module's one public type) puts both commands on every kind
  whose props are `BoxShapeProps`, read from the kind's definition, so a link, a tag or an arrow
  offers neither, and fills the table of contents' `ContentsMoves`; the report's line is
  `moving /move-to /move-near → every shape · ContentsMoves`. It's right before
  Reordering in the shipped list, after every plugin with a command for every shape, so a note's `/`
  list ends `title, lock, public, move-to, move-near`. Both steps are "Move", a drag's name ("Undo
  Move To" would read badly). A list with it needs `SlashCommandsPlugin()` and
  `TableOfContentsPlugin()`.
- **`/move-to` takes a frame or a subboard** (its `kinds`, the kinds that hold shapes or own boards,
  so the picker ranks only those, and only the titled ones, which have names) on any board the app
  can show, but not the shape itself, or what goes with it (what it holds at any depth, and what's on
  a board it, or a shape it holds, owns: the core's `move(_:to:)` traps on those); not one that's
  read-only (locked, in a locked frame, or on a board that takes no shapes: a locked subboard's, at
  any depth, `editor.isReadOnly(inFile:)`, the rule `move(_:to:)` refuses by, so a frame two boards
  under a locked subboard isn't taken though the subboard on the way isn't locked itself); not
  where the shape is already (the frame it's directly in, the subboard whose board is shown); and not
  a frame narrower or shorter than the shape. A frame is a place in it, on its board; a subboard,
  its own board, as draw's `in` takes one.
- **`/move-near` takes any shape** but the shape itself and, for a shape that holds shapes or owns a
  board, what goes with it. The picker asks this of every shape as the person types, so it costs
  next to nothing: a locked target is fine (it doesn't change), a shape on a read-only board too, and
  whether the target's board takes shapes is the move's to say (the move onto one is refused, and
  the owner of that board is heard). Each command asks its rule again as it runs: a target it no
  longer takes (gone, or locked since) moves nothing.
- **Where it lands is draw's** ([draw](#draw), step 3), worked out by Placing's `Surroundings`: the destination board read in place
  (`editor.reading(of:)`), every shape there with a solid an obstacle, filed once in DrawScript's
  `ObstacleGrid`, the shape itself left out on its own board and what it holds carried (never in its
  way), and the shape the problem's one free box, at its size, put down anew. **Near X**: four
  problems, one per side (right, below, left, above), each `<side> of X` at draw's default gap
  (`normal`, 80), centered on X the other way, the solver pushing the box out along that side's axis
  past what's in the way, with draw's clearances (40 across, 64 up and down); the side that lands
  nearest X wins, the earlier on a tie. **Into frame F**: draw's `in "F"` (`inside "F" top-left`, F
  holding it), 40 in, pushed clear of what's in F and kept within it, but held directly
  (`Holder.direct`): a frame in F is in its way like any shape there, never a zone it lands in, so it
  goes in F itself, not in a frame nested at F's top-left; with no room from that corner, from F's
  top-right, bottom-left and bottom-right in turn; with none, at F's top-left, 40 in (half its room,
  where F is barely bigger), over what's there. **Onto a subboard's board**:
  draw's one unplaced shape, at the middle of the view that board would be shown with, or the
  nearest clear spot around it, ring by ring. Zones are draw's too: a frame that holds X is a region
  the shape sits on, not a shape in its way, so a note moved beside a note in a frame lands in the
  frame, and one landing over a zone that paints above it is raised above it.
- **One step, all or nothing.** It's one `editor.transact("Move")`, with the core's tools as draw's
  commit uses them. On the board shown: `translate` (what a frame holds goes along),
  `move(_:above:)` over what it sits on that paints above it, and `settle` (the in-or-out rule: in
  the frame it's mostly over, out of the one it left, [Containers](#containers)). Onto another
  board: `move(_:to:)` first, so an arrow bound to it lets go where it was drawn, as after a cut,
  then `translate(_:by:on:)` and `settle(_:on:)` there ([Boards in a file](#the-editor-and-the-file)).
  A read-only shape in the way (a locked frame it would land in, the owner of a board that takes no
  shapes it would go onto, locked or under one that is, a locked note in a frame going onto another
  board) throws out of the transaction: nothing changes, no step is made, and the locked shapes shake
  (`editor.refuseChanges(to:)`), as a refused [turn](#turning) does. (A shape on a read-only board
  is offered no command at all, as no read-only shape is, so none moves off one.) On the board shown, what moved glides there and a note being
  edited is put down (editing ends, as a `canvas draw` that moves it ends it); onto another board,
  it's gone from the one shown, the window stays where it is, and Undo Move puts both boards back
  exactly. A move that lands where the shape is commits nothing.

- **Rows dropped in the table of contents** ([Dragging rows](#dragging-rows)) where their shapes
  aren't are Moving's too (`Drop`): the shapes move as one block (`Block`: on one board, any the app
  can show, less those another of them holds, placed by the box around them all, keeping where they
  are to each other), into a frame (its row, or among the rows it holds) as `/move-to` puts a shape
  there, if the block fits; onto a subboard's board (its row, or among its board's rows) as `/move-to`
  puts one there; out of the frames they're in (among the rows of a frame they're in at any depth, or
  of the board) beside the outermost one they leave, as `/move-near` puts a shape beside it, kept
  within the frame they go to (with no room beside it there, in that frame as `/move-to` puts one).
  From another board they move off it with the core's `move(_:from:to:)`. The same commit, then, in
  the same step, every shape dropped restacked where the drop says (`ContentsPlace.restack`); Undo
  Move takes it all back. Where the in-or-out rule leaves them out of the place (no room in a frame
  clear of the frame they leave, which takes them back), nothing changes: a drop puts them where it
  says, or nowhere. Refused as `/move-to` refuses: a locked frame, one too small, the locked owner
  of a board, what goes with them.

MovingTests hold it over CanvasTesting's boxes, corrals, pockets, links, cards and freezing, run
through `editor.slashCommands` and the table of contents' drops: what each takes, every landing, the
step and refusals; CompositionTests' `movingShippedTests` type both into a note's editor in the app
(the picker's list, a pick and the run, a subboard's board, Undo Move), and
`contentsDragShippedTests` drop notes' rows on a frame's, a subboard's and each other's.

## Neighbors

Neighbors ([`Sources/Neighbors`](../Sources/Neighbors)) shows what's connected to a shape at a glance,
which in a dense graph is the point: hover a shape, on the canvas or by its row in the [table of
contents](#the-table-of-contents), and every shape connected to it is outlined in a color that says
how, and the arrows between are colored too. The minimap fills the same shapes in the same colors,
so what's connected off screen shows there (the rest of it dims while anything is lit, and a shape
in two lights shows both, one inside the other), and a connected shape on another board (inside a
subboard) lights the card that holds it. It's a surface: what an edge's owner shows its edges on. It
builds on Queries (which finds the shapes), Selection (the hover, and the one a list sets for a shape
the canvas doesn't show), Topology (when a shape's edges change), the file (where a shape on another
board is drawn) and the core's [tinted outlines](#outlines), and it knows no kind, edge type or
concern: what counts as connected is a **light**, a color and a query, which the plugin that owns the
edges contributes to its point (`registrar.neighborLight`). Arrows' two are Connections'
(`ArrowLightsPlugin`) and mentions' two are Mentions' (`MentionLightsPlugin`), each a plugin value of
its own, so a list without Neighbors leaves them out.

| Light | Color | What's outlined, for the shape hovered |
|---|---|---|
| points to | green | the shapes an arrow out of it ends at, the shape a reference stands for, and those arrows; for an arrow, the shape it ends at |
| points to it | purple | the shapes that have an arrow into it, the references that stand for it, and those arrows; for an arrow, the shape it starts at |
| mentions | teal | the shapes its text mentions |
| mentioned by | lavender | the shapes whose text mentions it |

The colors are their owners' (`ArrowStyle.pointsToLight` and `pointedToByLight`,
`MentionStyle.mentionsLight` and `mentionedByLight`), chosen together in a design audit from renders of
the lights over both canvases: one fixed sRGB value for each appearance
(`NeighborLight.color(light:dark:)`, an `NSColor(name:)` as the
arrow's color is), never a system color (system pink read as Validation's error red, system purple as
the selection's blue, and the light-mode green and teal fell under 3:1). In the light and the dark:
green #07933B and #2FD359, purple #8C21A4 and #B851FD, teal #0E97B0 and #329AB4, lavender #A76FE2
and #D0B0FE. Each is clear of Validation's red and orange and of Find's orange, at least 3:1 against
the canvas it's drawn over in both appearances, and not the accent; the two purples are close for
some color-vision deficiencies.

```swift
// A light is a color and a query, given `#id`, the shape hovered, and the edge types come from
// their plugins' ids, never written out.

// Connections (ArrowLightsPlugin, id `arrow-lights`):
let arrow = ArrowEdge.id.rawValue, standing = StandingEdge.id.rawValue
registrar.neighborLight(color: ArrowStyle.pointsToLight) {
    ":edge-from(\($0), \(arrow)|\(standing)), :starts-at(\($0), \(arrow)), :end-of(\($0), \(arrow))"
}
registrar.neighborLight(color: ArrowStyle.pointedToByLight) {
    ":edge-to(\($0), \(arrow)|\(standing)), :ends-at(\($0), \(arrow)), :start-of(\($0), \(arrow))"
}

// Mentions (MentionLightsPlugin, id `mention-lights`):
let mention = MentionEdge.id.rawValue
registrar.neighborLight(color: MentionStyle.mentionsLight) { ":edge-from(\($0), \(mention))" }
registrar.neighborLight(color: MentionStyle.mentionedByLight) { ":edge-to(\($0), \(mention))" }
```

- **`NeighborsPlugin()`** (id `neighbors`, `PluginID.neighbors`; with `NeighborLight`, the colored
  question, and `NeighborLight.color(light:dark:)`, a color given as one sRGB value for each
  appearance; its point `NeighborLights`, filled with `registrar.neighborLight` and read as
  `registry.neighborLights`; and `NeighborState`, the service: the module's whole public surface)
  registers the service (`editor.neighbors`), which takes the lights from the registry,
  and `registrar.outlines { $0.neighbors?.outlines ?? Outlines() }`; the report's
  line is `neighbors service NeighborState · outlines`, and each face's is
  `neighbor light · neighbor light`. It's after the query plugins in the shipped
  list, and the lights' plugins are after it. It lights nothing without `QueriesPlugin()` and
  `TopologyPlugin()` (a hover asks nothing then), has nothing to hover without `SelectionPlugin()`,
  and nothing to light without a light; none of them is refused, since it
  contributes to none of their points. A light in a list without Neighbors is refused, as any
  contribution whose point's owner isn't installed is.
- **A light is a color and a question.** `registrar.neighborLight(color:query:)` contributes a
  `NeighborLight` to the `NeighborLights` point (owner `neighbors`): `query` is given the selector
  that names the shape hovered (`#`, then its id, as the query language writes one) and returns the
  query whose matches are outlined in that color. Lights are in plugin order, and a plugin's in the
  order it gives them: a shape's first light is its first ring, so the shipped list has arrows' before
  mentions'. They are the query language's
  ([Queries](#queries)): `:edge-from(X, arrow|stands-for)` is the shapes X has an arrow to, or
  stands for; `:starts-at(X, arrow)` the arrows (connections) that start at X; `:end-of(X, arrow)`
  the shape X ends at, where X is an arrow (and nothing for any other shape), so hovering an arrow
  lights its two ends; the `|` joins edge types, and a type takes in those under it (`arrow` is every
  channel's too). Another
  way to be connected, a new kind of edge, is another light from the plugin that owns the edge, with
  nothing in this module, or in the shipped list's code, changing.
- **The subject** is the shape hovered: `editor.hovered` (the select tool's, or any plugin's where it
  shows shapes), else the shape whose row the pointer is on when the canvas doesn't show it
  (`editor.hoveredElsewhere`, [Selection](#selection): a row of a board nested under its owner's in
  [the table of contents](#the-table-of-contents) sets it). Both are watched with Observation,
  re-armed after each change, and the look at a change is a turn of `editor.scheduler` later, never
  inside the `willSet` Observation tells it in.
- **Asking.** When the subject changes to a shape, any ask still running is let go of (the engine
  looks every 256 shapes, so it stops), and one batch asks the engine
  (`editor.queries.matches`, [Many at once](#many-at-once-edge-views-and-waiting)) for every light in
  the view `.resolved` and, where some shape stands in for others, `.literal` too, ids only, up to
  `QueryBudget.maxRows`: one capture, run alongside whatever else is asking the engine, and each text
  checked once. Each light keeps the union of its views. The answer lands a frame or so later, and
  only for the shape asked about (every change of the subject lets go of the ask); a request the
  engine refuses (a shape gone since) lights nothing, and the others still do. From one shape to the
  next, the lights of the first stay until the second's land; when the subject goes, they go at
  once. Without the engine, or Topology, or any light, nothing is asked and nothing is lit.
- **Asking again.** `topology.follow` tells it when a change to the edges touches the subject or a
  shape the last answer matched (a commit's, so an arrow drawn from the hovered shape lights as it's
  drawn, an undo, a file read afresh; or a provide's, a dynamic reference's answer arriving), and it
  asks again, which lets go of an ask under way. A change lists the ends of the edges it changed,
  never the arrow that carries one, so an arrow hovered is asked about again by where it was matched:
  the end it's re-aimed away from, or the pill a provide re-points at its end. A commit asks again
  too when it names the subject other than by moving it (an arrow bound at an end it had none at,
  the undo of a re-aim: the commit changed the arrow's record, and no end of its edge was matched
  before) or adds a shape the answer didn't match: a mention outlives the shape it names, so one of a
  shape deleted before the hover left its edge as it was, and the shape back changes no edge, but is
  what the answer left out (the lights are queries; a new shape may be what one finds). A commit
  whose change to the edges asked already asks no more. A commit that changes the edges of shapes
  the answer didn't match, or only moves shapes, asks nothing. Another board shown clears it: the
  hover is let go of with the switch.
- **Both views.** A reference is a [stand-in](#stand-ins-forwarding): an arrow into its pill is, in
  the resolved view, an arrow into the shape it stands for, and in the literal view one into the
  pill. Asking each light in both means the pill's own arrows count and so does what it stands for.
  Hovering a note with an arrow into a pill lights the shape (as the graph reads it), the pill (as
  drawn), and the arrow; hovering the shape lights the pill (it stands for it), what has an arrow into
  the pill, and the arrows; hovering the pill lights what it stands for, and, as drawn, what has an
  arrow into it. In a file where nothing stands in the two views are the same edges, and only the
  resolved view is asked.
- **What shows**, worked out when an answer lands and again by a commit that names a shape matched
  or one a match is drawn as (other than by moving it), reaches another board or replaces the
  document, never per frame; any other commit, a drag's every event or a keystroke in an unrelated
  note, costs a look at its change set and a few set intersections. A match on the board shown is
  outlined itself. A match on another board is outlined as the shape on the board shown that holds
  it (`file.shape(on:holding:)`: a subboard's card, the pocket it's in, however many boards down),
  once however many of its shapes match, with one walk up the boards for each board the matches are
  on; one on a board above, which no shape on the board shown holds, is left out. The subject is never
  lit, nor, where the subject isn't on the board shown (a row of another board), the card it's on:
  Selection outlines that card faintly, as a hover is, since that is where the subject is.
- **Rings.** A shape in two lights has a ring for each, in light order: the first light it's in is
  its first ring, the next light's the next, `TintedOutlines.ring`. A group is made for each light and
  ring that has shapes (an arrow is in one light; a note that's both pointed to and pointing back is
  in two, green first, then purple a ring further out), and the core, which knows no meaning, strokes
  them as the outline says ([Outlines](#outlines)): under every other outline, so a selected shape's
  line shows over the tint. A ring is 4 view points further out than the one before (a line 2 wide
  and a gap 2), so their centers are 4, 8 and 12 off a note's edge, whole pixels at 1× and 2×.
  The rest of how it looks is the core's too, for any group: a shape that's selected too has its
  tint one ring further out, clear of the selection's line, which would cover most of ring 0; a lit
  arrow is covered in its color, as wide as its line and a point more, not striped; the hovered
  shape's faint outline is stronger (85%) while anything is lit, so it reads above the lights; and
  Validation's ring stands outside the rings. Nothing is outlined while a session runs, a drag, and what was lit shows
  again when it ends. What's kept is one `Outlines` the core is handed as it is, and the canvas is asked
  for a frame only when a new one differs from the old: an answer that lights nothing, after one that
  lit nothing, draws nothing.
- **What it costs.** A hover is one batch: the main actor reads and resolves its four queries (eight
  where a shape stands in; some 0.02 ms each) and takes up the file in one turn, O(1); the answer is
  off the main actor (some 10 ms for a shape with 10,000 neighbors); the landing joins the views,
  keeps the set of what matched and places each match, O(what's lit and the boards it's on), a hash
  lookup or two each (some 0.8 ms for 10,000). It keeps nothing a commit must follow but what it
  matched and where that is drawn. A frame costs handing the core what's kept; the core strokes only
  what's in view, and looks at the rest's kept extents (10,000 lit in view at 10% add some 7 ms to
  a frame, as ⌘A's rings do; all out of view, some 0.35 ms), and the minimap fills them (some 4 ms
  for 10,000). `./build.sh bench` holds them.
- **Testing.** NeighborsTests use fixtures only (CanvasTesting's boxes, links as wires, memos as
  what quotes, pockets and corrals, a `Pill` that stands for what it cites and a `Lens` for what's
  provided, and four lights of the tests' own in pure colors, given by a plugin of the tests' own,
  `lightsPlugin`, over a `Star` and a `Nest`); they read
  `editor.outlines.tinted` after `settle()` (a turn of the scheduler, then the run loop until
  `isAsking` says the answer landed): each light's matches in its color, one view asked where nothing
  stands in and two where a shape does, an arrow hovered lighting where it ends and starts, a shape in
  two and three lights in rings, the subject never, a pocket's card for what's on its board and two
  boards down, nothing from a board above, a shape hovered elsewhere (its card faint, never lit), the
  canvas's hover over it, the answer before staying until the next lands, a changed hover letting go
  of the ask (the engine takes up the file once), a switch clearing it, nothing during a session, and
  nothing without the engine; and what keeps it right: asking again when the subject's edges change
  or an edge of what's lit does (a commit, an undo, a provide), when an arrow hovered is re-aimed,
  let go of and bound again or has its end deleted, when a pill is re-pointed at its end, and when a
  shape no answer matched comes (a deleted mention's shape back); not for others' edges or a move;
  working out what shows again, asking nothing, only for a commit that names what's lit or reaches
  another board (a lit shape moved down a board and back, deleted and undone), never for an unrelated
  edit, a restack or a drag; and the canvas drawing again only when what's outlined changed.
  CompositionTests' NeighborsShippedTests hold the four shipped lights as the registry has them
  (arrows' from Connections, then mentions' from Mentions; none in a list without the three plugins,
  and a list with a light and no Neighbors refused; each face's two queries, and its refusal without
  Neighbors, are held in its owner's tests too, ArrowPortsTests' and MentionsTests' `LightTests`),
  the shipped table of
  contents' rows, a reference and a subboard, an arrow re-aimed while hovered, the colors (each
  appearance's value, 3:1 against its canvas), a lit arrow covered, and the rings drawn at 4 and 8
  points in the app's own editor. BenchmarkTests' NeighborBenchmarks hold a hover on a shape
  with 10,000 neighbors and with ten, and the frames and the minimap with them lit.

## References

References ([`Sources/References`](../Sources/References)) is the vertical that makes [stand-ins](#stand-ins-forwarding)
something a person can place: the `reference` kind, a pill that stands for another shape anywhere in the
file, so that a shape too many others point at needs no arrow from each. An arrow drawn into the pill is,
for everything that reads the graph (queries, the table of contents, Topology's readers), an arrow into
the shape it stands for; as drawn, it's still into the pill. Only a [public](#publishing) shape can be
stood for. A reference stands for one picked shape (**direct**) or for what a query finds
(**dynamic**): the first match in file order, or with All every one. Words typed that already read as a
query are that query; others are turned into one by the model, live while they're typed
(Natural language, below).
Its registration ([References.swift](../Sources/References/References.swift)):

```swift
registrar.service { ReferenceState(editor: $0) }          // which references name which shape; what each stands for now
registrar.overlay(ReferenceButtonOverlay())               // the leading symbol's hover and pressed looks
registrar.canvasButtons(at: { editor, point in … }, click: { button, editor in … })   // the leading symbol goes to the original
registrar.command(.goToOriginal, isEnabled: { … }) { … }  // the panel's button, the menu's item
registrar.command(.interpretReference, isEnabled: { … }) { … }   // the panel's Interpret
registrar.detailStatusForEveryShape { shape, context in … }   // a warning line where an attached arrow's channel isn't taken
registrar.contextMenuForCanvas { … }                      // Go to Original (direct), Show Matches (dynamic)
registrar.shape(ReferenceDefinition()) { reference in     // ReferenceDefinition: NeverPublic, Editable, CustomSkeleton, DerivedProps
    let place = reference.editingPlacement(size: Reference.defaultSize) { Reference() }
    reference.tool(label: "Reference", systemImage: "arrow.turn.up.right", shortcut: "r", placing: place)
    reference.portsOnEveryChannel(sides: [.left, .right])  // what it takes is what it stands for ([Ports at a stand-in](#ports-at-a-stand-in))
    reference.standsIn(maxTargets: 50, admitting: { target, registry in registry.isPublic(target) },
                       needs: "public",                // a message says "only a public shape can be stood for"
                       makes: { props, target, label in ReferenceEdits.pick(&props, ReferenceTarget(id: target, label: label)) }) { shape, _ in
        if let target = shape.props.target { return .shapes([target.id]) }
        if let query = shape.props.query { return .provided(ReferenceState.key(query: query, all: shape.props.all)) }
        return nil
    }
    reference.standInRow { shape, _ in … }                 // its row in the shape's Referenced In
    reference.referenceRow()                               // the table of contents
    reference.referencePanel()                             // its header; Go to Original, or the Query and Matches sections
    reference.contextMenu { … }                            // Match All, Match First: a step each
    reference.validate(ignoringMoves: true) { shape, context in … }   // a query the engine can't read: a warning in its words
}
```

- **The props** (`Reference`): `frame` (32 tall, the width stored and fitted), `target: ReferenceTarget?`
  (`{id, label}`, a [name](#values-that-name-shapes), not a binding: it crosses boards, outlives its shape,
  is kept by cut and paste and by a copy that doesn't take the shape along, and renamed by one that does),
  `words`, `query: String?` (format `x-canvas-query`, so `canvas draw` refuses one the engine can't read)
  and `all`. `target` and `words` are `readOnly()`, so a script can't write them, and the kind has no
  title, so `canvas kinds` lists it with no edges. The mode is derived, never stored: a target makes it
  direct, words or a query make it dynamic, else it's empty. `ReferenceEdits` writes it: each of `pick`,
  `find(words:query:)` and `clear` keeps one mode and refits the width to what the pill now says. The
  v0 fixture, `Fixtures/kinds/reference.v0.json`, pins every member.
- **Made by name.** `makes` is how `canvas draw` makes a direct reference (`registry.standIns.make`): the
  pill's own writer, `ReferenceEdits.pick`, with the shape's id and the name its title folds to, so it's
  fitted to its label as a picked one is. An edge to a public shape on another board puts one beside the
  shape on this board ([draw](#draw)); a script still can't write `target` or `words`, nor name the pill.
- **What it stands for** (`ReferenceState.state(of:)`, a `ReferenceCondition`, derived from the props and
  the file, never stored; the render works it out through its own context, and the service keeps a
  direct pill's from frame to frame until a commit changes it or what it names): live (the shape is there,
  public and mentionable), not public (there, but not public: nothing is forwarded), missing (in no
  board: the name it holds), not available (in the file on a board the app can't show), and, for words,
  not interpreted, interpreting (the model is being asked), failed, or nothing to interpret them with; for a query, being found, found (`ReferenceFound`: all or first, the count, the
  matches given, the first's appearance), no matches, refused (in the engine's words), failed (past
  the deadline: Retry), or nothing to ask (no engine installed). The state also keeps which references
  name which shape across the whole file (from every commit's `ChangeSet`, reading only the references
  the commit touched: a shape's kind never changes), so a rename, a change of publicness or a deletion
  remakes the right rows, and a commit of thousands of shapes and no reference costs a set hit each.
- **What a dynamic reference finds** (`ReferenceAnswers.swift`). `ReferenceState` keeps every reference
  with a query in the file (from `ChangeSet`, other boards and boards added and removed included; read
  afresh for a file put in place) and asks the engine for them: one `queries.matches` batch, on one
  snapshot, for every one whose answer may be out of date and that isn't being typed into, each on the
  **recorded** view (what direct references forward, never another dynamic one's answer), admitting
  public shapes alone (`editor.publishing.admitting`), eight matches for a first-match one (what All
  would add, for its panel) and fifty for an All one. When: its own question changed (its query or flag,
  a gesture or an undo), at once, on the scheduler's next turn; any other commit but a move, after
  250 ms of quiet (`ReferenceStyle.settle`, each commit waiting again, on `editor.scheduler`); a commit
  that only moved shapes, never (one test). A plan that reads the person (`editorWords`) isn't asked:
  it's refused, “`:selected` can’t be used here.” An answer lands only for the question the record
  asks now and only if no older than the latest that landed for it (kept per key), and goes to Topology
  in one `provide` (the first match, or up to fifty), then, if it says something new (every quiet asks
  every reference again, and most answers are what they were), the pills (`setNeedsDisplay`), panels
  (observed per reference) and rows (`contentsDidChange(for:)`) are told. A title or id no shape has,
  or a container that can't hold shapes, is no matches, saying why; the deadline is a failure that
  Retry asks again. The last four answers of each reference are kept by key, so an undo, a redo or an
  All toggled back shows its answer at once (provided from a hop of the scheduler, exempt from the
  stale rule, then asked again). They are kept past the reference's deletion (for its undo), but for
  at most 256 references (`ReferenceStyle.memosKept`): the least recently landed or used gives way, so a
  long session's deleted references don't pile up. It's one of Topology's settle sources (busy while a wait is armed, a
  hop is due or a batch is out), so `canvas query` right after a draw waits for it, and "Finding…"
  shows only once a batch has been out 250 ms.
- **The pill** (`ReferenceStyle`): a capsule 32 tall, a leading symbol (the kind's, tinted, or a
  magnifier for every dynamic one, or a dashed square for what's gone), the label (14 medium, one line;
  a dynamic one's words, never its matches' names), and what trails (the eye of a shape gone private;
  the first match's kind symbol in its tint, an All one's count in a capsule, "50+" past fifty, a "0"
  for none or a refusal, the warning for a failure); filled and bordered, or, when it stands for
  nothing, a dashed border with no fill and the label in italic at two thirds; while it's looked for,
  solid with its words at half. Its width keeps room for what may trail it (a dynamic one's count, a
  direct one's eye or warning), so nothing that comes and goes refits it or cuts a short name short.
  Zoomed out it's one square fill. Labels and symbols are memoized, symbols as bitmaps, so a frame of a
  thousand pills builds none.
- **Typing** (`ReferenceEditor`): the Reference tool places an empty pill and edits it, in a step named
  "Add Reference" (an existing pill's is "Edit Reference", `Editable.editingStepName`): one line over the
  pill, in an `NSView` framed in view points with its bounds in world units, as an arrow's label editor is,
  its text where the render's label is (so nothing moves when editing starts) and the render drawing no
  label meanwhile. Each change is written as words with the width refitted (64 to 280, growing rightward,
  room kept for a count whenever it's words); Return, ⌘Return and a click away end it, ⇧Return does
  nothing, pasted newlines are spaces and the text is at most 200 characters. Under the field, a list of
  the public shapes (`ReferencePicker`, a headless model on TextEditing's `CaretList`, in a
  `CaretListWindow` like every caret list: `PublicShapes: MentionScope`, so the candidates are the `@`
  picker's, ranked as it ranks them, with the recent picks and the shapes nearby for nothing typed) with
  the words as typed always the last row, set off by a line (`CaretListItem.separated`); the first shape is
  highlighted, but the one a pill already stands for while the text is as the field opened. Return or Tab
  on a shape's row, or a click on it, picks it (`ReferenceEdits.pick`: it stands for the shape, the words and
  query let go of, the width fit to its name) and ends editing; Return on the words row, or ⌥Return on
  any, commits the words (words that read as a query, `queries.check`'s, are that query, canonical, in
  the same step: no model asked; a query the model wrote for exactly these words while they rested is
  written in the same step too; for others the model is asked, below); Escape closes the list and a second leaves the field,
  where changed text is kept as the pill's words (nothing is picked implicitly), and typing opens the list
  again. Once only the words row is left (the hand-off to natural language) the pill leads with the
  magnifier while it's edited. A new pill left empty is discarded inside its step
  (`Editable.discardsWhenEditingEnds`), and unchanged text makes no step. A scope that admits few shapes
  ranks only its members (`MentionState` keeps each scope's members as entries are read), so a keystroke
  costs what matches, not the board.
- **Natural language** (`ReferenceInterpreting.swift`, design 7.3, decision D9): live, once only the
  words row is left (`ReferencePicker.isHandoff`) and the text has rested `ReferenceStyle.interpretDelay`
  (600 ms on `editor.scheduler`, every keystroke starting the wait again and cancelling a call that is out),
  `editor.queryTranslator.translate(words, about: .reference)` is asked, so the query is one a reference
  can run (reads only the file, titles right, repaired once). Its answer is the reference's **draft**
  in `ReferenceState`, never in the document: the panel shows the words, the query, its status and its
  matches as they arrive (one extra `matches` request, which provides nothing, so nothing is forwarded);
  text that already reads as a query is a draft at once, with no model. At commit (Return on the words
  row, ⌥Return, or leaving with text) a draft that has landed for exactly these words is written in the
  editing step itself, no second call; a call still out when editing ends is not cancelled by it: it
  lands later as an undo step of its own, "Interpret" (`editor.transact(on: board, "Interpret")` in a
  task continuation, never inside undo), only if the reference is still there with the same words and no
  query and isn't read-only (a locked one is let be: no step, no shake, not interpreted, and Interpret
  is offered once it's unlocked); words committed before they rested are asked about when editing ends.
  Nothing asks on undo, redo, paste, `canvas draw` or open; undoing "Interpret" leaves the words,
  not interpreted, with Interpret offered in the panel (a borderless `DetailCommandButton("Interpret",
  systemImage: "sparkles")` in the status line's place, dimmed while it's locked). Editing the pill again,
  a keystroke, deleting it, undoing past its words, or the file closing cancels the call (`ReferenceState`
  goes with its editor and cancels what it has out, the model's call, the draft's request, the batch and every
  timer, as an `isolated deinit`; the editor goes while a call is out because `QueryTranslator` holds it only
  weakly across the call). A failure
  is said quietly (the pill dashed with a warning, "Interpreting" solid with its words dimmed): "No API key"
  or "Key rejected" with "Open Settings…" (`AnthropicSettingsView.showSettings()`, as a type's sync's),
  "Rate limited", "Can’t reach Anthropic", "Timed out" or any other of the model's own with "Retry", "No
  query for these words" (declined or unanswerable) with "Retry", "Unusable answer" (a repair that still
  refused); a key saved in Settings (`languageModelKeyDidChange`) asks again what failed for want of one.
- **Ports.** A reference has ports on every channel on its left and right, but what a person drags
  from and what ends on it is what it stands for ([Ports at a stand-in](#ports-at-a-stand-in)): a drag
  from a note ends on a pill that stands for a note and not on one that stands for a frame, and
  an arrow re-aimed onto one obeys the same rule. A pill that stands for a subboard has a subboard's
  dots and links: indigo, and a `subboard-link` to a subboard. A pill that stands for nothing has no
  dots and takes nothing. Arrows keep their bindings when it is re-pointed; if an arrow attached to it is on a
  channel the new targets don't take, a warning triangle trails the pill (where a dynamic one's count
  will be) and the panel says `“Order” doesn’t take note links.` (`ReferenceState.channelMismatch(of:)`,
  kept for each reference until its edges change, never worked out per frame).
- **Going to the original**: the leading symbol is a [canvas button](#canvas-buttons) (hovered, an accent
  arrow; a click goes as following a mention does, one step back, the pill not selected first), and the
  same command is the context menu's first item and the panel's plain "Go to Original" button, which work
  on a locked reference too. A dynamic one's symbol goes to what it stands for, and its menu has Show
  Matches (them, selected) and Match All or Match First.
- **The panel of a dynamic reference**: the header's line says how many it found ("First of 7", "12
  matches", "50 of 73", "No matches"; nothing while it's looked for). The Query section has the query,
  read-only and colored as code, one line per line, scrolling sideways (`DetailCodeEditor`), a status
  line only when there's something to say ("Interpreting…", "Finding…", a refusal, "Too slow" or a failed
  interpretation with its action, "Unavailable"), the Interpret button for words nobody has asked about, and `LabeledContent("Match") { DetailCheckbox("All", …) }`, a step of its own. The
  Matches section, while it found shapes, is a `DetailShapeRow` per match (the board's name where it
  isn't the board shown; in first mode the rows after the first dimmed, what All would add) and "and
  42 more" past eight; a click goes to one, the pointer hovers it on the canvas.
- **Validation**: a query the engine can't read (pasted, or written into a board by hand) is a warning
  in the engine's words, on `query`; what it finds or doesn't is the pill's to show, never an issue.
- **The table of contents**: its row is what it stands for (a dimmed placeholder where it stands for
  nothing), remade when the shape it names changes; an arrow that starts at a reference nests under the
  shape the reference stands for when that's on the same board ([Connections' arrow row](#the-table-of-contents),
  generic over stand-ins), else under the reference.
- **Tests.** ReferencesTests hold it over CanvasTesting's boxes and tiles as what it stands for (its `makes` too, through `registry.standIns`: a reference made for a public shape, fitted, standing for it once inserted, and for nothing where the shape isn't public); CompositionTests'
  `referencesShippedTests` the shipped pieces (an arrow drawn by hand into a pill, in the graph and a query, nesting, a drag
  ending on a pill for a note and not on one for a frame, copy, cut and paste, `canvas draw`, a drawn query read through by a
  query that waits for it); `ReferenceBenchmarks` a frame of a thousand pills, a keystroke in the list
  over a board of ten thousand shapes of which twenty are public, and twenty dynamic references answered after a commit.

## The command line

`canvas` is the app's command line, for agents first and people too: it runs commands on the
boards open in the app, which must be running, and each change shows in the board's window as it's
made. Agents never read or write a board's file; they go through `canvas`, so the file stays the
app's to change.

```
canvas status                           whether the app is running: its version, protocol and boards
canvas boards                           the open boards: each one's id, name, file, which is in front, and what it shows
canvas new <file>                       a new board's file, made and opened
canvas draw <script>|- [--dry-run] [--reveal] [--board <board>]
                                        shapes, and the edges between them, made, changed or deleted by a script, all at once
canvas kinds [<kind>] [--schema]        what a script can draw, and with what
canvas measure <script>|-               how big a script's shapes would be, and what the placement is done with, drawing nothing
canvas query <query>|- [--limit <number>] [--count] [--brief] [--fields <attribute>]… [--board <board>]
                                        the shapes of a file a query matches, on every board, in file order
canvas query --ask <question>|- […]     the same, the query written by the app's language model
canvas query-vocabulary                 what this app's queries can name: kinds and their attributes, edge types, words
canvas help [<command>]                 what a command takes (--format json: what the app says, schemas too)
```

The modules, one job each:

| Module | Layer | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| CanvasRPC | wire | What the app and `canvas` say to each other: JSON-RPC 2.0, a message a line, over a Unix-domain socket (`~/Library/Application Support/InfiniteCanvas/canvas.sock`, or `CANVAS_SOCKET`) only this user can reach; what a command is (`CommandSpec`, its params a JSON Schema) and how its params are spelled as arguments; the client, and the listener, which answers each request as a main-actor task of its own (one that waits holds up neither the main actor nor another connection), each connection's answers in the order its requests came, and cancels the requests still running (not notifications) once its client hangs up. Knows no canvas, plugin or AppKit. |
| CanvasCLI | cli | `canvas`: reads its own options, asks the app what it runs (`describe`), reads the rest as one of those commands, runs it, and prints what comes back. Knows only the wire. |
| CanvasUI's `CommandServer` | ui | The app's end: it listens, describes the app, and answers each request on the main actor. `status`, `boards` and `new` (a new board's file, saved as Save As saves one, `BoardDocument.newFile(at:)`, then opened) are its own; it runs the rest on the board a request names (`--board`: an id, a file or a name), or the one in front, on the board inside that file its window shows, each in a task kept against its board, and a board command's result, when it's an object, gains `board: {id, name, shows, showsPath}`, as `boards` lists it, read in the command's own job just before it runs, so an agent sees which board it worked on (a command that knows better says `shows` and `showsPath` in a `board` object of its own, which the server completes: a query's is the board shown as it took up the file). A client gone is answered `cancelled`, and a board closed (`BoardDocument.close()`) answers its running commands `board_closed`, at once, their tasks cancelled and what they return later dropped. |
| Automation | language | The commands plugins give the command line (`AutomationCommands`), its own three, `draw`, `kinds` and `measure`, and the four points `draw` takes what it doesn't own from (on the query engine, Queries, a surface, to check a query a property holds). The app hands the commands to its server through Composition (`ShippedPlugins.commands(in:)`, async). |
| DrawScript | foundation | The language `draw` reads (`Script(parsing:)`), the solver that places what it says (`LayoutProblem.solve()`), and the grid its obstacles are filed in (`ObstacleGrid`: boxes only, which any plugin may use to place a shape among others): pure, it knows no canvas, registry, kind or plugin. |
| FuzzyMatching | foundation | What's typed matched against text ([FuzzyMatching](#fuzzymatching)): `FuzzyMatcher` (every list's tiers), `TextSearch` (Find's, over folded texts) and `PathMatcher` (Jump To's, over containment paths): pure, it knows no canvas, registry or plugin. |
| JumpTo | vertical | Jump To (⌘K, [Jump To](#jump-to)): a palette that goes to a shape by its title and where it is, over Titles' titles and the containment tree; no kind opts into it, and nothing imports it. |
| Moving | vertical | `/move-to` and `/move-near` ([Moving](#moving)): the shape typed in moved into a frame, onto a subboard's board or beside a shape, on any board, placed with Placing's solver (DrawScript's, over `ObstacleGrid`) as `draw` places a shape; no kind opts into it, and nothing imports it. |
| Neighbors | surface | Hover a shape and what it's connected to is outlined by how ([Neighbors](#neighbors)): its lights are colors and the queries that find their shapes, each contributed by the plugin that owns the edges (Connections' `ArrowLightsPlugin`, Mentions' `MentionLightsPlugin`), asked of Queries, placed on the board shown by the file's boards (`shape(on:holding:)`), hovered on the canvas or in the table of contents (Selection's `hovered` and `hoveredElsewhere`). |
| DrawLexicon | lexicon | What `draw` takes from Titles (names), Connections (edges), Validation (warnings), Mentions (mention text) and Types (a type named by its title): a plugin value for each concern (`TitleNamesPlugin`, `PortEdgesPlugin`, `ValidationChecksPlugin`, `MentionTextsPlugin`, `TypeNamesPlugin`), joining Automation to the plugin that owns it. |
| QueryCommands | language | `query` and `query-vocabulary`, and `--ask` as a call to QueryTranslation's translator, its errors said as the wire's (on Automation, Queries, QueryTranslation and the wire; it declares no point). |
| QueryLanguage | foundation | The language `query` reads (`SelectorList(parsing:)`) and its canonical form: pure, it knows no canvas, registry or plugin. |
| Placing | surface | Where a box of shapes lands on a board, beside a shape, in a frame or anywhere, placed as `draw` places one ([Moving](#moving)): `Surroundings`, `Landing`; Moving's solver, for any plugin that puts shapes down. |
| Queries | surface | The engine that answers a query about a file ([Queries](#queries)), and its points: a surface, so any plugin may run a query. |
| QueryTranslation | surface | English into a query: `AskStyle`, `AskRequest`, `AskAnswer`, and the translator (`editor.queryTranslator`, `QueryTranslationPlugin(prompt:referenceRule:style:)`) that `--ask` and the app both ask, `ask` (run what it wrote) and `translate` (only check it, for a query stored to be run later); it declares no point (on Canvas, LanguageModels, Queries and QueryLanguage). |
| QueryLexicon | lexicon | What queries take from Titles (names), Boards (boards' names), Mentions (`:mentions`, `:mentioned-by`, mention text as it reads), Validation (`:invalid`, `:warned`) and Selection (`:selected`): a plugin value for each concern (`TitleQueriesPlugin`, `BoardQueriesPlugin`, `MentionQueriesPlugin`, `ValidationQueriesPlugin`, `SelectionQueriesPlugin`), joining Queries to the plugin that owns it. |

**The commands are the app's, so `canvas` never changes for one.** It knows no command but `help`:
each run asks the app to describe itself, and makes its commands, their arguments and their help
from what comes back. A plugin that adds a command adds it to `canvas`, help and all, and the two
can't disagree about what a command takes. The app carries the `canvas` it was built with
(`Contents/Helpers/canvas`; `build/canvas` links to it), and `canvas` refuses an app that speaks
another version of the protocol (`RPC.protocolVersion`: 2, in which text may be read from standard
input, and an error may say where in a script it is).

**A command is a name, its params, and what it does**, registered with Automation, as `draw` is
([Commands.swift](../Sources/Automation/Commands.swift), [Draw.swift](../Sources/Automation/Draw.swift)):

```swift
struct DrawParams: SchemaDefined {
    static let properties = Properties<DrawParams>(title: "draw") {
        Property("script", \.script).required().keywords(["x-stdin": true, "x-value-name": "script"])
            .description("What to draw: one statement a line (a shape, an edge, a delete or a style), in quotes for the shell.")
        Property("dryRun", \.dryRun).description("Work everything out and say what would happen, changing nothing.")
        Property("reveal", \.reveal).description("Then ease the view to what was drawn.")
    }
    var script = ""
    var dryRun = false
    var reveal = false
}

registrar.automationCommand("draw", "Draw shapes on a board, and connect them, from a script.", discussion: "…",
                            params: DrawParams.self, positionals: ["script"],
                            examples: [CommandExample(#"canvas draw 'edge "API" -> "DB"'"#, "Connect the two.")]) { params, context throws(AutomationError) in
    try draw(params, in: context)       // context.board(): the board --board names, or the one in front
}
```

- **Params are a list of properties** ([Properties](#properties)), whose JSON Schema is what
  `canvas` reads the arguments by: a string as it's typed, a number or an integer read as one, a
  boolean a flag (`--dry-run`, `--no-dry-run`), a fixed number of numbers (the core's point and
  size) as `x,y`, an array of any of those by giving the option again, and anything else as JSON
  (`-` reads it from standard input). Text whose schema says `"x-stdin": true`, as `draw`'s script
  does, is read from standard input when it's given as `-`, and help writes it `<script>|-`: a
  script quoted for the shell breaks at its first apostrophe. Each property is an option (`dryRun`
  is `--dry-run`), those in `positionals` also take their places in order, and help shows each
  one's `description`, its default, and what `x-value-name` calls its value. A param whose schema
  says `"x-timeout": N` (`Property(…).keywords(["x-timeout": 60])`, `--ask`'s) makes `canvas` wait
  up to N seconds for the answer when it's given (`CommandArgument.waits`): a call waits
  `--timeout`, else the longest such wait among the params given, else 10 s, and help says "(waits
  up to N s)". Text whose schema says `"x-path": true` (`new`'s file) is a file named from where
  `canvas` runs, which it sends whole (`CommandArgument.isPath`), since the app runs elsewhere. The app checks what comes against the schema and decodes it, so `run` gets its
  params typed.
- **A board command** (the default scope) runs on a board: `context.board()` is its editor. An app
  command (`scope: .app`, as `kinds` is) runs with the registry. `board` is the server's param, and
  `canvas`'s own options (`socket`, `format`, `timeout`, `help`, `version`) are `canvas`'s, so the
  registry refuses a command that declares one; a name the command line can't type (words of
  lowercase letters, digits and hyphens: `draw`, `board list`) or one that's kept
  (`RPC.reservedCommandNames`: the protocol's `describe`, the server's `status`, `boards` and `new`,
  `canvas`'s `help`); a positional that isn't a param; and two commands of one name.
- **An error says why, and what to do**: `AutomationError(message, reason:, hint:)`, where `reason`
  is a word an agent can branch on (`unknown_kind`) and `hint` is often the command, or the line,
  to write instead; a name that's nearly one gets a "did you mean". An error about a script or a
  query says where: `line:` (from 1), `column:` (from 1, in characters) and `length:` (in
  characters) of what's wrong on it, and `statement:` (that line as written: `draw`'s trimmed, its
  comment left out; a query's whole, so the column counts from its start); and a command that finds
  several problems at once throws the first, with every one in `errors:`. Anything else an agent
  can use goes in `details:` (`--ask`'s `transient`, the `query` a model wrote), under names of the
  command's own: a detail named like one of the error's members (`reason`, `message`, `hint`,
  `line`, `column`, `length`, `statement`, `errors`) is left out, whether the error has that member
  or not. They reach `canvas` as the error's data (`line`, `column`, `length`, `statement`, the
  details beside them, and `errors`, each `{line, column, length, statement, reason, message,
  hint}` and its details), which it prints beside its own members in JSON, never over them, and as
  text as `canvas: line 3, column 12: <message>`, the statement indented, carets under the columns
  it names, as a terminal draws them (a tab before them stays a tab, and an emoji or a CJK character
  takes two cells: `Invocation.caret(under:column:length:)`), the hint, then
  a line for each further problem. `canvas` prints a result on standard output (JSON when that isn't a terminal,
  which is how agents run it, or text, whose tables lead with `line`, `did`, `id`, `name`, `kind`
  and `title`, those a table has, end with sentences
  (a warning's `message`), which they never cut, and list what a row has that isn't a value (a
  kind's attributes) under it; `--format` says which), an error on standard error, and exits 0
  when it's done, 1 when the app couldn't do it, 2 when the command line is wrong (standard input
  that can't be read, or isn't UTF-8, included), and 3 when the app couldn't be reached or didn't
  answer in time. The app doesn't drop a request it's slow to answer: after a timeout
  (`timed_out`) it may still do it, so check before running it again.
- **A command changes a board as anything does**: through `editor.transact`, on the main actor, so
  the window shows each change, the board is edited and saves itself, read-only shapes refuse, and
  services hear the change set; its commit is an undo step of its own, named as the command names
  its transaction (`transact("Draw")`). Who made a change is recorded only as whether an agent did:
  a command that changes the board for one says so (`transaction.byAgent = true`, as `draw` does),
  and its commit carries it (`ChangeSet.byAgent`), so a service that acts on a person's edits
  leaves it be (a type's sync, which would ask a language model, takes what an agent wrote
  as in step). An agent's name on its commits is still to come.

**A file's boards.** A file can hold boards inside its shapes ([Boards in a file](#boards-in-a-file));
a command works on the one its window shows, `editor.board`, as the window does: `document`,
`transact` and the undo step its change makes are that board's (a `draw` is one step, Draw, there,
and undoing it from another board shows that one first). `canvas boards` says which, for each open
file: `shows`, the board shown (`"root"`, or the id of the shape that owns it, as a `BoardID` is
written), `showsPath`, the boards from the root down to it, `shapes`, how many it holds, and
`fileShapes`, how many the file holds, on every board;
`canvas status` names the front file's as `frontmostShows`; and a board command's result names it
in its `board` (`id`, `name`, `shows`, `showsPath`, as `boards` has them), read in the
command's own job as it starts: a command that doesn't wait (`draw`) runs in that job, so no
switch of board comes between the two. A [query](#query) says where it ran itself, the board shown
as it took up the file (`QueryResult.shown` and `shownPath`, `:current-board`'s), which may be
later than its request (it waits for answers to settle, and `--ask` waits on the model), and the server
completes that `board` with the file's `id` and `name`. A query reads every board of the file the
app can show, whichever the window shows, and names each row's board (`board`, and `inside`, the path's names for the boards it's
inside). A `draw` never names a board either: it works out the one it draws on from what its
script names (Automation's `Drawing.board(for:in:)`: a title names a shape on any board of the file
the app can show, the board shown's first; a new shape goes on the board of what it's placed
against, or the one `in "X"` names, the board X holds, or, for X a [container](#containers) on its
board (a frame), the board X is on; with neither, the board shown), reads that
board through the core's `editor.reading(of:)` (a `BoardReading`: its shapes, a `ShapeContext`
and paint order over them, and the view it would be shown with, a first visit's fit included), and
commits there with `transact(on:)`, the window staying where it is; a script that lands on two
boards is `several_boards`, since a run is one transaction and one undo step, made on one board,
but for an edge between shapes on two, which goes through a [stand-in](#stand-ins-forwarding) for
the end that a kind can be made to stand for ([Edges through a stand-in](#draw)): such an end
claims its board only softly, so the run draws on the first hard claim, else on the board of the
first such edge's start; one already drawn through a stand-in claims the board the stand-in is on,
hard, and a shape the script draws, which is on the board the run draws on, claims none. One that
would put a shape or an edge on a board that can't change (a locked subboard's, and every board
under it) is `read_only`. Its result's `on` says which (`board`, that shape's `title`, `shown`).
`canvas show "<title>"` (or
`--root`) moves the window, through `editor.showBoard`, and says where it is in a `board` of its
own, which the server completes.

The app that holds the socket's lock (`canvas.sock.lock`, beside it) is the one listening: a second
copy of the app gives up and runs without the command line, and a socket that one that crashed left
behind is taken over. A command's options may also come before its name
(`canvas --board 2 draw - < plan.txt`), as agents often write them.

### A command may be async

A command that waits on something (a language model's answer, a query answered off the main actor)
answers later: `runAsync:` in place of `run:`, its output `Encodable & Sendable`
([Automation.swift](../Sources/Automation/Automation.swift)), as [`query`](#query) does
([QueryCommands.swift](../Sources/QueryCommands/QueryCommands.swift)):

```swift
registrar.automationCommand("query", "Find the shapes of a file that a query matches, …", discussion: "…",
                            params: QueryParams.self, positionals: ["query"], examples: […],
                            runAsync: { (params: QueryParams, context: AutomationContext) async throws(AutomationError) -> JSON in
                                try await query(params, in: context, asking: asking)   // its answer built as JSON, off the main actor
                            })
```

- **It runs on the main actor, awaiting**, and the main actor is free while it waits: the listener
  answers each request as a task of its own, and `CommandServer` runs each command in a task kept
  against its board, so a command that waits holds up neither drawing nor another connection's
  commands. On one connection only the answers keep their order: a `draw` sent after a query may run
  before the query's answer comes.
- **Its output is written as JSON off the main actor** (`AutomationCommand.encoded`, `@concurrent`,
  handed the output whole, `consume`), where it's freed too, so a large one costs the main actor
  neither its writing nor its freeing. One that's the wire's `JSON` already passes through as it is
  (`JSON(_: JSONValue)` makes one; `query` builds its answer member by member, off the main actor).
